questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes Article 226 from Article 32?
o: Article 226 also covers legal rights beyond Fundamental Rights
Article 226 can be used only against state governments
Article 32 petitions are heard only by High Courts
questions.e: High Courts under Article 226 may issue writs for Fundamental Rights and 'for any other purpose', i.e. ordinary legal rights — wider subject-matter scope than Article 32, which is confined to Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The writ of Certiorari is issued to:
o: Produce a detained person before the court
Command a public authority to perform its duty
Quash the order of a lower court or tribunal
Question a person's claim to public office
questions.e: Certiorari quashes an order already passed by a lower court/tribunal acting beyond jurisdiction. Prohibition stops proceedings in advance; Habeas Corpus produces the detainee; Mandamus commands performance of duty; Quo Warranto questions authority to hold office.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: Which Fundamental Right is available to citizens and non-citizens alike?
o: Article 16 — equality of opportunity in public employment
Article 21 — protection of life and personal liberty
questions.e: Articles 15, 16 and 19 are citizen-only. Article 21 ('no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty') uses 'person', so it protects everyone, including non-citizens.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted which Fundamental Right?
o: Right to free and compulsory education for ages 6–14 (Article 21A)
questions.e: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A (free and compulsory education, 6–14 years), substituted Article 45, and added a Fundamental Duty (51A(k)) for parents. The RTE Act, 2009 gave it statutory shape.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: Untouchability is abolished and its practice punishable under:
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Article 15 bars discrimination on listed grounds; Article 23 bars trafficking and forced labour.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: The Directive Principles are 'fundamental in the governance of the country' yet not enforceable by courts because of:
questions.e: Article 37 expressly bars courts from enforcing the Directive Principles, while declaring them fundamental in governance and a duty of the State to apply in law-making.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: The Fundamental Duties were inserted into the Constitution by the:
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment added Part IVA (Article 51A) on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation. The 44th Amendment is the one that rolled back Emergency-era changes.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Which Directive Principle was given institutional shape by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: Article 39 — equal pay for equal work
questions.e: Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats; the 73rd Amendment (1992) constitutionalised them as the third tier of government.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: The eleventh Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(k), added by the 86th Amendment, requires:
o: The State to provide free legal aid
Parents or guardians to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6–14
Citizens to protect monuments of national importance
questions.e: 51A(k) makes it a parent's/guardian's duty to ensure education for children between 6 and 14 — the duty-side companion of the Article 21A right to education.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Article 50 of the Directive Principles directs the State to:
o: Take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive
questions.e: Article 50 mandates separation of the judiciary from the executive in public services — the constitutional root of judicial independence. UCC is Article 44; panchayats Article 40; environment Article 48A.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha, and the number of members nominated by the President, are:
questions.e: Article 80 caps the Rajya Sabha at 250 — 238 elected plus 12 nominated for eminence in fields like art, science and literature. The present strength is 245.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: After a money bill is passed by the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha must return it within:
questions.e: Article 109 gives the Rajya Sabha 14 days to return a money bill with recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. Silence for 14 days means deemed passage.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: A no-confidence motion can be moved:
questions.e: No-confidence targets the Council of Ministers' collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha (Article 75), so it lies only there, and needs 50 members' support for admission.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The 104th Constitutional Amendment (2020) is associated with:
o: End of Anglo-Indian reservation in legislatures
questions.e: The 104th Amendment discontinued the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, while extending SC/ST reservation to 2030.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: A joint sitting of Parliament under Article 108 is presided over by the:
questions.e: Article 118(4): the Speaker presides over a joint sitting; in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker. It resolves deadlocks on ordinary bills by simple majority.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 covers:
o: Appeals in criminal cases from High Courts
Disputes between the Centre and States, or between States
Advisory opinions sought by the President
Transfer of cases between High Courts
questions.e: Article 131 gives the SC exclusive original jurisdiction over Centre–State and inter-State disputes — no other court can hear them at first instance. Advisory jurisdiction is Article 143.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The basic structure doctrine was propounded in:
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
questions.e: Kesavananda Bharati (1973), decided by a 13-judge bench, held Parliament may amend the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure. Minerva Mills (1980) later confirmed judicial review is part of it.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The collegium system for judicial appointments was created by the:
questions.e: The Second Judges case (1993) gave primacy to the CJI-led collegium. The 99th Amendment tried to replace it with the NJAC, which the Court struck down in 2015.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: The President seeks the Supreme Court's advisory opinion under:
questions.e: Article 143 lets the President refer questions of law or fact of public importance to the SC. Article 136 is special leave to appeal; 141 makes SC law binding.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · Very high weightage
questions.q: Which statement about High Courts' writ jurisdiction is correct?
o: It is narrower than the Supreme Court's Article 32 power
It covers Fundamental Rights and other legal rights under Article 226
It cannot be used against private bodies
questions.e: Article 226 lets High Courts issue writs for Fundamental Rights and 'for any other purpose' — i.e., ordinary legal rights — making it wider in scope than Article 32.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Residuary legislative powers — subjects not enumerated in any list — vest in:
o: Both Parliament and state legislatures concurrently
questions.e: Article 248 assigns residuary subjects (cyber law, space) to Parliament — a key unitary tilt, unlike the US where residuary powers rest with the states.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Parliament may legislate on a State List subject in the national interest when:
o: The Lok Sabha passes a simple-majority resolution
The Rajya Sabha passes a two-thirds resolution under Article 249
questions.e: Article 249: a Rajya Sabha resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting lets Parliament legislate on a State subject for one year (renewable).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted under:
questions.e: Article 280 mandates a Finance Commission every five years (or earlier). The 15th Commission recommended 41% vertical devolution to states for 2021–26.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: The GST Council is established under:
questions.e: Article 279A (101st Amendment) creates the GST Council — Union FM as chair, state FMs as members, decisions by three-fourths majority.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Which commission on Centre–State relations submitted its report in 1988?
questions.e: The Sarkaria Commission (1983–88) is the landmark review of Centre–State relations. Punchhi reported in 2010; Rajamannar was a Tamil Nadu state committee (1971).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment came into force on:
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment took effect on 24 April 1993 (observed as Panchayati Raj Day). The 74th followed on 1 June 1993.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment, contains:
questions.e: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects (agriculture, health, drinking water, etc.) for devolution to panchayats. The Twelfth Schedule has 18 urban functions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Reservation of seats for women in panchayats and municipalities is mandated at:
questions.e: Articles 243D and 243T mandate one-third reservation for women (including SC/ST women). Many states have since raised it to 50%.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: PESA, 1996, is significant because it:
o: Extended panchayat provisions to Scheduled Areas with tribal safeguards
Merged rural and urban local bodies
questions.e: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 adapts Part IX for Fifth Schedule areas, giving Gram Sabhas powers over land alienation, forests and minor minerals.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The committee that first recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj system was the:
questions.e: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the Zila Parishad–Panchayat Samiti–Gram Panchayat structure; Ashok Mehta (1977) later suggested a two-tier model.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: The Preamble was amended:
questions.e: Only the 42nd Amendment touched the Preamble, adding 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'. The Court has held the Preamble is part of the Constitution and hence amendable within basic-structure limits.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Which case first held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution?
questions.e: Berubari (1960) said the Preamble was not part of the Constitution; Kesavananda (1973) overruled that view. S.R. Bommai (1994) later held secularism a basic feature.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, citizenship CANNOT be acquired by:
questions.e: The Act lists five modes — birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory. Mere long residence, without meeting a statutory mode, confers nothing.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: Which of the following is a citizen-only Fundamental Right?
o: Article 21 — protection of life and personal liberty
questions.e: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 are reserved for citizens; Articles 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25–28 use 'person' and cover everyone.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS II · High weightage
questions.q: The basic structure doctrine implies that:
o: Parliament cannot amend the Constitution at all
Parliament can amend any part but cannot destroy the Constitution's essential features
Only the Supreme Court can amend the Constitution
Fundamental Rights can never be amended
questions.e: Kesavananda (1973): the amending power is wide but not unlimited — the Constitution's basic structure (supremacy, rule of law, judicial review, secularism, federalism, etc.) is inviolable.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The excavator of Harappa in 1921 was:
questions.e: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa (1921); R.D. Banerji dug Mohenjo-daro (1922); John Marshall, as Director-General of the ASI, announced the discovery in 1924; S.R. Rao excavated Lothal.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Great Bath is located at:
questions.e: The watertight Great Bath (about 12 × 7 m) is at Mohenjo-daro's citadel — likely used for ritual bathing. Harappa is known for granaries, Dholavira for water management, Kalibangan for the ploughed field.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Which Harappan site is associated with a dockyard?
questions.e: Lothal (Gujarat), excavated by S.R. Rao, has the famous dockyard and bead factory — evidence of maritime trade with the Persian Gulf and Mesopotamia.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Harappan script is best described as:
o: Deciphered and read as early Sanskrit
questions.e: The script is undeciphered — inscriptions are short (mostly on seals), with no bilingual text to crack them. Brahmi belongs to a much later period (Ashokan edicts).

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Which is the largest Harappan site excavated in India?
questions.e: Rakhigarhi (Hisar, Haryana) is the largest Harappan site in India. Dholavira is notable for water management, Lothal for the dockyard, Kalibangan for the ploughed field.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Arthashastra is attributed to:
questions.e: Kautilya, Chandragupta's minister, authored the Arthashastra on statecraft. Megasthenes wrote the Indica; Vishakhadatta wrote the play Mudrarakshasa (about Chandragupta's rise).

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Kalinga war, after which Ashoka embraced Dhamma, was fought in:
questions.e: The Kalinga war (261 BCE, Ashoka's 8th regnal year) caused the remorse recorded in Major Rock Edict XIII — the turning point of his reign.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: Ashokan edicts were first deciphered by:
questions.e: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837, unlocking the edicts. The Maski minor rock edict is the one that names the author as 'Ashoka' (most edicts call him Devanampiya Piyadasi).

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Third Buddhist Council was held during Ashoka's reign at:
questions.e: The Third Council (~250 BCE) met at Pataliputra under Moggaliputta Tissa's presidency, with Ashoka's patronage. First: Rajgir; Second: Vaishali; Fourth: Kashmir/Kundalvana (Kanishka).

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The last Mauryan ruler, assassinated by Pushyamitra Shunga, was:
questions.e: Brihadratha (c. 185 BCE) was killed by his commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Shunga, who founded the Shunga dynasty.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · High weightage
questions.q: In the mansabdari system, 'zat' and 'sawar' denoted respectively:
o: Personal rank/status and the cavalry to be maintained
questions.e: Zat fixed the mansabdar's personal status and salary; sawar fixed the horsemen he maintained. Both were expressed as numbers (e.g., 5000 zat / 5000 sawar).

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · High weightage
questions.q: The zabt/dahsala land revenue system is associated with:
o: Akbar, implemented by Raja Todar Mal
questions.e: Todar Mal's dahsala (1580) averaged ten years' produce and prices to fix assessments — building on Sher Shah's earlier zabt experiments, but systematised under Akbar.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · High weightage
questions.q: The Ain-i-Akbari was authored by:
questions.e: Abul Fazl's Ain-i-Akbari (third volume of the Akbarnama) is the great gazetteer of Akbar's empire — administration, revenues, army, and court life.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · High weightage
questions.q: The Din-i-Ilahi was propounded by Akbar in:
questions.e: Din-i-Ilahi (1582) was Akbar's syncretic order blending elements of Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism and others — joined by a handful of courtiers, never a popular movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · High weightage
questions.q: Which Mughal officer was in charge of military pay and recruitment?
questions.e: The Mir Bakshi headed military administration — pay, recruitment and the dagh/chehra checks. Mir Saman managed the imperial household; Sadr-us-Sudur handled religious grants.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was presided over by:
questions.e: W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session at Bombay (Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College), attended by 72 delegates. A.O. Hume was the founder-organiser, not the president.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Surat split of 1907 divided the Congress into:
questions.e: At Surat (president: Ras Behari Ghosh), Moderates and Extremists (Lal-Bal-Pal) split over the pace and methods of the swadeshi movement, reuniting only at Lucknow in 1916.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced by the:
questions.e: The 1909 reforms conceded separate electorates — Muslims voting only for Muslim candidates — a demand first pressed after the 1906 Simla deputation. The 1919 reforms extended the principle.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Lucknow Pact (1916) is notable for:
o: A joint Congress–Muslim League platform of demands
The launch of the Khilafat movement
questions.e: At Lucknow, the Congress and League presented common demands (brokered by Tilak and Jinnah), and the two Congress wings reunited — the high-water mark of Hindu-Muslim political unity.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on:
questions.e: On 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day), General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful gathering at Amritsar, protesting the Rowlatt Act. The Hunter Committee inquired; the episode radicalised a generation.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement after:
o: The arrest of the Ali brothers
questions.e: After a mob killed 22 policemen at Chauri Chaura (UP), Gandhi called off the movement via the Bardoli resolution (12 Feb 1922), arguing the masses were not ready for non-violence — a decision that split the Congress.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Dandi March (1930) began on:
questions.e: Gandhi set out from Sabarmati on 12 March 1930 with 78 followers, reaching Dandi on 6 April to break the salt law — the opening of Civil Disobedience. 26 January 1930 was the Purna Swaraj pledge day.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Poona Pact (1932) was an agreement between:
questions.e: After Gandhi's fast against the Communal Award's separate electorates for Depressed Classes, the Poona Pact (24 Sep 1932) substituted reserved seats within joint electorates.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The 'Do or Die' call was given during the:
questions.e: 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) was Gandhi's mantra at the Bombay AICC session on 8 August 1942 launching Quit India — the only movement demanding immediate British withdrawal.

questions.subject: History
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Mains GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947 proposed:
o: Partition of India with transfer of power in August 1947
A federal India with strong provinces
questions.e: The 3 June Plan accepted partition: two dominions (India and Pakistan), with power transferred on 15 August 1947; the Radcliffe Award drew the boundary lines.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: K2 (8,611 m), the highest peak in territory claimed by India, lies in the:
questions.e: K2 is in the Karakoram (Baltistan, PoK). Kanchenjunga (8,586 m, Sikkim) is the highest peak wholly within India; Everest (8,848.86 m) is on the Nepal–Tibet border.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The correct west-to-east order of the Northern Plains' sub-belts is:
questions.e: From the foothills outward: Bhabar (porous, streams disappear) → Terai (marshy re-emergence) → Bhangar (older alluvium) → Khadar (newer, floodplain alluvium).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Anamudi (2,695 m), the highest peak of peninsular India, is in the:
questions.e: Anamudi is in the Anaimalai Hills (Kerala), part of the Western Ghats. Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the Nilgiris' highest; the Cardamom Hills lie further south.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: India's only active volcano is at:
questions.e: Barren Island (Andaman Sea) is India's only active volcano. Narcondam is dormant; Saddle Peak (737 m) is the highest point of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Lakshadweep Islands are of:
questions.e: Lakshadweep's 36 islands are coral atolls. The Andaman–Nicobar chain, by contrast, is the emerged tip of a volcanic island arc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: The south-west monsoon normally strikes the Kerala coast around:
questions.e: Normal onset over Kerala is ~1 June (the 'burst' of the monsoon), reaching Mumbai around 10 June and covering India by mid-July.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: About what share of India's annual rainfall comes from the south-west monsoon?
questions.e: The June–September SW monsoon delivers roughly three-fourths of annual rainfall — which is why a weak monsoon hits agriculture, GDP and food inflation together.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: Mawsynram receives the world's heaviest rainfall mainly because:
o: It lies in the path of western disturbances
The Bay of Bengal branch is forced to rise over the Khasi hills (orographic lift)
questions.e: Moist Bay-branch winds hit the Khasi hills and are forced upward, cooling and condensing — classic orographic rainfall. The funnel-shaped Meghalaya plateau amplifies it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: El Niño is generally associated with the Indian monsoon as:
questions.e: El Niño (eastern Pacific warming) typically suppresses the monsoon via altered Walker circulation; La Niña usually strengthens it. The Indian Ocean Dipole can offset or reinforce the effect.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.module: Prelims GS I · Very high weightage
questions.q: Tamil Nadu's main rainy season (October–December) is caused by the:
questions.e: As the monsoon retreats, NE winds pick up Bay of Bengal moisture and strike the Coromandel coast — Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain in Oct–Dec, opposite to the rest of India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the longest river flowing through India?
questions.e: The Ganga (2,525 km) has the longest course within India. The Indus (~3,180 km) and Brahmaputra (~2,900 km) are longer overall but mostly flow outside India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 'Panchnad' — the five tributaries of the Indus — are:
questions.e: 'Panj-nad' (five rivers): Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej merge and join the Indus in Pakistan. The second set feeds the Ganga; the third, the Brahmaputra.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) was brokered by the:
questions.e: The World Bank brokered the 1960 treaty: eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan, with restricted Indian usage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Inter-state river water disputes are adjudicated under:
questions.e: Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide for adjudication of inter-state waters — exercised via the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 and its tribunals.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea forming estuaries because they:
o: Flow through rift valleys and carry relatively less silt
questions.e: Both occupy tectonic rift valleys with hard-rock channels, so they deposit little silt and meet the sea as estuaries — unlike the delta-building east-flowing rivers.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.topic: National Income & Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: National Income is defined as:
questions.e: National Income = NNP at factor cost = GNP minus depreciation, measured at factor cost (i.e., net of indirect taxes). Per capita income is this figure divided by population.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.topic: National Income & Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: The difference between GDP at market prices and GDP at factor cost is:
questions.e: GDP(fc) = GDP(mp) − net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies). Depreciation separates gross from net; NFIA separates domestic from national.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.topic: National Income & Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP in that it is measured:
o: At factor cost instead of market prices
questions.e: Real GDP values output at base-year prices (2011–12 series), isolating volume growth from price rises. The GDP deflator (nominal/real × 100) measures the price change.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.topic: National Income & Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Which sector contributes the largest share to India's Gross Value Added?
questions.e: Services contribute over half of GVA — even though agriculture still employs the largest share of workers, a classic structural feature of the Indian economy.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.topic: National Income & Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: India's national income estimates currently use the base year:
questions.e: The 2011–12 base-year series (introduced 2015, CSO, now NSO) is current. Base years are revised periodically to update the consumption and production basket.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · Very high weightage
questions.q: India's inflation target under the monetary policy framework is:
questions.e: The government notifies a 4% CPI (Combined) target with a 2–6% tolerance band, reviewed every five years; the MPC must explain itself if inflation breaches the band for three quarters.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · Very high weightage
questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee consists of:
questions.e: The MPC (set up 2016) has six members — Governor (chair, casting vote), Deputy Governor, one RBI officer, and three government nominees; decisions need at least four votes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · Very high weightage
questions.q: If the RBI raises the repo rate, the expected sequence is:
o: Cheaper credit → higher demand → higher inflation
Costlier credit → lower demand → lower inflation
questions.e: A higher repo raises banks' funding costs, lifting lending rates; costlier credit shrinks money supply and demand, cooling inflation — the standard transmission chain.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · Very high weightage
questions.q: CRR differs from SLR in that:
o: CRR is kept with the RBI as cash; SLR is kept by banks as liquid assets
CRR applies only to foreign banks
SLR earns no interest while CRR does
CRR is decided by banks themselves
questions.e: Cash Reserve Ratio: a share of net demand and time liabilities parked as cash with the RBI (no interest). Statutory Liquidity Ratio: a share banks hold themselves in cash, gold or approved securities.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · Very high weightage
questions.q: Stagflation refers to:
o: Stagnant growth combined with high inflation
questions.e: Stagflation — stagnation + inflation — is painful because the usual remedies conflict: raising rates to fight inflation worsens the slowdown.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.q: The Annual Financial Statement is presented to Parliament under:
questions.e: Article 112 requires the President to lay the Annual Financial Statement (the Budget) before Parliament each year. Article 110 defines money bills; 265 bars taxation without law.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.q: Fiscal deficit is defined as:
o: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
questions.e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts), i.e., the government's total borrowing requirement. Revenue deficit covers only the revenue account; subtracting interest gives the primary deficit.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.q: The FRBM Act, which sets fiscal discipline targets for the Union government, was enacted in:
questions.e: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (2003, effective 2004) mandates deficit reduction paths; the N.K. Singh committee (2017) reviewed it and suggested debt-to-GDP targets.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.q: GST was launched in India on:
questions.e: GST went live on 1 July 2017 via the 101st Amendment (2016), replacing excise, service tax, VAT and others with a destination-based CGST+SGST/IGST structure.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.module: Prelims GS III · Mains GS III · High weightage
questions.q: The separate Railway Budget was merged into the Union Budget from:
questions.e: On the Bibek Debroy committee's recommendation, the 92-year-old separate Railway Budget (a legacy of the 1924 Acworth Committee) was merged from 2017–18, and the Budget date moved to 1 February.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Harappan Civilisation:
1. The Great Bath has been discovered at Mohenjo-daro.
2. Harappan seals were generally made of steatite.
3. The dockyard has been excavated at Lothal.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Mohenjo-daro's Great Bath, steatite seals with unicorn motifs, and Lothal's dockyard are all established Harappan features.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Harappan sites with the modern states/countries where they are located:
A. Dholavira — 1. Haryana
B. Rakhigarhi — 2. Gujarat
C. Mohenjo-daro — 3. Pakistan
D. Kalibangan — 4. Rajasthan
questions.e: Dholavira (Gujarat), Rakhigarhi (Haryana, largest Harappan site), Mohenjo-daro (Sindh, Pakistan), Kalibangan (Rajasthan, ploughed field evidence).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Harappan town planning is/are correct?
1. The citadel was built on a raised platform in the western part.
2. Streets followed a grid pattern intersecting at right angles.
3. Burnt bricks were used in construction.
questions.e: Harappan cities show a raised western citadel, grid-pattern streets, and standardised burnt bricks — the hallmarks of its urban planning.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The earliest evidence of the ploughed field in the Indian subcontinent comes from:
questions.e: Kalibangan (Rajasthan) yielded a ploughed field with criss-cross furrow marks, indicating two-crop cultivation.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
With reference to the Rig Vedic period, consider the following statements:
1. The staple crop was barley (yava).
2. The cow was the chief medium of exchange.
3. Iron was widely used in agriculture.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Rig Vedic economy centred on barley and cattle as wealth/medium of exchange; iron (krishna ayas) appears only in the Later Vedic period.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Battle of Ten Kings' (Dasarajna) described in the Rig Veda was fought on the banks of the river:
questions.e: The Dasarajna, won by Sudas of the Bharatas, was fought on the Parushni (Ravi) — described in Mandala 7 of the Rig Veda.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Vedic texts with their associated content:
A. Rig Veda — 1. Musical chants
B. Sama Veda — 2. Hymns of praise
C. Atharva Veda — 3. Spells and charms
D. Yajur Veda — 4. Sacrificial formulae
questions.e: Rig Veda (praise hymns), Sama Veda (melodies), Atharva Veda (magic/medicine), Yajur Veda (ritual formulae).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which Upanishad contains the dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama on the nature of the soul?
questions.e: The Katha Upanishad presents Nachiketa's three boons and Yama's teaching on atman and immortality.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mahavira and Jainism:
1. Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara.
2. He attained kevalajnana at the age of 42 under a sal tree.
3. Jainism recognises the existence of gods but denies a creator God.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Mahavira (24th Tirthankara) attained kevalin at 42 under a sal tree at Jrimbhikagrama; Jainism accepts gods as souls but rejects a creator God. All three are correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The first Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha under the patronage of:
questions.e: The First Council (c. 483 BCE) at Sattapanni cave, Rajagriha, was patronised by Ajatashatru; Mahakassapa presided, Upali recited Vinaya and Ananda the Sutta.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Buddhist Councils with their venues:
A. First — 1. Pataliputra
B. Second — 2. Rajagriha
C. Third — 3. Vaishali
D. Fourth — 4. Kundalvana (Kashmir)
questions.e: First (Rajagriha), Second (Vaishali, split into Sthavira/Mahasanghika), Third (Pataliputra, Ashoka), Fourth (Kundalvana, Kanishka — Sarvastivada).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Tripitaka consists of the Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka and Abhidhamma Pitaka. Which of them deals with monastic discipline?
questions.e: Vinaya Pitaka lays down monastic rules; Sutta contains discourses; Abhidhamma is philosophical analysis.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Ashoka's Dhamma, as expounded in his edicts, primarily emphasised:
o: Moral and ethical conduct — tolerance, non-violence, respect for elders
State Buddhism and persecution of other sects
questions.e: Ashoka's Dhamma was a moral code (tolerance among sects, ahimsa, respect for parents/teachers) — not sectarian Buddhism; he never persecuted other faiths.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following Ashokan edicts is written in Greek and Aramaic?
questions.e: The Shar-i-Kuna (Kandahar) edict is bilingual Greek-Aramaic; Girnar is in Prakrit (Brahmi); Maski first named 'Ashoka'; Rummindei records the Lumbini visit.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mauryan administration:
1. The empire was divided into provinces headed by kumara (princes).
2. The Arthashastra of Kautilya is the principal source on Mauryan polity.
3. Ashoka maintained a standing army of about 600,000 infantry according to Megasthenes.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Mauryan provinces were governed by kumaras; Kautilya's Arthashastra is the key administrative text; Megasthenes (via later writers) credits Chandragupta with a 600,000-strong infantry.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Saptanga' theory of the state in the Arthashastra lists seven limbs. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.e: Saptanga: swami, amatya, janapada, durga (fort), kosha (treasury), danda (army), mitra (ally). Sangha is not among them.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which Mauryan ruler is credited with the construction of the Sanchi Stupa's original brick core?
questions.e: Ashoka built the original brick stupa at Sanchi (3rd century BCE); the stone casing, gateways and railings are Shunga–Satavahana additions.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela is located at:
questions.e: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription (Udayagiri-Khandagiri, Odisha) records his reign and mentions the Nanda king's canal — a key Jain/Chedi source.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Indo-Greek king Menander is known in Buddhist literature as:
questions.e: Menander (c. 165–130 BCE) appears as Milinda in the Milindapanha, his dialogue with Nagasena; he issued bilingual coins.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Satavahanas:
1. They issued coins mostly of lead.
2. Gautamiputra Satakarni is called 'the destroyer of Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas' in the Nasik inscription.
3. Their capital was Pratishthana (Paithan).
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Satavahanas issued lead (and potin) coins, Gautamiputra's Nasik prashasti by his mother Gautami Balashri makes the destroyer claim, and Pratishthana was their capital.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Gandhara school of art flourished under the patronage of:
questions.e: Gandhara (Greco-Buddhist) art peaked under Kanishka and the Kushanas (1st–3rd century CE); Mathura school developed alongside under the same patronage.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which Kushana ruler convened the Fourth Buddhist Council and started the Shaka era?
questions.e: Kanishka (78 CE — start of the Shaka era) convened the Fourth Council at Kundalvana, Kashmir, where Sarvastivadin doctrine was codified.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Allahabad Pillar inscription (Prayag Prashasti) eulogising Samudragupta was composed by:
questions.e: Harishena, Samudragupta's court poet, composed the Prayag Prashasti; Ravikirti composed Pulakeshin II's Aihole inscription.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gupta period:
1. It is often called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India.
2. The decimal system and the concept of zero developed during this period.
3. Fa-Hien visited India during Chandragupta II's reign.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Gupta age: classical Sanskrit literature, Aryabhata's astronomy/mathematics (zero, decimals), and Fa-Hien's visit (c. 405–411 CE) during Chandragupta II Vikramaditya.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Nalanda Mahavihara was founded during the reign of:
questions.e: Kumaragupta I (Mahendraditya, early 5th century) founded Nalanda; it was later patronised by Harsha and the Palas.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Gupta-era scholars with their works:
A. Aryabhata — 1. Panchasiddhantika
B. Varahamihira — 2. Aryabhatiya
C. Kalidasa — 3. Abhijnanashakuntalam
D. Vishakhadatta — 4. Mudrarakshasa
questions.e: Aryabhata (Aryabhatiya), Varahamihira (Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita), Kalidasa (Shakuntalam), Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The iron pillar at Mehrauli (Delhi) attributes its erection to a king named 'Chandra', identified by most scholars with:
questions.e: The rust-resistant Mehrauli iron pillar's 'Chandra' is generally identified with Chandragupta II Vikramaditya of the Guptas.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Harshavardhana's court poet Banabhatta wrote:
questions.e: Banabhatta authored Harshacharita (Harsha's biography) and the romance Kadambari; Hiuen Tsang visited during Harsha's reign.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II was composed by Ravikirti and records his victory over:
questions.e: Ravikirti's Aihole prashasti (634 CE) celebrates Pulakeshin II's check of Harsha on the Narmada; Narasimhavarman later defeated Pulakeshin.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chola administration:
1. The Uttaramerur inscription details the electoral system of village assemblies.
2. The Chola army had a strong navy.
3. Land revenue was the main source of state income.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Uttaramerur (Parantaka I) describes kudavolai elections; Rajaraja I and Rajendra I built a formidable navy (Sri Vijaya expedition); land revenue anchored Chola finance.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Brihadeshwara Temple at Thanjavur was built by:
questions.e: Rajaraja I (c. 1010 CE) built the Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshwara) temple; Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Sangam literature is/are correct?
1. It is the earliest known Tamil literature.
2. Tolkappiyam is a work on Tamil grammar.
3. The Sangams were assemblies of Tamil poets held at Madurai.
questions.e: Sangam corpus (c. 300 BCE–300 CE) is the earliest Tamil literature; Tolkappiyam is its grammatical treatise; tradition speaks of three Sangams at Madurai.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The port city of Arikamedu, an Indo-Roman trading station, is located near:
questions.e: Arikamedu (near Puducherry) yielded Roman amphorae, Arretine ware and beads — evidence of 1st-century CE Indo-Roman trade; Muziris was on the Malabar coast.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following was the capital of the Pallavas?
questions.e: Kanchipuram was the Pallava capital; Mahabalipuram's shore temple and rathas are Pallava (Narasimhavarman I–II) monuments.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Dashavatara' temple at Deogarh is an example of:
questions.e: Deogarh's Dashavatara temple (c. 6th century, Jhansi district) is a classic Gupta panchayatana temple with the famous Sheshashayi Vishnu panel.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vedic 'Sabha' and 'Samiti':
1. They were popular assemblies of the Rig Vedic period.
2. Women participated in the Sabhas and Samitis.
3. The king was bound by their decisions.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Sabha and Samiti were tribal assemblies with women's participation (Rig Veda); the king sought their support but was not constitutionally bound by them.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The earliest Buddhist stupa believed to contain the Buddha's relics and patronised by Ashoka, later enlarged by the Shungas, is at:
questions.e: Sanchi's Great Stupa: Ashokan brick core, Shunga stone casing and railings; Bharhut's railings are Shunga; Amaravati is Satavahana–Ikshvaku.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following texts is known as the 'Fifth Veda'?
questions.e: The Mahabharata calls itself the fifth Veda; the Natya Shastra is also sometimes so styled.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Junagadh inscription' of Rudradaman I is significant because it:
o: Is the earliest long inscription in chaste Sanskrit
questions.e: Rudradaman's Junagadh rock inscription (c. 150 CE) on Sudarshana lake repairs is the first major royal inscription in classical Sanskrit prose.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the position of women in the Rig Vedic period:
1. Women attended assemblies and offered sacrifices.
2. Child marriage was widely prevalent.
3. Gargi and Maitreyi were noted women philosophers.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Rig Vedic women enjoyed relative freedom — assembly participation, composers like Lopamudra, philosophers Gargi and Maitreyi (Brihadaranyaka); child marriage is a later development.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The capital of the ancient kingdom of Magadha under the Haryanka dynasty was first at Rajagriha and later shifted to:
questions.e: Udayin (Ajatashatru's successor) shifted the Magadhan capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra (confluence of Ganga, Son and Gandak).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following Mahajanapadas was a republic (sangha) rather than a monarchy?
questions.e: Vajji (with capital Vaishali) was a confederacy of eight clans including the Lichchhavis — a gana-sangha; the Buddha praised its seven principles of non-decline.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'second urbanisation' in Indian history is associated with which period?
o: The Mahajanapada period (6th century BCE onwards)
questions.e: The 6th century BCE saw the second urbanisation — towns like Pataliputra, Vaishali, Shravasti — driven by iron, surplus agriculture and trade; the first was Harappan.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Punch-marked coins, the earliest coins of India, were made of:
questions.e: Punch-marked (ahat) coins were predominantly silver (some copper), bearing multiple punched symbols; issued from the 6th century BCE by Mahajanapadas and Mauryas.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Ajanta caves are primarily associated with:
questions.e: Ajanta's 29 caves (Satavahana–Vakataka phases) are Buddhist — chaityas and viharas with Jataka murals; Ellora has all three faiths.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Ellora caves is/are correct?
1. They contain Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.
2. The Kailasa temple was excavated under Rashtrakuta patronage.
3. Cave 16 (Kailasa) was built during Krishna I's reign.
questions.e: Ellora's 34 caves span Buddhism, Hinduism and Jainism; the monolithic Kailasa temple (Cave 16) was excavated under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Vikram Samvat era (57 BCE) is traditionally associated with:
o: King Vikramaditya of Ujjain defeating the Shakas
questions.e: Vikram Samvat (57 BCE) commemorates the legendary Vikramaditya of Ujjain's victory over the Shakas; Shaka era (78 CE) marks Kanishka; Harsha era (606 CE) Harsha's accession.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sangam-age Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas:
1. The Cheras controlled the Malabar coast with ports like Muziris.
2. Karikala was a famous Chola king credited with building Kallanai.
3. The Pandyas had their capital at Madurai.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Cheras (Malabar/Muziris trade), Karikala Chola (Kallanai/Grand Anicut on the Kaveri), Pandyas of Madurai — the three Sangam-age Tamil powers.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea' is a:
o: Greek work on Indian Ocean trade (1st century CE)
questions.e: The Periplus (c. 1st century CE), by an anonymous Greek-Egyptian merchant, details Red Sea–Indian Ocean trade ports including Barygaza and Muziris.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Ancient History — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following was NOT a centre of learning in ancient India?
questions.e: Taxila, Nalanda and Vikramashila were famed ancient universities; Fatehpur Sikri is a Mughal (Akbar's) capital, not an ancient learning centre.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the classical dances of India:
1. Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu.
2. Kathakali is from Kerala.
3. Odissi is from Odisha.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathakali (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha) — all correctly matched; the Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises 8 classical forms (plus Chhau).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following classical dances with their states:
A. Kathak — 1. Assam
B. Sattriya — 2. Uttar Pradesh
C. Kuchipudi — 3. Andhra Pradesh
D. Manipuri — 4. Manipur
questions.e: Kathak (UP), Sattriya (Assam, Sankardev monasteries), Kuchipudi (AP), Manipuri (Manipur, Raslila) — correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Natya Shastra' is attributed to:
questions.e: Bharata's Natya Shastra (c. 200 BCE–200 CE) is the foundational treatise on dramaturgy, music and dance (rasa theory).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Hindustani and Carnatic music:
1. Hindustani music was influenced by Persian traditions.
2. Carnatic music emphasises kritis and is centred in South India.
3. Tansen was a court musician of Akbar.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Hindustani (Persian influence, gharanas), Carnatic (kriti-based, Trinity: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Shyama Shastri), Tansen (Akbar's navratna) — all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Dhrupad' is:
questions.e: Dhrupad (Tansen's lineage): austere, meditative Hindustani form — older than khayal; the Dagar brothers are its exponents.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following musical instruments with their maestros:
A. Sitar — 1. Bismillah Khan
B. Shehnai — 2. Ravi Shankar
C. Tabla — 3. Hariprasad Chaurasia
D. Flute — 4. Zakir Hussain
questions.e: Ravi Shankar (sitar), Bismillah Khan (shehnai), Zakir Hussain (tabla), Hariprasad Chaurasia (flute) — iconic pairings.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Sangeet Natak Akademi' was established in:
questions.e: SNA (1952): apex body for performing arts; its Tagore Ratna/Tagore Puraskar and Akademi awards honour artists.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:
1. The Taj Mahal was among the first Indian sites inscribed (1983).
2. India has over 40 World Heritage Sites.
3. Dholavira (2021) is a Harappan city World Heritage Site.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Taj, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora (1983 first batch); 40+ sites now (43+ by 2024, incl. Santiniketan 2023, Hoysala temples 2023); Dholavira inscribed 2021.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Ramnagar Ramlila' is famous as:
o: A UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage-associated Ramlila of Varanasi
questions.e: Varanasi's Ramnagar Ramlila (month-long, Kashi Naresh's patronage) — Ramlila traditions are on UNESCO's intangible list (2008).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following UNESCO Intangible Heritage elements of India:
A. Kumbh Mela — 1. 2017
B. Yoga — 2. 2016
C. Ramlila — 3. 2008
D. Chhau dance — 4. 2010
questions.e: Ramlila (2008), Chhau (2010), Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017) — inscription years; Durga Puja (2021) and Garba (2023) followed.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Pattachitra' painting style belongs to:
questions.e: Pattachitra (cloth scrolls: Jagannath themes in Odisha, Kalighat-adjacent Bengal patas) — GI-tagged craft.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Art & Culture — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about miniature paintings:
1. Mughal miniatures blended Persian and Indian styles.
2. Rajput miniatures include the Pahari and Rajasthani schools.
3. The Kangra style is known for Bhagavata Purana themes.
Select the correct answer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the measurement of national income in India:
1. The Central Statistics Office (now NSO) compiles national accounts.
2. The base year for GDP series was revised to 2011-12.
3. GDP is measured at both constant and current prices.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NSO (under MoSPI) compiles national accounts; the 2011-12 base revision (2015) changed methodology; GDP is released at constant and current prices.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The difference between GDP and GNP is:
questions.e: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad (income of residents from overseas minus foreigners' income domestically).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about inflation measurement in India is/are correct?
1. CPI (Combined) is the RBI's nominal anchor for inflation targeting.
2. WPI measures wholesale prices and includes services.
3. The inflation target is 4% CPI with a ±2% band.
questions.e: Since 2016 the RBI targets CPI (Combined) at 4% ±2%; WPI covers only goods (no services) with base 2011-12.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee:
1. It has six members — three from RBI and three external.
2. The RBI Governor has a casting vote.
3. It decides the policy repo rate.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: MPC (2016, RBI Act amendment): 3 RBI officials + 3 government nominees; Governor's casting vote; it fixes the repo rate to hit the inflation target.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: An increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio by the RBI will:
o: Reduce lendable resources of banks and tighten liquidity
questions.e: Higher CRR locks more deposits with the RBI interest-free, shrinking lendable funds — a quantitative tightening tool.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Match the following RBI instruments with their nature:
A. Repo rate — 1. Rate at which RBI borrows from banks
B. Reverse repo rate — 2. Rate at which RBI lends to banks
C. Bank rate — 3. Long-term rate for RBI lending without collateral
D. Marginal Standing Facility — 4. Overnight emergency borrowing window for banks
questions.e: Repo (RBI lends), reverse repo (RBI borrows), bank rate (long-term, no collateral), MSF (overnight emergency against SLR securities).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Open Market Operations of the RBI refer to:
o: Intervention in the forex market only
Buying and selling of government securities to adjust liquidity
questions.e: OMOs — RBI's purchase/sale of G-secs — inject or absorb durable liquidity; forex intervention is separate.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act is/are correct?
1. It was enacted in 2003.
2. It originally targeted eliminating the revenue deficit.
3. The N.K. Singh Committee reviewed it in 2017.
questions.e: FRBM (2003): fiscal deficit 3% of GDP, revenue deficit elimination targets; the N.K. Singh panel (2017) suggested a debt-anchor framework (60% combined debt).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The difference between the fiscal deficit and interest payments is called the:
questions.e: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments; it shows the current year's borrowing excluding past-debt servicing.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union Budget:
1. It is presented under Article 112 as the Annual Financial Statement.
2. The Railway Budget was merged with it from 2017-18.
3. The budget is presented on 1 February since 2017.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Article 112's Annual Financial Statement; Bibek Debroy panel led to the 2017 railway-budget merger; presentation moved from 28 Feb to 1 Feb (2017).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following taxes is NOT subsumed under GST?
questions.e: GST subsumed excise (except on petroleum/tobacco), service tax, VAT, octroi/entry tax; excise on petroleum remains outside GST (as do basic customs duties).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Laffer Curve' illustrates the relationship between:
questions.e: The Laffer curve posits revenue rises with tax rates up to a point, then falls as higher rates discourage activity.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the NABARD:
1. It was established in 1982.
2. It refinances rural credit institutions.
3. It regulates cooperative banks and RRBs.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NABARD (1982, Shivraman Committee): apex refinance for agriculture/rural credit; supervises RRBs and cooperative banks (excluding primary cooperatives' regulation nuances).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Priority Sector Lending' target for domestic scheduled commercial banks is:
questions.e: Domestic banks must lend 40% of ANBC to priority sectors (agriculture 18%, micro-enterprises 7.5%, weaker sections 12% sub-targets).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Small Finance Banks is/are correct?
1. They primarily serve unserved and underserved sections.
2. The minimum paid-up capital requirement was ₹200 crore.
3. They can accept deposits like commercial banks.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: SFBs (licensed from 2015, e.g., AU, Equitas): financial inclusion focus, ₹200 crore minimum capital (later raised norms), full deposit-taking banks.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
The 'Payments Banks' in India:
1. Can accept demand deposits up to ₹2 lakh per customer
2. Cannot issue loans or credit cards
3. Were recommended by the Nachiket Mor Committee
questions.e: Payments banks (Nachiket Mor panel): deposits capped (raised to ₹2 lakh in 2021), no lending, must invest 75% in G-secs — e.g., Airtel, Paytm, India Post Payments Bank.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016:
1. It provides a time-bound resolution process (330 days including litigation).
2. The Committee of Creditors decides the resolution plan.
3. It applies to companies, LLPs and individuals.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: IBC (2016): 330-day outer limit, CoC (financial creditors) approves plans with 66% vote, NCLT adjudicates; covers companies, LLPs, partnership firms and individuals.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'SARFAESI Act, 2002' enables banks to:
o: Enforce security interest without court intervention
questions.e: SARFAESI lets secured creditors (banks/FIs) seize and sell collateral of defaulters above ₹1 lakh dues without court process (except farm land).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following is measured by the 'Human Development Index'?
1. Life expectancy
2. Education (mean and expected years of schooling)
3. Per capita income (GNI)
questions.e: UNDP's HDI (Mahbub ul Haq/Amartya Sen): health, education, income — geometric mean of the three dimension indices.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Multidimensional Poverty Index' was developed by:
questions.e: The MPI (2010, Oxford Poverty & Human Development Initiative + UNDP) measures deprivations in health, education and living standards; NITI Aayog releases India's national MPI.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act:
1. It guarantees 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year.
2. Unemployment allowance is payable if work is not provided within 15 days.
3. At least one-third of beneficiaries must be women.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: MGNREGA (2005): 100 days/household, 15-day work guarantee with unemployment allowance, one-third women's participation — the world's largest workfare programme.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'National Food Security Act, 2013' covers approximately what share of the population?
questions.e: NFSA covers up to 75% of rural and 50% of urban population (~81 crore) with 5 kg/person/month at ₹3/2/1 per kg (now free under PMGKAY extension).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the 'Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana' is/are correct?
1. It aims at universal banking access with zero-balance accounts.
2. It provides RuPay debit cards with in-built accident insurance.
3. It is a pillar of the JAM trinity.
questions.e: PMJDY (2014): zero-balance accounts, RuPay cards with ₹2 lakh accident cover, overdraft facility — the 'J' in JAM (Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Goods and Services Tax' is best described as:
o: A tax levied only by states
A destination-based indirect tax on consumption
questions.e: GST (101st Amendment, 2017) is a destination-based, dual (CGST+SGST/IGST) indirect tax subsuming most indirect taxes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Make in India' initiative:
1. It was launched in 2014.
2. It aims to raise manufacturing's share of GDP to 25%.
3. It covers 25 sectors of the economy.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Make in India (Sept 2014): manufacturing hub goal (25% of GDP), 25 focus sectors, with FDI liberalisation and ease-of-doing-business reforms.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Startup India' initiative was launched in the year:
questions.e: Startup India (January 2016): tax holidays, self-certification, Fund of Funds — DPIIT recognises startups.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Special Economic Zones' is/are correct?
1. They are deemed foreign territory for trade purposes.
2. The SEZ Act was passed in 2005.
3. Units enjoy tax holidays and single-window clearance.
questions.e: SEZs (Act 2005): duty-free enclaves deemed outside the customs territory, with income-tax benefits and single-window clearance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Foreign Exchange Management Act' replaced FERA in the year:
questions.e: FEMA (1999, effective 2000) replaced the draconian FERA (1973) — shifting from 'control' to 'management' of forex; violations became civil offences.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's forex reserves:
1. They are managed by the RBI.
2. They include foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the IMF reserve position.
3. They provide import cover and external stability.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: RBI manages reserves comprising FCA, gold, SDRs and RTP; they cushion the rupee and cover imports/debt.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: A 'current account deficit' in the balance of payments means:
o: Imports of goods and services exceed exports plus net transfers
questions.e: CAD = trade deficit in goods/services adjusted for primary/secondary income; financed by capital inflows or reserve drawdown.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'FDI' and 'FPI' is/are correct?
1. FDI involves lasting interest (10%+ voting power). 
2. FPI is more volatile ('hot money').
3. Both are part of the capital account.
questions.e: FDI (≥10% stake, lasting control) vs FPI (portfolio, volatile); both sit in the capital account of the BoP.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Masala Bonds' are:
o: Dollar bonds issued by Indian firms abroad
questions.e: Masala bonds (2015, IFC's pioneering issue): rupee-denominated offshore bonds — the currency risk sits with the foreign investor.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'NITI Aayog':
1. It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
2. It follows a bottom-up approach with cooperative federalism.
3. It allocates central plan assistance to states.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NITI Aayog (1 Jan 2015) replaced the Planning Commission as a think-tank for cooperative/competitive federalism; it does not allocate plan funds (Finance Commission does transfers).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Fifteenth Finance Commission' (2020–26) was chaired by:
questions.e: N.K. Singh chaired the 15th FC: 41% vertical devolution to states (after J&K reorganisation), with criteria including income distance and demographic performance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is the largest component of the Union Government's tax revenue?
o: Corporation tax and income tax (direct taxes)
questions.e: Direct taxes (corporation + personal income tax) together exceed GST collections as the largest revenue source in recent budgets — approximate, varies by year.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Disinvestment' of public sector enterprises in India began in earnest with:
questions.e: 1991 liberalisation began PSU disinvestment (Rangarajan Committee); strategic disinvestment/privatisation accelerated later (e.g., Air India 2022).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'New Industrial Policy, 1991':
1. It abolished industrial licensing for most industries.
2. It opened most sectors to private and foreign investment.
3. It retained licensing only for a short list of strategic industries.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The 1991 policy delicensed industry (except ~18, later 6 compulsory-licence sectors), raised FDI caps, and ended most public-sector monopolies.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'LPG' reforms of 1991 stand for:
questions.e: LPG = Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation — the Manmohan Singh–Narasimha Rao 1991 reform package.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Demonetisation' (2016) is/are correct?
1. ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes ceased to be legal tender on 8 November 2016.
2. Its stated objectives included curbing black money and counterfeiting.
3. The RBI Act was amended to enable it.
questions.e: 8 Nov 2016: ₹500/₹1000 demonetised under Section 26(2) of the RBI Act (no amendment needed); objectives included black money, terror funding and counterfeiting.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code' adjudicating authority for companies is the:
questions.e: NCLT adjudicates corporate insolvency; DRT handles individual/partnership cases; NCLAT is the appellate body.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Non-Performing Assets':
1. A loan becomes NPA if interest/instalment is overdue for 90 days.
2. The '4R' strategy (Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation, Reforms) addressed them.
3. Asset Reconstruction Companies buy bad loans from banks.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: 90-day NPA norm; the government's 4R approach; ARCs (under SARFAESI) acquire stressed assets — all correct.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Prompt Corrective Action' framework of the RBI applies to:
o: Weak banks breaching capital, asset quality or profitability thresholds
questions.e: PCA (revised 2017) restricts weak banks (CRAR, net NPA, RoA triggers) on lending, dividends and expansion until health is restored.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Inflation targeting' in India is/are correct?
1. The framework was formalised in 2016.
2. Failure to meet the target requires the RBI to report to the government.
3. The target is reviewed every five years.
questions.e: Flexible inflation targeting (RBI Act amendment, 2016): 4% ±2%; the RBI must explain misses to the government; the target is reviewed every five years.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'base year' for the Consumer Price Index (Combined) in India is:
questions.e: CPI (Combined, base 2012) covers rural, urban and combined inflation; CPI-IW (industrial workers) uses base 2016.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Wholesale Price Index':
1. It is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser.
2. Its base year is 2011-12.
3. Food articles have the highest weight among primary articles.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: WPI (Economic Adviser, DPIIT; base 2011-12): manufactured products ~64%, primary articles ~22.6%, fuel ~13.2%. Statement 3 is imprecise — manufactured products dominate overall.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Phillips Curve' shows the relationship between:
questions.e: The Phillips curve posits an inverse short-run relation between inflation and unemployment; stagflation challenged it in the 1970s.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a 'regressive tax'?
o: A uniform GST rate on essential goods
questions.e: A flat-rate tax on essentials takes a larger share of the poor's income — regressive; progressive income tax takes a larger share from the rich.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'GST Compensation Cess' was levied to compensate states for revenue loss for a period of:
questions.e: The 101st Amendment guaranteed compensation for five years (till June 2022), funded by the cess on luxury/sin goods; the cess continued after 2022 to repay back-to-back loans.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Digital India' initiatives:
1. UPI was developed by the NPCI.
2. India Stack includes Aadhaar, e-KYC and DigiLocker.
3. The Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile trinity enables direct benefit transfer.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: UPI (NPCI, 2016), India Stack layers, and JAM-driven DBT are the pillars of India's digital public infrastructure.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Open Network for Digital Commerce' (ONDC) aims to:
o: Democratise e-commerce with interoperable open protocols
questions.e: ONDC (DPIIT, 2021) is an open e-commerce network unbundling buyer/seller apps from the transaction layer — UPI-like interoperability for commerce.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' is/are correct?
1. It was announced in 2020 with a ₹20 lakh crore package.
2. It includes Production Linked Incentive schemes.
3. It focuses on five pillars: economy, infrastructure, technology, demography, demand.
questions.e: Aatmanirbhar Bharat (May 2020, ~₹20 lakh crore ≈ 10% of GDP): PLI schemes across sectors; the five pillars (economy, infrastructure, system/technology, demography, demand) frame it.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Production Linked Incentive' scheme provides:
o: Incentives to firms based on incremental sales of manufactured goods
questions.e: PLI (2020) rewards incremental production/sales in 14 sectors (electronics, pharma, autos, textiles etc.) to boost domestic manufacturing.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'MSME' sector:
1. The revised definition (2020) uses investment and turnover criteria.
2. Udyam registration is required for MSME benefits.
3. MSMEs contribute about one-third of India's GDP.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: 2020 revision: micro (₹1 cr investment/₹5 cr turnover), small (₹10 cr/₹50 cr), medium (₹50 cr/₹250 cr); Udyam registration; ~30% of GDP and major employment.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'MUDRA Yojana' provides loans under three categories — Shishu, Kishore and Tarun — with maximum limits of:
questions.e: PMMY: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001–₹5 lakh), Tarun (₹5–10 lakh); Tarun Plus (up to ₹20 lakh) was added later.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Direct Benefit Transfer' is/are correct?
1. It transfers subsidies directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts.
2. PAHAL (LPG subsidy) was the first major DBT scheme.
3. It uses the Aadhaar Payment Bridge.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: DBT (2013): direct transfers cutting leakages; PAHAL is the world's largest DBT scheme; APB routes Aadhaar-linked payments.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana' provides crop insurance with farmer premium capped at:
o: 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops
questions.e: PMFBY (2016): farmer pays max 2% (kharif), 1.5% (rabi), 5% (commercial/horticulture); the balance is shared by Centre and states.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'e-NAM' platform:
1. It is a pan-India electronic trading portal for agricultural commodities.
2. It aims at 'One Nation, One Market'.
3. It is implemented by the Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: e-NAM (2016, SFAC): online mandi integration for transparent price discovery toward one national agriculture market.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Minimum Support Price' in India is recommended by the:
o: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
questions.e: CACP recommends MSPs (currently for 22 mandated crops + sugarcane FRP); the Cabinet approves; FCI/Nafed undertake procurement.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ecological succession:
1. Primary succession occurs on lifeless areas like bare rock.
2. Secondary succession occurs where a community was disturbed but soil remains.
3. The climax community is stable and self-perpetuating.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Primary (bare rock/lava), secondary (post-disturbance with soil), climax (stable equilibrium) — the standard succession sequence.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The '10% law' of energy transfer in food chains was proposed by:
questions.e: Lindeman's trophic-dynamic (1942) 10% law: only ~10% of energy passes to each successive trophic level.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Match the following ecological terms:
A. Autotrophs — 1. Decomposers
B. Heterotrophs — 2. Producers
C. Saprotrophs — 3. Consumers
