questions.e: Autotrophs (producers, photosynthesis), heterotrophs (consumers), saprotrophs (decomposers like fungi/bacteria).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'biodiversity hotspots' is/are correct?
1. The concept was introduced by Norman Myers.
2. India has four hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Sundaland.
3. A hotspot must have at least 1,500 endemic plant species.
questions.e: Myers (1988/2000): hotspots need ≥1,500 endemic vascular plants and ≥70% habitat loss; India hosts four (Nicobar falls in Sundaland).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Red Data Book' is published by the:
questions.e: IUCN's Red List of Threatened Species assesses extinction risk (categories: LC, NT, VU, EN, CR, EW, EX).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the categories of protected areas in India:
1. National Parks ban all human activity except permitted tourism.
2. Wildlife Sanctuaries allow limited human activity.
3. Biosphere Reserves have core, buffer and transition zones.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: National Parks (strictest, Wildlife Protection Act 1972), sanctuaries (regulated use), biosphere reserves (UNESCO MAB: core-buffer-transition) are all correctly described.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The first national park established in India was:
o: Jim Corbett National Park (1936, as Hailey National Park)
questions.e: Hailey National Park (1936, United Provinces) — renamed Corbett; Kaziranga (1974), Kanha and Gir came later.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Match the following national parks with their states:
A. Kaziranga — 1. Madhya Pradesh
B. Kanha — 2. Assam
C. Gir — 3. Kerala
D. Periyar — 4. Gujarat
questions.e: Kaziranga (Assam, one-horned rhino), Kanha (MP, tiger/barasingha), Gir (Gujarat, Asiatic lion), Periyar (Kerala, elephant/tiger reserve).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Tiger was launched in the year:
questions.e: Project Tiger (1973, from Jim Corbett NP) now covers 50+ tiger reserves; NTCA oversees it; the Wildlife Protection Act came in 1972.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Project Elephant:
1. It was launched in 1992.
2. It focuses on elephant corridors and human-elephant conflict.
3. Kerala has the highest number of elephants in India.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Project Elephant (1992) addresses corridors and conflict; recent elephant census data put Karnataka among the highest — Kerala is not definitively first, so statement 3 is uncertain.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Great Indian Bustard' is critically endangered and found mainly in:
questions.e: The GIB (Rajasthan's state bird) survives in the Desert NP and Gujarat grasslands; power lines and habitat loss drive its decline.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Ramsar Sites' is/are correct?
1. They are wetlands of international importance under the 1971 Ramsar Convention.
2. India has the largest network of Ramsar sites in Asia.
3. Chilika Lake was India's first Ramsar site.
questions.e: Ramsar (Iran, 1971) wetlands; India has Asia's largest tally (75+ sites and growing); Chilika and Keoladeo were India's first two (1981).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Montreux Record' under the Ramsar Convention lists:
o: Wetlands where ecological character has changed or is changing
questions.e: The Montreux Record flags Ramsar sites needing priority conservation (Loktak and Keoladeo were once listed; both later removed).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about mangroves:
1. They grow in intertidal zones of tropical coasts.
2. They have pneumatophores (breathing roots).
3. The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Mangroves: salt-tolerant intertidal forests with pneumatophores, vivipary; Sundarbans is the largest contiguous tract.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following is a correct match of endangered species and their habitat?
1. Snow leopard — Himalayas
2. Lion-tailed macaque — Western Ghats
3. Hangul — Dachigam (Kashmir)
questions.e: Snow leopard (high Himalaya), lion-tailed macaque (Western Ghats evergreen), hangul/Kashmir stag (Dachigam) — all correct.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Wildlife Protection Act, 1972' provides for schedules. Which schedule lists species with the highest protection?
questions.e: Schedule I (tiger, elephant, GIB etc.) carries the harshest penalties; the 2022 amendment rationalised schedules (I–IV).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Forest Conservation Act, 1980':
1. It requires central approval for diversion of forest land.
2. It was amended in 2023.
3. It applies to all deemed forests.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: FCA 1980: Centre's prior approval for non-forest use; the 2023 amendment (Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam) narrowed its scope — deemed forests' coverage became contested, so statement 3 is debatable.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'National Green Tribunal' was established in 2010 under:
questions.e: NGT (2010 Act): specialised environmental adjudication applying sustainable development, precautionary and polluter-pays principles.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the 'Environment (Protection) Act, 1986' is/are correct?
1. It was enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy.
2. It empowers the Centre to take all measures to protect the environment.
3. It provides for environmental impact assessment notifications.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: EPA 1986 (post-Bhopal, 1984): umbrella legislation; Section 3 powers; EIA notifications (1994, 2006) issued under it.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'EIA Notification, 2006' categorises projects into:
o: Category A (central appraisal) and Category B (state appraisal)
questions.e: EIA 2006: Category A (MoEFCC appraisal) and B (SEIAA); B1 needs EIA, B2 doesn't — distinct from pollution-control's red/orange/green.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Kyoto Protocol':
1. It was adopted in 1997.
2. It imposed binding emission targets on developed countries.
3. India had binding targets under it.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Kyoto (1997, in force 2005): Annex-I binding cuts; developing countries like India had no binding targets (CBDR principle).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Paris Agreement' aims to limit global warming to:
questions.e: Paris (2015): well below 2°C above pre-industrial, pursuing 1.5°C; NDCs are voluntary pledges with 5-year ratchets.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
India's updated NDC (2022) includes which of the following targets?
1. 50% cumulative electric power from non-fossil sources by 2030
2. Reduce emission intensity of GDP by 45% by 2030 (vs 2005)
3. Net-zero by 2070
questions.e: India's NDC: 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030, 45% emission-intensity cut, and the Panchamrit net-zero-by-2070 pledge (COP26, Glasgow).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Convention on Biological Diversity' was opened for signature at:
questions.e: CBD (Rio 1992): conservation, sustainable use, fair benefit-sharing — implemented via the Nagoya Protocol (access and benefit sharing).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'CITES':
1. It regulates international trade in endangered species.
2. Species are listed in three appendices.
3. India is a party to it.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: CITES (1973): Appendix I (no commercial trade), II (regulated), III (cooperation); India is a signatory.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Basel Convention' deals with:
questions.e: Basel (1989): control of hazardous waste shipments; the Ban Amendment prohibits OECD-to-non-OECD hazardous exports.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'e-waste' in India is/are correct?
1. The E-Waste (Management) Rules were notified in 2016.
2. Extended Producer Responsibility applies to manufacturers.
3. India is among the largest e-waste generators.
questions.e: E-Waste Rules 2016 (amended 2022): EPR on producers, CPCB/SPCB enforcement; India ranks among the top e-waste generators globally.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Single-Use Plastic' ban in India (2022) covers:
o: Identified single-use plastic items like cutlery, straws and cigarette packets' wrapping
questions.e: From 1 July 2022, 19 low-utility high-litter SUP items were banned; carry-bag thickness was raised to 120 microns (Dec 2022).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'air pollution' control in India:
1. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1981.
2. The National Clean Air Programme targets 40% PM reduction by 2026 in 131 cities.
3. GRAP is invoked in Delhi-NCR during severe pollution.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Air Act 1981; NCAP (2019, revised 40% target by 2025-26 vs 2017); GRAP (CAQM) stages curbs by AQI — all correct.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'National Action Plan on Climate Change' (2008) includes how many missions?
questions.e: NAPCC's 8 missions: Solar, Energy Efficiency, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Sustainable Habitat, Strategic Knowledge.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the 'National Solar Mission' is/are correct?
1. It is part of the NAPCC.
2. India targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030.
3. The International Solar Alliance is headquartered in India.
questions.e: NSM (2010, NAPCC mission); 500 GW non-fossil by 2030 (Panchamrit); ISA HQ at Gurugram — all correct.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Chipko Movement' (1973) was led by:
questions.e: Chipko (1973, Mandal village, Chamoli): tree-hugging against logging; Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt were its faces.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Narmada Bachao Andolan':
1. It opposed large dams on the Narmada.
2. Medha Patkar was its prominent leader.
3. The Supreme Court allowed the Sardar Sarovar dam with conditions.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NBA (1985): anti-large-dam movement; Patkar's leadership; SC's 2000 judgment permitted Sardar Sarovar's completion with resettlement conditions.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Silent Valley' was saved from a hydroelectric project due to protests led by:
questions.e: KSSP's 'Save Silent Valley' campaign (1970s–80s) stopped the Kunthipuzha project; Silent Valley became a national park in 1984.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following is a correct match of environmental movements?
1. Appiko — Karnataka (tree-hugging)
2. Tehri anti-dam — Uttarakhand
3. Chilika anti-aqua culture — Odisha
questions.e: Appiko (1983, Uttara Kannada), Tehri dam opposition (Bahuguna), Chilika fisherfolk vs aquaculture — all correctly matched.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Bishnoi' community is known for:
questions.e: Bishnois (Guru Jambheshwar's 29 principles): the 1730 Khejarli massacre (363 killed protecting khejri trees) under Amrita Devi — precursor of Chipko.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'wetlands' in India:
1. India has the largest number of Ramsar sites in Asia.
2. Wetlands are protected under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017.
3. The Montreux Record lists degraded Ramsar sites.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: India's 75+ Ramsar sites lead Asia; the 2017 Rules decentralised wetland management to states; Montreux flags sites with changed ecological character.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Keoladeo National Park' is famous for:
o: Migratory birds, especially the Siberian crane
questions.e: Keoladeo (Bharatpur, Rajasthan): World Heritage wetland; once wintered the Siberian crane (no longer visiting) — now rich in waterfowl.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'tiger reserves' is/are correct?
1. They have core (critical tiger habitat) and buffer zones.
2. Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam is India's largest tiger reserve.
3. The NTCA was set up under the Wildlife Protection Act amendment of 2006.
questions.e: Core-buffer model; Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam (AP/Telangana) is the largest; NTCA and the Tiger and Other Endangered Species Crime Control Bureau came via the 2006 amendment.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'one-horned rhinoceros' is found in India primarily in:
o: Kaziranga and other Assam protected areas
questions.e: The Indian rhino (Rhinoceros unicornis): Kaziranga holds ~70% of the world population; also Manas, Pobitora, Jaldapara.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Asiatic lion':
1. It survives in the wild only in Gir, Gujarat.
2. It is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
3. Project Lion was announced for its conservation.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Gir is the sole wild home; IUCN Endangered (population recovered to 600+); Project Lion (2020) funds habitat and a second home (Kuno proposal debated).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Ganges river dolphin' was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in:
questions.e: Platanista gangetica declared National Aquatic Animal (2009); Vikramshila (Bihar) sanctuary protects it; Project Dolphin launched 2020.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'coral reefs' in India is/are correct?
1. They occur in the Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch and Lakshadweep.
2. They are protected under the Wildlife Protection Act.
3. Coral bleaching events have been recorded in Indian reefs.
questions.e: India's four major reef areas (Mannar, Kutch, Lakshadweep, A&N); corals are Schedule I protected; bleaching recorded in 1998, 2010, 2016 events.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
The 'Gulf of Mannar' is known for:
1. Coral reefs and dugongs
2. Being India's first marine biosphere reserve
3. Pearl fishing traditions
questions.e: Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu): 21 islands, corals, dugongs, historic pearl fisheries; declared biosphere reserve in 1989.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'biodiversity' in India:
1. India is one of 17 megadiverse countries.
2. It holds about 8% of global biodiversity.
3. The Biological Diversity Act was passed in 2002.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: India: megadiverse (17 countries), ~7–8% of recorded species on 2.4% of land; BD Act 2002 (NBA, SBBs, BMCs; amended 2023).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Nagoya Protocol' is related to:
o: Access to genetic resources and benefit-sharing
questions.e: Nagoya (2010, CBD): ABS — fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources and traditional knowledge.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'carbon trading' is/are correct?
1. The Kyoto Protocol introduced Clean Development Mechanism.
2. The Paris Agreement's Article 6 enables carbon markets.
3. India launched the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme in 2023.
questions.e: Kyoto's CDM/JI/ET; Paris Article 6 (6.2, 6.4); India's CCTS (2023, Bureau of Energy Efficiency) for obligated entities — all correct.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Green Climate Fund' was established under the:
questions.e: GCF (Cancun, 2010, UNFCCC): $100-billion climate-finance vehicle for developing countries.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'desertification' in India:
1. About one-third of India's land is degraded/desertified.
2. India hosted COP-14 of the UNCCD in 2019.
3. India pledged to restore 26 million hectares by 2030.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: ISRO's desertification atlas (~30% land degradation); UNCCD COP-14 at Delhi (2019); Bonn Challenge-linked 26 mha restoration pledge — all correct.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Aravalli' range is significant environmentally because it:
o: Is the origin of the Ganga
Checks the eastward spread of the Thar Desert
Hosts the highest peak of India
questions.e: The Aravallis (oldest fold mountains, Guru Shikhar highest) act as a barrier to desertification of eastern Rajasthan — mining bans protect them.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'groundwater' in India is/are correct?
1. India is the world's largest groundwater user.
2. The Atal Bhujal Yojana addresses groundwater management.
3. CGWB monitors groundwater levels.
questions.e: India extracts the most groundwater globally (~25% of world use); Atal Bhujal Yojana (2020, 7 states); CGWB monitors and notifies over-exploited blocks.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Namami Gange' programme was launched in:
questions.e: Namami Gange (2014, ₹20,000 crore): NMCG-led Ganga rejuvenation — sewage treatment, riverfront, biodiversity (dolphins, gharials).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'National Water Policy':
1. The latest policy was adopted in 2012.
2. It treats water as an economic good.
3. It prioritises drinking water over other uses.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NWP 2012: water as economic good, demand management, drinking-water priority; a new policy draft has been under discussion — approximate on 'latest'.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Ken-Betwa' river interlinking project connects rivers in:
questions.e: Ken-Betwa (first ILR project, foundation 2021): Daudhan dam (MP) to irrigate Bundelkhand in MP–UP; Panna tiger reserve submergence is the controversy.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022' is/are correct?
1. They introduced EPR certificates tradable on a portal.
2. They cover 106 electrical and electronic items.
3. They apply to manufacturers, producers and recyclers.
questions.e: E-Waste Rules 2022: EPR authorisation, credit trading on CPCB portal, expanded item coverage — all correct in substance.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Swachh Bharat Mission' was launched on:
questions.e: SBM (2 Oct 2014, Gandhi Jayanti): rural (ODF by 2019 claimed) and urban missions; SBM 2.0 (2021) targets garbage-free cities.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'solid waste management' in India:
1. The SWM Rules, 2016 mandate segregation at source.
2. Bulk waste generators must process waste on-site.
3. Waste-to-energy is promoted under the rules.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: SWM Rules 2016: source segregation (3 streams), bulk generators' on-site processing, user fees, and waste-processing promotion — all correct.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'National Biodiversity Authority' is headquartered at:
questions.e: NBA (2003, BD Act 2002) sits in Chennai; State Biodiversity Boards and local BMCs complete the three-tier structure.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Which of the following is a 'Man and Biosphere' reserve in India recognised by UNESCO?
1. Nilgiri
2. Sundarbans
3. Nanda Devi
questions.e: India has 12 UNESCO MAB reserves (of 18 designated nationally) — Nilgiri (2000), Sundarbans (2001), Nanda Devi (2004) among them.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Great Nicobar' project controversy is mainly about:
o: A transhipment port and development threatening tribal reserves and biodiversity
questions.e: The ₹72,000-crore Great Nicobar project (port, airport, township) raises concerns over Galathea Bay, leatherback nesting and Shompen/Nicobarese tribal areas.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Right to Equality' jurisprudence:
1. E.P. Royappa (1974) linked equality to arbitrariness.
2. The creamy layer doctrine was introduced in Indra Sawhney (1992).
3. Jarnail Singh (2018) dealt with reservation in promotions.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Royappa ('equality vs arbitrariness'), Indra Sawhney (creamy layer, 50% cap), Jarnail Singh (promotion reservations need quantifiable data) — all correct.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'Second Administrative Reforms Commission' was chaired by:
questions.e: Second ARC (2005–09, Moily): 15 reports on ethics, e-governance, local governance, crisis management — key governance reform blueprint.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Social Justice' provisions:
1. Article 15(4) enables special provisions for SCs/STs/OBCs.
2. Article 16(4A) provides for reservation in promotions for SCs/STs.
3. The 103rd Amendment introduced EWS reservation.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: 15(4) (1st Amendment), 16(4A) (77th Amendment, promotions), 103rd (2019, EWS 10% — upheld in Janhit Abhiyan, 2022) — all correct.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'National Commission for Backward Classes' got constitutional status through the:
questions.e: 102nd Amendment (2018): Article 338B created the constitutional NCBC; the 105th (2021) restored states' OBC-list powers.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Disaster Management' in India is/are correct?
1. The DM Act was passed in 2005.
2. NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister.
3. NDRF battalions respond to disasters.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: DM Act 2005 (post-2004 tsunami): NDMA (PM chairs), SDMA (CM chairs), NDRF (16 battalions) — the three-tier structure.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's location:
1. India lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.
2. The Tropic of Cancer divides India into two nearly equal parts.
3. India's southernmost mainland point is Kanyakumari.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: India (8°4′N–37°6′N) is fully in the Northern Hemisphere; the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) bisects it; Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) is the mainland's southern tip (Indira Point is southernmost overall).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The northernmost point of India is:
questions.e: Indira Col (Siachen, Ladakh) is the northernmost; Kibithu (Arunachal) easternmost; Guhar Moti (Gujarat) westernmost; Indira Point (Nicobar) southernmost.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Himalayan ranges from north to south:
A. Karakoram — 1. Northernmost
B. Zaskar — 2. South of Karakoram
C. Pir Panjal — 3. Part of Lesser Himalaya
D. Shiwalik — 4. Southernmost foothills
questions.e: North to south: Karakoram (Trans-Himalaya), Zaskar, Pir Panjal (Lesser Himalaya), Shiwalik (outer foothills) — the standard sequence.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following Himalayan peaks is located in India?
1. Kanchenjunga
2. Nanda Devi
3. Kamet
questions.e: Kanchenjunga (Sikkim, 8,586 m — India's highest), Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand), Kamet (Uttarakhand) are all in India; Everest and K2 lie outside.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Karewas' of Kashmir are known for the cultivation of:
questions.e: Karewas (lacustrine deposits) of the Kashmir valley grow saffron (Pampore), besides almonds and apples.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Western Ghats:
1. They run parallel to India's western coast.
2. Anaimudi is the highest peak of peninsular India.
3. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Western Ghats (Sahyadris) run north–south; Anaimudi (2,695 m, Kerala) is peninsular India's highest; the Ghats were inscribed as World Heritage in 2012.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Eastern Ghats and Western Ghats meet at the:
questions.e: The two Ghat ranges converge at the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu–Kerala–Karnataka trijunction); Doddabetta is the Nilgiris' highest peak.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following passes connects Srinagar to Leh?
questions.e: Zoji La (on NH-1) links Srinagar–Leh; Banihal links Jammu–Srinagar (Chenani-Nashri tunnel); Rohtang links Manali–Leh; Nathu La is Sikkim–Tibet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following passes with their locations:
A. Nathu La — 1. Sikkim
B. Shipki La — 2. Himachal Pradesh
C. Bomdi La — 3. Arunachal Pradesh
D. Lipulekh — 4. Uttarakhand
questions.e: Nathu La (Sikkim–Tibet), Shipki La (Himachal–Tibet, Sutlej gorge), Bomdi La (Arunachal), Lipulekh (Uttarakhand–Tibet, Kailash-Manasarovar route).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Thar Desert is located primarily in:
questions.e: The Thar (Great Indian Desert) lies mainly in western Rajasthan, extending into Gujarat, Punjab and Haryana — a rain-shadow desert east of the Aravallis.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indo-Gangetic Plain:
1. The 'bhabar' is a porous piedmont zone.
2. The 'terai' is a marshy, forested zone south of the bhabar.
3. The 'khadar' is the newer alluvium of floodplains.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Bhabar (porous, streams disappear), terai (marshy re-emergence zone), bhangar (older alluvium) and khadar (newer floodplain alluvium) are the classic plain subdivisions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of the Ganga?
questions.e: Yamuna, Son and Gomti join the Ganga; Mahanadi is an independent east-flowing river of Odisha/Chhattisgarh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following rivers with their origin:
A. Ganga — 1. Amarkantak
B. Narmada — 2. Gangotri (Gomukh)
C. Godavari — 3. Nashik (Trimbakeshwar)
D. Krishna — 4. Mahabaleshwar
questions.e: Ganga (Gangotri), Narmada (Amarkantak), Godavari (Trimbakeshwar, Nashik), Krishna (Mahabaleshwar) — standard origins.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Dakshin Ganga' is another name for the river:
questions.e: The Godavari (1,465 km, longest peninsular river) is called Dakshin Ganga; it rises in Maharashtra and drains into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Brahmaputra:
1. It originates in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
2. It enters India through Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang/Dihang.
3. Majuli, one of the world's largest river islands, lies in it.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Yarlung Tsangpo (Tibet) → Siang/Dihang (Arunachal) → Brahmaputra (Assam); Majuli (Assam) is among the largest river islands.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following lakes is a freshwater lake?
1. Wular Lake
2. Dal Lake
3. Chilika Lake
questions.e: Wular and Dal (Kashmir) are freshwater; Chilika (Odisha) is a brackish lagoon — India's largest coastal lagoon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra is a:
o: Crater lake formed by meteorite impact
questions.e: Lonar (Buldhana) is a basaltic meteorite-crater lake (~35,000–50,000 years old) — one of few such hypervelocity impact craters on Earth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following lakes with their states:
A. Chilika — 1. Rajasthan
B. Sambhar — 2. Odisha
C. Vembanad — 3. Kerala
D. Loktak — 4. Manipur
questions.e: Chilika (Odisha), Sambhar (Rajasthan, salt lake), Vembanad (Kerala, longest lake), Loktak (Manipur, floating phumdis, Keibul Lamjao).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Silent Valley' National Park is located in:
questions.e: Silent Valley (Palakkad, Kerala) — a pristine tropical evergreen forest saved from a hydro project in the 1980s; part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sundarbans:
1. It is the world's largest mangrove forest.
2. It is shared between India and Bangladesh.
3. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Sundarbans (Ganga-Brahmaputra delta): largest mangrove tract, split India–Bangladesh, World Heritage (1987), home of the Royal Bengal tiger.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following states has the longest coastline in India?
questions.e: Gujarat (~1,600 km, including the Gulf of Kutch/Khambhat indentations) has the longest state coastline; Andhra Pradesh is second.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Nine Degree Channel' separates:
questions.e: Nine Degree Channel (Lakshadweep–Minicoy); Ten Degree Channel (Andaman–Nicobar); the Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Andaman and Nicobar Islands:
1. They lie in the Bay of Bengal.
2. Barren Island has India's only active volcano.
3. Saddle Peak is the highest point.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: A&N in the Bay of Bengal; Barren Island (active volcano); Saddle Peak (North Andaman, 732 m) is the highest point.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Duncan Passage' lies between:
questions.e: Duncan Passage separates South and Little Andaman; the Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman group from the Nicobar group.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct north-to-south order of the given cities along India's west coast?
questions.e: North to south: Mumbai → Mangaluru → Kochi → Thiruvananthapuram — the standard west-coast sequence.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Palghat Gap' in the Western Ghats connects:
questions.e: The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap (~30 km wide) links Coimbatore (TN) with Palakkad (Kerala); the Thal and Bhor Ghats serve Mumbai.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian agriculture:
1. India is the largest producer of pulses in the world.
2. West Bengal is the largest producer of rice in India.
3. Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of wheat and sugarcane.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: India leads in pulses; UP leads in wheat and sugarcane; West Bengal is among the top rice producers but the largest-producer rank has varied between West Bengal and UP in recent years — statement 2 is approximate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Green Revolution' in India is most associated with the states of:
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
questions.e: The 1960s Green Revolution (HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation — M.S. Swaminathan's leadership) centred on Punjab, Haryana and western UP wheat belts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following crops with their ideal climatic conditions:
A. Rice — 1. Cool climate, well-drained loamy soil
B. Wheat — 2. Hot and humid, 125+ cm rainfall
C. Cotton — 3. Warm climate, black soil, 50–100 cm rainfall
D. Tea — 4. Cool, humid, sloping well-drained land
questions.e: Rice (hot, humid), wheat (cool rabi), cotton (black regur soil, moderate rain), tea (sloped, well-drained, humid) — standard crop geography.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the 'White Revolution' is/are correct?
1. It is associated with Verghese Kurien and the Amul model.
2. Operation Flood was implemented by the NDDB.
3. India is the world's largest milk producer.
questions.e: White Revolution: Kurien's Amul cooperative model, Operation Flood (1970, NDDB); India is the largest milk producer globally.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Blue Revolution' in India is related to:
questions.e: Blue Revolution = fisheries/aquaculture growth (7th Five Year Plan onwards; Matsya Sampada Yojana, 2020); India is among the top fish producers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about mineral resources in India:
1. Jharkhand is rich in coal and iron ore.
2. Karnataka is the largest producer of gold.
3. Odisha is the largest producer of bauxite.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Jharkhand (Jharia coal, Singhbhum iron), Karnataka (Kolar/Hutti gold — largest producer), Odisha (largest bauxite producer) are all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Digboi' oil field is located in:
questions.e: Digboi (Assam) — India's oldest producing oilfield (1889) and first refinery; Naharkatiya and Mumbai High are other major fields.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Mumbai High, India's largest offshore oil field, lies in the:
questions.e: Mumbai High (discovered 1974) is in the Arabian Sea off Mumbai; operated by ONGC.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following industrial regions with their characteristics:
A. Chotanagpur — 1. Cotton textiles
B. Mumbai-Pune — 2. Heavy industry, coal-iron base
C. Ahmedabad-Vadodara — 3. Petrochemicals, textiles
D. Vishakhapatnam — 4. Port-based steel and industry
questions.e: Chotanagpur (mineral-based heavy industry), Mumbai-Pune (cotton textiles), Ahmedabad-Vadodara (textiles, petrochemicals), Vizag (port-based steel) — classic industrial regions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Indian Railways is/are correct?
1. It is among the world's largest rail networks.
2. The first train ran between Mumbai and Thane in 1853.
3. The Konkan Railway connects Mumbai and Mangaluru.
questions.e: Indian Railways (~68,000 km, among the largest); first train 16 April 1853 (Bori Bunder–Thane); Konkan Railway (1998) links Roha–Mangalore.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Golden Quadrilateral' connects:
questions.e: The Golden Quadrilateral (NHDP) links Delhi–Mumbai–Chennai–Kolkata; the North-South/East-West corridors link Srinagar–Kanyakumari and Porbandar–Silchar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the major ports of India:
1. Kandla (Deendayal Port) is a tidal port in Gujarat.
2. Paradip is a major port in Odisha.
3. Nhava Sheva (JNPT) is India's largest container port.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Kandla (tidal, Gulf of Kutch), Paradip (Odisha), and JNPT/Nhava Sheva (largest container handler) are all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following is India's largest public sector steel plant in terms of capacity (SAIL)?
questions.e: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh, with Soviet assistance, 1959) is SAIL's largest plant; Bokaro is also among the largest — Bhilai is generally cited first by capacity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Sardar Sarovar Dam' is built on the river:
questions.e: Sardar Sarovar (Gujarat) on the Narmada — the terminal dam of the Narmada valley project; the Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tehri Dam:
1. It is built on the Bhagirathi river.
2. It is one of the tallest dams in India.
3. It is located in Uttarakhand.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Tehri (260.5 m, among India's tallest) on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand — a rock-and-earth-fill dam with seismic concerns.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Indira Gandhi Canal' brings water to the Thar Desert from the river:
questions.e: The Indira Gandhi (Rajasthan) Canal carries Sutlej–Beas water from Harike Barrage (Punjab) to western Rajasthan — India's longest canal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Census of India is/are correct?
1. The first synchronous census was held in 1881.
2. The Census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.
3. The Registrar General and Census Commissioner conducts it.
questions.e: First regular census 1881 (Ripon); Census Act 1948; Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner (Home Ministry) conducts the decennial census.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: According to the 2011 Census, the most populous state and the least populous state of India are:
questions.e: 2011 Census: UP (~199.8 million, most populous), Sikkim (~610,000, least populous state).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The state with the highest population density in India (2011 Census) is:
questions.e: Bihar (~1,106 persons/sq km) is the densest state (2011); among UTs, Delhi is densest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Demographic Dividend' of India:
1. Over 60% of India's population is in the working-age group.
2. India has one of the world's youngest populations.
3. The dividend is automatic and requires no policy support.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: India's working-age share (~62%+) and young median age (~28) create the dividend — but it needs education, health and jobs; it is not automatic.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'tribal' population of India is concentrated most in which of the following states (largest absolute ST population, 2011)?
questions.e: Madhya Pradesh has the largest Scheduled Tribe population (~15.3 million, 2011); Maharashtra is second.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following languages has the largest number of speakers in India (2011 Census)?
questions.e: Hindi (~43.6% including mother-tongue variants) is first; Bengali second (~8%), Marathi third.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
The 'Standard Meridian of India' (82°30′E) passes through which of the following states?
1. Uttar Pradesh
2. Madhya Pradesh
3. Chhattisgarh
4. Odisha
questions.e: 82°30′E passes through UP, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh — so all four listed states.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Indian Geography — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Coal' reserves of India:
1. Gondwana coalfields hold most of India's coal.
2. Jharia is famous for coking coal.
3. Neyveli is famous for lignite.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Gondwana fields (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro) hold ~99% of reserves; Jharia gives prime coking coal; Neyveli (Tamil Nadu) is the lignite hub.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations:
1. It was founded in 1945 after World War II.
2. India is a founding member.
3. The UN Charter was signed at San Francisco.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: UN (24 Oct 1945, San Francisco Charter); India, though not yet independent, signed as a founding member.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The permanent members of the UN Security Council with veto power are:
questions.e: The P5 (US, UK, France, Russia, China) hold the veto; India (G4 with Germany, Japan, Brazil) seeks permanent membership.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: India's 'Act East Policy' was launched in 2014 as an upgrade of the:
questions.e: Act East (2014) upgraded Rao's Look East (1991) — deeper engagement with ASEAN and the Indo-Pacific.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Quadrilateral Security Dialogue' (Quad) comprises:
questions.e: Quad (revived 2017): India, US, Japan, Australia — Indo-Pacific cooperation on security, tech and supply chains.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about BRICS:
1. The 2024 expansion added Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and UAE.
2. The New Development Bank is headquartered in Shanghai.
3. India hosted the BRICS summit in 2021.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: BRICS expanded (2024: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE; Indonesia joined 2025); NDB (Shanghai, 2014); India chaired the 2021 virtual summit.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'International Solar Alliance' headquarters is located at:
questions.e: ISA HQ at Gurugram (National Institute of Solar Energy campus) — launched by India and France at COP-21 (2015).

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: India's 'Neighbourhood First' policy prioritises:
questions.e: Neighbourhood First (2014): priority to South Asia — connectivity, development partnership and disaster aid (e.g., Vaccine Maitri).

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Gujral Doctrine' in Indian foreign policy emphasises:
o: Generosity towards smaller neighbours without expecting reciprocity
questions.e: I.K. Gujral's doctrine (1996): India gives to neighbours (Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, Sri Lanka) without demanding reciprocity.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Shanghai Cooperation Organisation':
1. India became a full member in 2017.
2. It is headquartered in Beijing.
3. It focuses on regional security and counter-terrorism.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: SCO (2001, Beijing): India and Pakistan joined in 2017 (Astana); RATS (Tashkent) handles counter-terrorism; India chaired in 2023.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Indo-Pacific Economic Framework' (IPEF) was launched in 2022 by:
o: The USA with 13 Indo-Pacific partners including India
questions.e: IPEF (May 2022, Tokyo): US-led 14-member framework on supply chains, clean economy and trade — India opted out of the trade pillar.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the 'WTO' is/are correct?
1. It was established in 1995, succeeding GATT.
2. It is headquartered in Geneva.
3. India is a founding member.
questions.e: WTO (Marrakesh, 1995; Geneva HQ): India is a founding member; its dispute-settlement Appellate Body has been non-functional since 2019.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Panchsheel' agreement (1954) was signed between India and:
questions.e: Panchsheel (1954, Nehru–Zhou Enlai): five principles of peaceful coexistence — later violated by the 1962 war.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Non-Aligned Movement':
1. The first NAM summit was held at Belgrade in 1961.
2. India was a founding member.
3. It was a response to Cold War bloc politics.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NAM (Belgrade 1961; Nehru, Nasser, Tito, Sukarno, Nkrumah): non-alignment in the Cold War — India remains a member though its salience faded.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation' (1971) was signed between India and:
questions.e: The Indo-Soviet Treaty (August 1971) preceded the Bangladesh war — Article 9 provided for consultations in case of attack.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: India's 'Look West' / 'Think West' policy primarily concerns:
questions.e: 'Link West' (Modi era): energy, diaspora (9 million Indians) and defence ties with the Gulf — IMEC corridor (2023) extends it.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'IMEC' (India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor) was announced at the:
questions.e: IMEC (Sept 2023, G20 Delhi): India–UAE–Saudi–Europe connectivity (ports, rail, green hydrogen) — a counterpoint to BRI.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Belt and Road Initiative':
1. It is China's transcontinental infrastructure programme.
2. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor passes through PoK.
3. India has opposed BRI over sovereignty concerns.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: BRI (2013): CPEC traverses Gilgit-Baltistan (PoK); India boycotts BRI forums citing sovereignty and debt-trap concerns.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Arctic Council' observer status of India was granted in:
questions.e: India became an Arctic Council observer in 2013 (Kiruna); Himadri station (Ny-Ålesund) supports its polar research; India's Arctic Policy released 2022.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'SAARC' is/are correct?
1. It was founded in 1985 at Dhaka.
2. It has 8 member states including Afghanistan.
3. Its secretariat is at Kathmandu.
questions.e: SAARC (1985, Dhaka; 8 members with Afghanistan 2007; Kathmandu secretariat) — moribund since the 2016 summit's cancellation; BIMSTEC is India's alternative focus.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.topic: International Relations — Prelims Question Bank (20 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'BIMSTEC' grouping connects South and Southeast Asia. Its secretariat is at:
questions.e: BIMSTEC (1997, Dhaka secretariat): 7 members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand) — Bay of Bengal cooperation.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi Sultanate's administration:
1. The iqta system assigned revenue of territories to nobles in lieu of salary.
2. Alauddin Khalji introduced the branding of horses (dagh) and descriptive rolls (chehra).
3. Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Iqta (Iltutmish systematised it), Alauddin's dagh-chehra military reforms, and Tughlaq's Daulatabad transfer (1327) are all established Sultanate features.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Sultanate rulers with their associated measures:
A. Alauddin Khalji — 1. Token currency
B. Muhammad bin Tughlaq — 2. Market control regulations
C. Firoz Shah Tughlaq — 3. Translation of Sanskrit works; founded cities
D. Iltutmish — 4. Silver tanka and copper jital
questions.e: Alauddin (market control), Muhammad Tughlaq (token currency), Firoz (translations, cities like Jaunpur/Hisar), Iltutmish (tanka-jital coinage).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Chahalgani' (Corps of Forty) was a group of Turkish nobles created by:
questions.e: Iltutmish organised the Chahalgani; Balban later destroyed it to assert despotic kingship.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Razia Sultana, the only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.e: Razia (r. 1236–40) was Iltutmish's daughter of the Mamluk/Slave dynasty; the nobles deposed her for favouring the Abyssinian Yakut.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bhakti saints:
1. Ramanuja propounded Vishishtadvaita.
2. Kabir's verses are included in the Adi Granth.
3. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu popularised Krishna bhakti in Bengal.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita, 11th–12th c.), Kabir (verses in Guru Granth Sahib), and Chaitanya (Gaudiya Vaishnavism, sankirtan) are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Bhakti philosophers with their doctrines:
A. Shankaracharya — 1. Dvaita
B. Ramanuja — 2. Advaita
C. Madhvacharya — 3. Vishishtadvaita
D. Vallabhacharya — 4. Shuddhadvaita
questions.e: Shankara (Advaita/Kevaladvaita), Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita), Madhva (Dvaita), Vallabha (Shuddhadvaita/Pushtimarga).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The Sufi silsila most associated with the doctrine of Wahdat-al-Wujud (unity of being) in India and with Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya is the:
questions.e: The Chishti order (Muinuddin Chishti, Nizamuddin Auliya, Nasiruddin Chiragh) emphasised love, tolerance and Wahdat-al-Wujud; it kept distance from the state.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Vijayanagara Empire is/are correct?
1. It was founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336.
2. Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.
3. The Battle of Talikota (1565) led to its decline.
questions.e: Vijayanagara (1336, Sangama brothers), Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva, 1509–29, author of Amuktamalyada), and Talikota (1565, confederacy of Deccan sultanates) are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The famous Hazara Rama temple and the Vittala temple are located at:
questions.e: Hampi (Vijayanagara capital) hosts the Hazara Rama and Vittala temples; the stone chariot at Vittala is iconic.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bahmani kingdom:
1. It was founded by Alauddin Bahman Shah in 1347.
2. Its capital was initially Gulbarga, later Bidar.
3. Mahmud Gawan was its famous wazir.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Bahmani kingdom (1347, Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah), capitals Gulbarga then Bidar (1429), and Mahmud Gawan's reforms (madrasa at Bidar) are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Ashtadiggajas' were the eight celebrated Telugu poets in the court of:
questions.e: Krishnadevaraya's court hosted the Ashtadiggajas including Allasani Peddana (author of Manucharitram); the king himself wrote Amuktamalyada.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Which Mughal emperor built the city of Fatehpur Sikri?
questions.e: Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri (1571) honouring Sheikh Salim Chishti; the Buland Darwaza commemorates his Gujarat conquest.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Mughal rulers with their tombs' locations:
A. Babur — 1. Sikandra (Agra)
B. Humayun — 2. Kabul
C. Akbar — 3. Delhi
D. Aurangzeb — 4. Khuldabad (Maharashtra)
questions.e: Babur (Kabul, Bagh-e Babur), Humayun (Delhi), Akbar (Sikandra), Aurangzeb (Khuldabad, Aurangabad) — unmarked simple grave.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's administration:
1. He introduced the mansabdari system.
2. Todar Mal's zabti system was a land revenue settlement.
3. He abolished the jizya in 1564.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Akbar's mansabdari (1571), Todar Mal's zabti/dahsala revenue system, and jizya abolition (1564; pilgrim tax 1563) are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Din-i Ilahi' promulgated by Akbar was primarily a:
o: Syncretic order (Tauhid-i-Ilahi) blending elements of various faiths
questions.e: Din-i Ilahi (1582) was an eclectic spiritual order around Akbar, not a mass religion; it had few adherents (notably Birbal).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Shah Jahan's reign is/are correct?
1. The Peacock Throne was commissioned during his reign.
2. The Taj Mahal was built as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal.
3. He shifted the Mughal capital from Agra to Delhi (Shahjahanabad).
questions.e: Shah Jahan: Peacock Throne (1635), Taj Mahal (1632–53), and the new capital Shahjahanabad with Red Fort and Jama Masjid — the peak of Mughal architecture.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in the year:
questions.e: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679 (Akbar had abolished it in 1564); 1669 saw the ban on new temple construction orders.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Zabt' system of land revenue under the Mughals was based on:
o: A fixed share of actual produce each year
Revenue farming to the highest bidder
Measurement of land and assessment on average produce of past ten years
questions.e: Zabti (Todar Mal's dahsala): measured land, classified soils, and fixed demand at one-third of the average produce of the last ten years, payable in cash.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Shivaji:
1. He was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674.
2. He established the Ashtapradhan council of eight ministers.
3. His revenue system included chauth and sardeshmukhi levies.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Shivaji's coronation (1674, Raigad), Ashtapradhan (Peshwa, Amatya etc.), and chauth (1/4) + sardeshmukhi (1/10) levies are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between:
o: The Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali
questions.e: Panipat III (14 January 1761): Ahmad Shah Abdali's Afghan coalition defeated the Marathas under Sadashivrao Bhau — halting Maratha northern expansion.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following Sikh Gurus compiled the Adi Granth?
questions.e: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth (1604, installed at Harmandir Sahib); Guru Gobind Singh added Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns, finalising the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The Khalsa was founded by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699 at:
questions.e: The Khalsa was created on Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur Sahib with the Panj Pyare; the Guru Granth Sahib was declared the eternal Guru at Nanded (1708).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bhakti movement:
1. The Alvars were Vaishnavite saints of Tamil Nadu.
2. The Nayanars were Shaivite saints.
3. Basavanna led the Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement in Karnataka.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Alvars (Vaishnava, Divya Prabandham), Nayanars (Shaiva, Tevaram), and Basavanna's 12th-century Virashaiva movement (Anubhava Mantapa) are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The Qutb Minar was begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by:
questions.e: Aibak began the Qutb Minar (c. 1199); Iltutmish completed it; Firoz Shah Tughlaq later repaired its damaged storeys.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Which Sultan of Delhi is known as the 'Prince of Moneyers' for his extensive coinage reforms?
questions.e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token (bronze/copper) currency experiment (1329–30) earned him the title 'Prince of Moneyers'; Sher Shah issued the rupiya.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Sher Shah Suri's administration is noted for:
1. The introduction of the rupiya silver coin
2. The Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam)
3. A systematic land revenue system based on measurement
questions.e: Sher Shah (1540–45): rupiya coin, Grand Trunk Road from Sonargaon to the Indus, and zabt-based revenue (later adapted by Akbar).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Ibadat Khana' built by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri was meant for:
o: Religious discussions with scholars of various faiths
questions.e: The Ibadat Khana (1575) hosted interfaith debates (ulama, Jesuits, Jains, Parsis, Hindus) that shaped Akbar's sulh-i-kul outlook.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal mansabdari system:
1. 'Zat' indicated personal rank and 'sawar' the cavalry contingent.
2. Mansabdars were paid in cash or through jagirs.
3. The system was hereditary.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Zat (personal status/salary) and sawar (horsemen maintained) defined a mansabdar; payment was cash or jagir (non-hereditary — jagirs were transferable and lapsed at death).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The famous Persian chronicle 'Akbarnama' was written by:
questions.e: Abul Fazl's Akbarnama (with the Ain-i Akbari as its third volume) is the official history of Akbar's reign; Gulbadan wrote Humayunnama.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following monuments was built by the Tughlaqs?
questions.e: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq built Tughlaqabad (1321); Alai Darwaza is Khalji, Humayun's Tomb early Mughal, Buland Darwaza Akbar's.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Rana Sanga' who fought Babur at the Battle of Khanwa (1527) was the ruler of:
questions.e: Rana Sanga of Mewar led the Rajput confederacy at Khanwa (1527); Babur's victory consolidated Mughal rule after Panipat (1526).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Maratha Confederacy in the 18th century:
1. The Peshwa became the de facto ruler after Shahu.
2. The Maratha sardars (Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad, Bhonsle) controlled different regions.
3. The Marathas collected chauth from Mughal territories.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Post-Shahu (d. 1749), Peshwa dominance; the confederacy's great sardar houses; and chauth/sardeshmukhi exactions across Mughal lands are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Treaty of Purandar' (1665) was signed between Shivaji and:
o: Jai Singh I (on behalf of Aurangzeb)
questions.e: Jai Singh I forced Shivaji to sign Purandar (1665) — ceding 23 forts; Shivaji's 1666 Agra visit and escape followed.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Amir Khusrau is/are correct?
1. He was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.
2. He is credited with the invention of the sitar and tabla.
3. He wrote the 'Khazain-ul-Futuh' on Alauddin Khalji's conquests.
questions.e: Khusrau (1253–1325), 'Tuti-i-Hind', was Nizamuddin's murid and wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh; the sitar/tabla attribution is traditional but historically debated, so statement 2 is marked uncertain.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The Golconda fort and the Charminar are associated with which dynasty?
questions.e: The Qutb Shahis of Golconda (1518–1687); Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built Hyderabad and the Charminar (1591).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chola temples:
1. They represent the Dravida style of temple architecture.
2. The vimana is the towering spire over the sanctum.
3. Bronze Nataraja images are a Chola hallmark.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Chola temples are Dravida style (vimana, gopuram, mandapa); the Brihadeshwara's vimana rises 66 m; Chola bronze Natarajas are world-famous.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Kitab-ul-Hind' (Tahqiq-i-Hind), an account of India, was written by:
questions.e: Al-Biruni (accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni) wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind (c. 1030) on Indian religion, philosophy and sciences.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, visited India during the reign of:
questions.e: Ibn Battuta (1333–42) served as qazi under Muhammad bin Tughlaq and left the Rihla account of the Sultanate.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct chronological order of the Delhi Sultanate dynasties?
questions.e: Mamluk/Slave (1206) → Khalji (1290) → Tughlaq (1320) → Sayyid (1414) → Lodi (1451–1526).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Medieval History — Prelims Question Bank (40 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Nur Jahan' junta during Jahangir's reign is significant because:
o: She issued coins and farmans in her own name, wielding de facto power
She led the Mughal army at Kandahar
questions.e: Nur Jahan (married 1611) issued coins jointly with Jahangir and ran the administration with her father Itimad-ud-Daula and brother Asaf Khan during Jahangir's decline.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Plassey (1757):
1. It was fought between the British East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah.
2. Mir Jafar's defection was decisive for the British victory.
3. It established British political supremacy in Bengal.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Plassey (23 June 1757): Clive vs Siraj-ud-Daulah; Mir Jafar, Rai Durlabh and Jagat Seth conspired; it made the Company the kingmaker in Bengal.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was significant because it:
o: Led to the annexation of Awadh
Gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa via the Treaty of Allahabad
questions.e: Buxar (1764): Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II; the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad granted the Diwani.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following Governor-Generals with their associated events:
A. Warren Hastings — 1. Abolition of Sati
B. William Bentinck — 2. First Anglo-Maratha War
C. Dalhousie — 3. Doctrine of Lapse
D. Cornwallis — 4. Permanent Settlement
questions.e: Hastings (First Anglo-Maratha War, 1775–82), Bentinck (Sati abolition 1829), Dalhousie (Doctrine of Lapse, annexations), Cornwallis (Permanent Settlement 1793).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was used to annex which of the following states?
1. Satara
2. Jhansi
3. Nagpur
4. Awadh
questions.e: Dalhousie annexed Satara (1848), Jhansi (1854) and Nagpur (1854) under the Doctrine of Lapse; Awadh was annexed (1856) on grounds of misgovernance.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Permanent Settlement (1793):
1. It was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
2. Zamindars were recognised as proprietors of land.
3. The revenue demand was fixed permanently.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Cornwallis's 1793 settlement made zamindars landowners with a fixed, permanent revenue demand — creating absentee landlordism and peasant distress.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Ryotwari system of land revenue was pioneered by:
o: Holt Mackenzie in the North-Western Provinces
questions.e: Munro's Ryotwari (1820s, Madras) settled revenue directly with the ryot; Mackenzie devised the Mahalwari system in the NW Provinces.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Revolt of 1857 is/are correct?
1. It began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
2. Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed the symbolic leader.
3. The revolt failed due to lack of central organisation and modern arms.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The sepoys mutinied at Meerut (10 May 1857), marched to Delhi, proclaimed the Mughal emperor; disunity, limited spread and British resources doomed it.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following leaders of the 1857 Revolt with their centres:
A. Rani Lakshmibai — 1. Kanpur
B. Nana Saheb — 2. Jhansi
C. Kunwar Singh — 3. Lucknow
D. Begum Hazrat Mahal — 4. Arrah (Bihar)
questions.e: Jhansi (Lakshmibai), Kanpur (Nana Saheb/Tantia Tope), Arrah (Kunwar Singh, aged 80), Lucknow (Begum Hazrat Mahal).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The British Crown assumed direct control of India through:
questions.e: The 1858 Act ended Company rule after the Revolt, creating the Secretary of State for India and the Viceroy (Canning, the first).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian National Congress's founding:
1. It was founded in 1885 at Bombay.
2. A.O. Hume played a key role in its formation.
3. W.C. Bonnerjee was its first president.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: INC founded December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay; Hume was the guiding spirit; W.C. Bonnerjee presided (72 delegates).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Safety Valve' theory regarding the formation of the Congress is associated with:
questions.e: The safety-valve thesis (Hume founded Congress to vent Indian discontent) was popularised by Wedderburn's biography of Hume; later historians debate it.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Drain Theory' was expounded in his book:
o: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
questions.e: Naoroji's 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) quantified the drain of wealth to Britain.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Partition of Bengal (1905) was annulled in the year:
questions.e: Curzon's 1905 partition was revoked at the 1911 Delhi Durbar (George V), with the capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Swadeshi Movement:
1. It was launched in response to the Partition of Bengal.
2. It promoted boycott of foreign goods and national education.
3. The Surat Split (1907) weakened the movement.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Swadeshi (1905): anti-partition agitation, boycott, national schools (e.g., Bengal National College); the 1907 Surat split divided Moderates and Extremists.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Surat Split of 1907 divided the Congress into Moderates and Extremists over the issue of:
o: The pace and methods of the anti-partition agitation
questions.e: At Surat (1907), Moderates (Gokhale, Mehta) and Extremists (Tilak, Lajpat Rai, Bipin Pal) split over extending boycott beyond Bengal and the presidency question.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Lucknow Pact (1916) is significant because it:
o: Created separate electorates for the first time
Brought the Congress and Muslim League together on constitutional reforms
Accepted complete independence as the goal
questions.e: The 1916 Lucknow Pact united Congress and League (and reunited Moderates–Extremists) with joint reform demands; the League accepted Congress's scheme.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Home Rule Movement was launched by:
o: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant
questions.e: Tilak (April 1916, Poona) and Besant (September 1916, Madras) ran parallel Home Rule Leagues demanding self-government within the Empire.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Jallianwala Bagh massacre:
1. It occurred on 13 April 1919 at Amritsar.
2. General Dyer ordered firing on an unarmed gathering.
3. The Hunter Committee condemned Dyer's action.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Jallianwala Bagh (Baisakhi, 13 April 1919): Dyer's troops killed hundreds; the Hunter Committee (majority) criticised Dyer but the House of Lords and Morning Post praised him — statement 3 overstates a unanimous condemnation.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn by Gandhi after:
questions.e: After Chauri Chaura (5 February 1922), where a mob killed 22 policemen, Gandhi suspended Non-Cooperation — a decision criticised by many Congressmen.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted because:
o: It was headed by a Conservative
questions.e: The all-white Simon Commission (7 British MPs) to review the 1919 Act was boycotted; Lala Lajpat Rai died after a lathi charge during protests.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Nehru Report (1928) demanded:
questions.e: Motilal Nehru's committee report (1928) asked for dominion status with joint electorates; Jinnah's 14 points responded to it.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: At the Lahore session of the Congress (1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the resolution of 'Purna Swaraj' was adopted, and the first Independence Day was observed on:
questions.e: Lahore (December 1929): Purna Swaraj resolution; 26 January 1930 observed as Independence Day — later chosen as Republic Day.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Dandi March (1930) was undertaken to protest the:
questions.e: Gandhi's 240-mile march (12 March–6 April 1930) from Sabarmati to Dandi broke the salt law, launching Civil Disobedience.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) is also known as the:
questions.e: The Delhi Pact (5 March 1931): Civil Disobedience suspended; Congress to attend the Second Round Table Conference; political prisoners released (not Bhagat Singh).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar on the issue of:
questions.e: After Gandhi's fast against the Communal Award's separate electorates, the Poona Pact gave reserved seats with joint electorates for depressed classes.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. It provided for an All-India Federation.
2. It introduced provincial autonomy.
3. It abolished dyarchy at the provinces but retained it at the Centre.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The 1935 Act: proposed federation (never formed — princes stayed out), provincial autonomy (Congress ministries 1937), and dyarchy shifted to the Centre.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'August Offer' (1940) was made by:
questions.e: Linlithgow's August Offer (1940): dominion status as the goal, expansion of the Viceroy's council — rejected by Congress and League.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Cripps Mission (1942) proposed:
o: A constituent assembly with universal franchise
Dominion status after the war with a constitution-making body
questions.e: Cripps offered post-war dominion status and a constitution-making body; Gandhi called it 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched on:
questions.e: The AICC adopted the Quit India resolution on 8 August 1942 at Gowalia Tank, Bombay ('Do or Die'); leaders were arrested on 9 August.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) was first conceived by:
questions.e: Mohan Singh raised the first INA from POWs in 1942; Rash Behari Bose handed leadership to Subhas Bose in 1943 (Singapore).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The INA trials at the Red Fort (1945–46) involved which three officers?
o: Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
Mohan Singh, Lakshmi Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan
Prem Sahgal, Dhillon, Rash Behari Bose
Gurbaksh Dhillon, Mohan Singh, Lakshmi Sehgal
questions.e: The famous first INA trial: Major General Shah Nawaz Khan, Colonel Prem Sahgal, Colonel Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon — defended by Bhulabhai Desai.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) proposed:
o: A united India with a weak Centre and provincial grouping
Dominion status without a constituent assembly
questions.e: The Cabinet Mission's May 1946 plan: a three-tier federation with grouping of provinces (A, B, C) — accepted by Congress and League initially, then wrecked over grouping.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) is also known as:
questions.e: Mountbatten's 3 June Plan provided for partition with referendums/assemblies deciding — enacted as the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: India's Constituent Assembly adopted the national flag on:
