questions.e: The tricolour (saffron-white-green with the navy-blue Ashoka Chakra) was adopted 22 July 1947; Jana Gana Mana and Vande Mataram on 24 January 1950.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the socio-religious reform movements:
1. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828.
2. Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875.
3. Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Brahmo Samaj (1828, Roy), Arya Samaj (1875, Dayananda — 'Back to the Vedas'), Ramakrishna Mission (1897, Vivekananda) are all correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 for:
o: The uplift of lower castes and women in Maharashtra
questions.e: Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj fought caste oppression; with Savitribai he opened schools for girls and lower castes (1848).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Theosophical Society's headquarters in India was established at Adyar (Madras) by:
questions.e: Blavatsky and Olcott founded the Theosophical Society (New York, 1875) and moved its headquarters to Adyar in 1882; Besant joined later (1889).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Deccan Riots (1875) is/are correct?
1. They were directed against moneylenders.
2. They led to the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879.
3. They began in Supa village of Poona district.
questions.e: The 1875 Deccan uprising targeted Marwari/Gujarati sahukars; it began at Supa (Poona) and prompted the 1879 Relief Act.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Indigo Revolt (1859–60) in Bengal was led by:
questions.e: The Biswas brothers of Nadia led the raiyats' refusal to sow indigo; Harish Chandra Mukherjee's Hindoo Patriot publicised it; Dinabandhu Mitra wrote Nil Darpan.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: Birsa Munda's Ulgulan (1899–1900) was a tribal uprising in the region of:
questions.e: Birsa's Munda rebellion centred on Chotanagpur (Ranchi); the Santhal Rebellion (1855–56, Sidu-Kanhu) was in the Rajmahal hills.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Pabna Agrarian League' (1873) was formed to:
o: Resist enhanced rents by zamindars in East Bengal
questions.e: Pabna raiyats organised against zamindari oppression; the movement fed into the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rowlatt Act (1919):
1. It allowed detention without trial for up to two years.
2. Gandhi launched a nationwide satyagraha against it.
3. It was officially called the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The Rowlatt Act (based on the Sedition Committee) permitted detention without trial; Gandhi's April 1919 satyagraha was his first all-India agitation.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Khilafat Movement' was launched to protest:
o: The dismemberment of the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I
questions.e: Ali brothers' Khilafat movement (1919) defended the Caliph; Gandhi yoked it to Non-Cooperation for Hindu-Muslim unity.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following was the first newspaper published in India?
questions.e: James Augustus Hicky's Bengal Gazette (1780, Calcutta) was India's first newspaper; Samachar Darpan (1818) was the first Bengali paper.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) was repealed by:
questions.e: Lytton's 1878 'gagging Act' targeted the vernacular press; Ripon repealed it in 1882.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms):
1. It introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
2. It increased the size of legislative councils.
3. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The 1909 Act gave separate electorates and enlarged councils; dyarchy came only with the 1919 Act (Montagu-Chelmsford).

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) introduced:
questions.e: The 1919 Act's dyarchy split provincial subjects into reserved and transferred; separate electorates were extended to Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Round Table Conferences is/are correct?
1. Three sessions were held in London (1930–32).
2. Gandhi attended only the Second session.
3. B.R. Ambedkar attended all three sessions.
questions.e: Three RTCs (1930, 1931, 1932); Gandhi attended only the second (1931) after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact; Ambedkar attended all three, clashing with Gandhi over separate electorates.

questions.subject: History
questions.topic: Modern History — Prelims Question Bank (49 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Communal Award' (1932) was announced by:
questions.e: MacDonald's Communal Award (August 1932) extended separate electorates to depressed classes — triggering Gandhi's Yeravada fast and the Poona Pact.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Earth's interior:
1. The Mohorovicic discontinuity separates the crust from the mantle.
2. The Gutenberg discontinuity separates the mantle from the core.
3. The inner core is solid while the outer core is liquid.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Moho (crust–mantle), Gutenberg (mantle–core at ~2900 km), and a solid inner/liquid outer core are the standard seismic discontinuities.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Ring of Fire' is associated with:
questions.e: The circum-Pacific belt hosts ~75% of the world's active volcanoes and ~90% of earthquakes due to convergent plate margins.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following types of volcanoes with their characteristics:
A. Shield volcano — 1. Explosive, steep-sided
B. Stratovolcano — 2. Broad, gentle slopes of basaltic lava
C. Cinder cone — 3. Small, steep piles of volcanic debris
questions.e: Shield (Mauna Loa — fluid basalt), stratovolcano/composite (Fujiyama — alternating layers), cinder cone (small, fragmental).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about plate tectonics is/are correct?
1. The Himalayas were formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates.
2. The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a divergent plate boundary.
3. The San Andreas Fault is a transform boundary.
questions.e: Himalayas (continent–continent convergence), Mid-Atlantic Ridge (seafloor spreading/divergence), San Andreas (transform/strike-slip) are textbook examples.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The deepest known point in the world's oceans, the Challenger Deep, is located in the:
questions.e: Challenger Deep (~10,900 m) in the Mariana Trench (western Pacific) is the ocean's deepest point; Java Trench is the Indian Ocean's deepest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ocean currents:
1. The Gulf Stream is a warm current in the North Atlantic.
2. The Humboldt (Peru) Current is a cold current along South America's west coast.
3. The Agulhas Current flows along Africa's southeast coast.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Gulf Stream (warm, North Atlantic), Humboldt/Peru (cold, upwelling, anchovy fisheries), Agulhas (warm, SE Africa) are all correctly described.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: El Niño is characterised by:
o: Warming of the eastern Pacific off Peru, weakening trade winds
Cooling of the western Pacific near Indonesia
questions.e: El Niño: anomalous warming of the eastern equatorial Pacific, weakened trades and Walker cell — often linked to weak Indian monsoons.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the layers of the atmosphere is/are correct?
1. Temperature decreases with height in the troposphere.
2. The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere.
3. Meteors burn up in the mesosphere.
questions.e: Troposphere (lapse rate ~6.5°C/km), stratospheric ozone (15–35 km), mesosphere (meteor burn-up, coldest layer) are all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'jet streams' are:
o: Winds blowing from the poles to the equator
Ocean currents in the Southern Ocean
Seasonal winds of the Indian Ocean
Fast-flowing narrow air currents in the upper troposphere
questions.e: Jet streams are narrow, high-speed winds (100–400 km/h) near the tropopause; the subtropical jet influences India's winter weather and monsoon onset.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tropical cyclones:
1. They form over warm ocean waters above 27°C.
2. They rotate anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.
3. The eye is a region of calm at the centre.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Warm SSTs (>27°C), Coriolis-driven anticlockwise rotation (NH), and a calm eye are the defining features of tropical cyclones.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following regional names of tropical cyclones:
A. Typhoon — 1. North Indian Ocean
B. Cyclone — 2. Northwest Pacific
C. Hurricane — 3. North Atlantic and Northeast Pacific
questions.e: Typhoons (NW Pacific), cyclones (North Indian Ocean/South Pacific), hurricanes (Atlantic/NE Pacific) — same phenomenon, different names.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone' (ITCZ) is:
o: The boundary between the troposphere and stratosphere
A low-pressure belt near the equator where trade winds converge
questions.e: The ITCZ (doldrums) is the equatorial low-pressure convergence zone; its northward shift brings the Indian monsoon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Indian monsoon is/are correct?
1. The southwest monsoon is driven by the differential heating of land and sea.
2. The Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats first.
3. The monsoon trough and Tibetan High influence its strength.
questions.e: The monsoon is a thermal circulation; the Arabian Sea branch hits Kerala/Western Ghats in early June; the monsoon trough and Tibetan anticyclone modulate it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
The retreating monsoon in India is associated with:
1. The southwest monsoon withdrawing from north to south
2. Heavy rainfall on the Coromandel coast
3. Cyclonic activity in the Bay of Bengal
questions.e: Retreat (Oct–Dec): withdrawal from NW India, northeast monsoon rains on the Tamil Nadu coast, and Bay cyclones.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Western Disturbances:
1. They are extratropical storms originating in the Mediterranean region.
2. They bring winter rainfall to northwest India.
3. They are important for rabi crops.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Western disturbances ride the subtropical westerly jet from the Mediterranean, giving winter rain/snow to NW India — vital for rabi wheat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'loo' experienced in North India during summer is a:
questions.e: The loo is a hot, dry afternoon wind of the Indo-Gangetic plain in May–June; nor'westers (Kalbaisakhi) are the pre-monsoon thunderstorms of Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following soils of India with their characteristics:
A. Alluvial — 1. Rich in potash, deposited by rivers
B. Black (regur) — 2. Rich in iron, formed from basalt
C. Red — 3. Deficient in nitrogen, formed from crystalline rocks
D. Laterite — 4. Leached, found in high-rainfall areas
questions.e: Alluvial (riverine, potash-rich), black/regur (Deccan basalt, cotton soil), red (crystalline rocks, iron oxides), laterite (leached in heavy rainfall).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The Deccan Traps were formed by:
o: Volcanic fissure eruptions at the end of the Cretaceous
questions.e: The Deccan Traps (~66 million years ago) are flood basalts from fissure eruptions — linked to the Reunion hotspot and the K–Pg extinction debate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Himalayan rivers is/are correct?
1. The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra are antecedent rivers.
2. They form deep gorges in the Himalayas.
3. They are perennial, fed by glaciers and rainfall.
questions.e: The three great Himalayan rivers predate the uplift (antecedent), cut gorges, and flow year-round from snowmelt and rain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'dendritic' drainage pattern is characteristic of:
questions.e: Dendritic (tree-like) drainage develops on homogeneous rocks; trellis on folded terrain, radial on domes/volcanoes, rectangular on faulted joints.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
questions.e: Narmada (and Tapi) flow west through rift valleys between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges — unusual for peninsular rivers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about coral reefs:
1. They require warm, shallow, clear tropical waters.
2. The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system.
3. Coral bleaching is caused by expulsion of zooxanthellae due to stress.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Corals need warm (>20°C), shallow, sunlit waters; the Great Barrier Reef is the largest system; bleaching is the loss of symbiotic zooxanthellae under heat stress.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'continental shelf' is best described as:
o: The gently sloping submerged edge of a continent
questions.e: The shelf (average ~80 km wide, <200 m deep) holds most marine life and resources; beyond it lie the slope, rise and abyssal plain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of the planets from the Sun?
o: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus
Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Earth, Venus, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune
questions.e: The order is Mercury–Venus–Earth–Mars (terrestrial) then Jupiter–Saturn–Uranus–Neptune (jovian giants).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Moon:
1. It has no atmosphere.
2. Its gravitational pull causes tides on Earth.
3. The same side always faces the Earth.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The Moon's negligible atmosphere, tidal influence (with the Sun), and synchronous rotation (tidal locking) are all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: A solar eclipse occurs when:
o: The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
The Moon is farthest from the Earth
questions.e: Solar eclipse (new moon alignment); lunar eclipse is Earth's shadow on the Moon (full moon).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Goldilocks zone' around a star refers to:
o: The outer edge of a galaxy
The habitable zone where liquid water can exist
questions.e: The circumstellar habitable zone — not too hot, not too cold — where liquid water (and potentially life) can exist.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about latitudes and longitudes is/are correct?
1. The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich, London.
2. India Standard Time is based on 82.5°E longitude.
3. The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states.
questions.e: Prime Meridian (0°) at Greenwich; IST = 82.5°E (Mirzapur, UP); Tropic of Cancer crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram — 8 states.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The International Date Line is:
o: An imaginary line at roughly 180° longitude where the calendar date changes
A time zone boundary in Europe
questions.e: The IDL (zigzagging around 180° to avoid splitting island nations) separates calendar days; crossing westward you gain a day.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about earthquakes:
1. The focus is the point of origin below the surface.
2. The epicentre is the point on the surface above the focus.
3. P-waves travel faster than S-waves.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Focus (hypocentre), epicentre, and P-waves (primary, faster, through solids/liquids) vs S-waves (secondary, shear, solids only) are all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The Richter scale measures:
questions.e: Richter (now moment magnitude) measures energy released (magnitude); the Mercalli scale measures observed intensity/damage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following landforms is formed by glacial erosion?
questions.e: Cirque (armchair-shaped hollow) is erosional; moraines, drumlins and outwash plains are depositional glacial features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Barchan' is a:
questions.e: Barchans are crescentic dunes with horns pointing downwind, common in deserts like the Thar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tundra biome:
1. It has permafrost and a short growing season.
2. Vegetation is mainly mosses, lichens and dwarf shrubs.
3. It is found in high latitudes and high altitudes.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Tundra (Arctic and alpine): permafrost, treeless, cryptogam-dominated vegetation, brief summers — all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Mediterranean climate' is characterised by:
questions.e: Mediterranean (westerlies in winter, subtropical high in summer): winter rain, summer drought — ideal for citrus, olives and viticulture.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the savanna biome is/are correct?
1. It has tall grasses with scattered trees.
2. It experiences distinct wet and dry seasons.
3. The African savanna supports large herbivore herds.
questions.e: Tropical savanna: grassland with scattered trees, seasonal rainfall, and iconic megafauna — all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'thermocline' in oceans refers to:
o: A layer where temperature decreases rapidly with depth
questions.e: The thermocline separates the warm mixed surface layer from cold deep water; it is pronounced in tropical oceans.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: Which of the following is a warm ocean current?
questions.e: Kuroshio (warm, NW Pacific, Japan's 'Black Stream'); Labrador, Canary and Benguela are cold currents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The salinity of ocean water is highest in:
o: Enclosed seas in arid regions like the Red Sea
questions.e: High evaporation + low freshwater input raise salinity (Red Sea ~41 ppt); polar melt and equatorial rain lower it (~35 ppt average).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tides:
1. Spring tides occur at new and full moon.
2. Neap tides occur at first and third quarter moon.
3. The Bay of Fundy has the world's highest tidal range.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Spring (syzygy, sun-moon-earth aligned), neap (quadrature), and Fundy's ~16 m range are all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Aleutian Low' and 'Icelandic Low' are examples of:
questions.e: The Aleutian and Icelandic Lows (with the Azores/Bermuda and Pacific Highs) are semi-permanent pressure systems driving mid-latitude weather.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the ozone hole is/are correct?
1. It was first observed over Antarctica.
2. Chlorofluorocarbons are the main cause.
3. The Montreal Protocol (1987) aims to phase out ozone-depleting substances.
questions.e: Antarctic ozone hole (Farman et al., 1985), CFC-driven depletion, and the Montreal Protocol — the most successful environmental treaty — are all correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Köppen' climate classification uses which of the following as primary criteria?
questions.e: Köppen (A–E groups) classifies climates by monthly temperature and precipitation thresholds, with vegetation as the underlying indicator.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Physical Geography — Prelims Question Bank (44 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following is a correctly matched pair of local winds?
1. Chinook — Rockies (warm, dry)
2. Mistral — Rhone valley (cold)
3. Sirocco — Sahara to Mediterranean (hot, dusty)
questions.e: Chinook (snow-eater, Rockies), Mistral (cold Rhone valley wind), Sirocco (Saharan dust to southern Europe) are all correctly matched.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Preamble to the Indian Constitution is/are correct?
1. It is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. It has been amended only once, by the 42nd Amendment.
3. It is enforceable by the courts.
questions.e: The Preamble draws on the Objectives Resolution (1946) and was amended only once in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment, which inserted 'Socialist, Secular, Integrity'. It is non-justiciable, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
With reference to the Constituent Assembly of India, consider the following statements:
1. It was constituted under the scheme of the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
2. Members were elected by the provincial assemblies through proportional representation by single transferable vote.
3. The total membership of the Assembly was reduced to 299 after Partition.
questions.e: The Assembly was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan; members were elected indirectly by provincial assemblies via PR-STV; and after Partition its strength fell from 389 to 299.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Match the following Lists of the Seventh Schedule with their entries:
A. Union List — 1. Police
B. State List — 2. Defence of India
C. Concurrent List — 3. Bankruptcy and insolvency
questions.e: Defence is a Union subject, police is a State subject, and bankruptcy and insolvency fall under the Concurrent List.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following Articles of the Constitution deal with the Right to Equality?
1. Article 14
2. Article 15
3. Article 19
4. Article 18
questions.e: Articles 14 to 18 form the Right to Equality; Article 19 belongs to the Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the power of judicial review in India:
1. It is available to both the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
2. It extends to constitutional amendments.
3. It is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
questions.e: Judicial review (Articles 13, 32, 226, 136 etc.) is available to the SC and HCs, applies to amendments (Kesavananda/Minerva Mills), and is a basic-structure feature.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The doctrine of 'eminent domain' in Indian constitutional law is most closely associated with which of the following?
o: The power of Parliament to legislate on residuary subjects
The immunity of the President from legal proceedings
The State's power to acquire private property for public purpose
questions.e: Eminent domain is the State's inherent power to take private property for public use; after the 44th Amendment (1978), property is only a legal right under Article 300A with a duty to pay compensation implied.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following writs can be issued by the Supreme Court only against judicial or quasi-judicial authorities and not against purely administrative authorities?
questions.e: Prohibition (like Certiorari) is issued to lower courts/tribunals to stop them exceeding jurisdiction; it cannot be issued against purely administrative or legislative authorities.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 32 of the Constitution:
1. It is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. The Supreme Court cannot refuse to entertain a petition under it.
3. Parliament can suspend it during a national emergency.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right (the 'heart and soul'), and the Court cannot decline to hear a genuine Article 32 petition. It is not suspended during emergency — only enforcement of the Article 32 right itself can be suspended under Article 359 for non-Articles 20–21 rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under the Indian Constitution, the residuary powers of legislation are vested in:
o: Both Union and State legislatures equally
questions.e: Article 248 read with Entry 97 of the Union List vests residuary legislative power in Parliament — a departure from the US model.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains the languages officially recognised, and how many languages does it currently contain?
questions.e: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 officially recognised languages; the last additions were Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd Amendment (2003).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Match the following Constitutional Amendments with their subject matter:
A. 42nd Amendment — 1. Lowered voting age to 18
B. 52nd Amendment — 2. Mini-Constitution; added Fundamental Duties
C. 61st Amendment — 3. Anti-defection law
D. 73rd Amendment — 4. Panchayati Raj institutions
questions.e: 42nd (1976) added Fundamental Duties; 52nd (1985) inserted the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection); 61st (1988) lowered voting age from 21 to 18; 73rd (1992) constitutionalised Panchayats.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The phrase 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 was interpreted by the Supreme Court in which landmark case to mean 'due process of law' in substance?
o: R.C. Cooper v. Union of India
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
questions.e: In Maneka Gandhi (1978) the Court read 'procedure established by law' as requiring a procedure that is fair, just and reasonable — effectively importing due process into Article 21.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
1. It is a permanent and independent constitutional body under Article 324.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner prescribed for a Supreme Court judge.
3. The conditions of service of the Election Commissioners are determined by Parliament.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Article 324 creates the ECI; the CEC enjoys removal protection identical to an SC judge; and Parliament fixes service conditions (Article 324(5)).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a qualification prescribed for election as the President of India?
o: Qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
Must have held a ministerial office
questions.e: Article 58 requires Indian citizenship, age 35+, and eligibility for Lok Sabha membership; no prior office is required.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The impeachment of the President of India can be initiated in:
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
questions.e: Under Article 61, impeachment charges may be preferred by either House; the other House then investigates and must pass the resolution by a two-thirds majority.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
With reference to the Vice-President of India, consider the following statements:
1. He is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. He can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
3. While acting as President, he ceases to perform the duties of Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The VP is elected by MPs of both Houses (no state legislatures), removable by a Rajya Sabha resolution agreed by Lok Sabha, and when acting as President he does not chair the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to create new states and alter boundaries of existing states?
questions.e: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new states and alter areas, boundaries or names of existing states by simple-majority law.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Council of Ministers:
1. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
2. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
3. A minister must be a member of Parliament within six months of appointment.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Articles 75(2), 75(3) and 75(5) cover these: pleasure of the President, collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha, and the six-month membership rule.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The office of the Attorney General of India is provided under which Article, and what is his term of office?
o: Article 76; holds office during the pleasure of the President
Article 165; holds office during the pleasure of the Governor
questions.e: Article 76 creates the Attorney General, who holds office during the President's pleasure; Article 165 is the state-level counterpart (Advocate General).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following committees is/are exclusively composed of Lok Sabha members?
1. Public Accounts Committee
2. Estimates Committee
3. Committee on Public Undertakings
questions.e: The Estimates Committee (30 members) is drawn entirely from the Lok Sabha; PAC has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS) and COPU has 22 (15 LS + 7 RS).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: A Money Bill can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the:
questions.e: Article 109 requires the prior recommendation of the President for introduction of a Money Bill, which can originate only in the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding a Money Bill:
1. The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
2. If the Lok Sabha rejects the Rajya Sabha's recommendations, the Bill is deemed passed in its original form.
3. The President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Rajya Sabha has 14 days to recommend amendments; Lok Sabha may accept or reject them; the President may either assent or withhold assent to a Money Bill — he cannot return it (Article 111), making statement 3 wrong.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'Guillotine' in parliamentary procedure refers to:
o: A device for recording division votes
Putting budget demands to vote without discussion
A motion to remove the Speaker
The process of electing committee chairmen
questions.e: Guillotine is the closure device by which outstanding demands for grants are put to vote at a fixed time without further discussion.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following motions requires the support of at least 50 members to be admitted in the Lok Sabha?
questions.e: An adjournment motion needs the support of at least 50 members; a no-confidence motion requires only the Speaker's admission (conventionally 50 members' backing is cited for leave). Note: adjournment motion formally requires 50 members' support.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
The power of the President to promulgate ordinances under Article 123 is subject to which of the following limitations?
1. He must be satisfied that circumstances exist rendering immediate action necessary.
2. The ordinance must be laid before both Houses when they reassemble.
3. An ordinance ceases to operate six months after it is promulgated.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Ordinance power requires the President's satisfaction and laying before Parliament; an ordinance lapses six weeks (not six months) after reassembly, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Match the following Articles with their subject matter:
A. Article 50 — 1. Uniform civil code
B. Article 44 — 2. Separation of judiciary from executive
C. Article 48A — 3. Protection of environment
D. Article 51A — 4. Fundamental Duties
questions.e: Article 50 (separation of judiciary), Article 44 (uniform civil code), Article 48A (environment protection, 42nd Amendment), Article 51A (Fundamental Duties).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Sarkaria Commission (1983) was appointed to examine:
questions.e: The Sarkaria Commission examined Centre–State relations and recommended, among other things, restraint in the use of Article 356.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under Article 356, President's Rule in a state must be approved by Parliament within ____ and can continue for a maximum of ____ with periodic approvals.
questions.e: Proclamation under Article 356 lapses after two months unless approved; with Parliament's approval every six months it can run up to three years (with Election Commission certification after one year).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission is/are correct?
1. It is constituted by the President every five years under Article 280.
2. Its recommendations are binding on the government.
3. It recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
questions.e: Article 280 mandates a Finance Commission every five years to recommend tax-sharing and grants; its recommendations are advisory, not binding.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India audits the accounts of:
1. The Union Government
2. The State Governments
3. Local bodies, when requested by the President or Governor
questions.e: Article 149–151: CAG audits Union and state accounts and any other authority on the request of the President/Governor — covering all three.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' into the Preamble?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 — the 'Mini-Constitution' — inserted Socialist, Secular and Integrity into the Preamble.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The basic structure doctrine was propounded by the Supreme Court in:
o: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Waman Rao v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
questions.e: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held Parliament can amend but not destroy the Constitution's basic structure.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:
1. It is a permanent body not subject to dissolution.
2. One-third of its members retire every two years.
3. The Vice-President is its ex-officio Chairman.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Rajya Sabha is the continuing House: one-third retire biennially, it is never dissolved, and the Vice-President chairs it ex-officio.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as prescribed by the Constitution is:
questions.e: Article 81 caps Lok Sabha at 550 (530 states + 20 UTs); the Anglo-Indian nomination provision (erstwhile 552) was discontinued by the 104th Amendment (2020).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian federal system that departs from the classical federal model?
questions.e: India has single citizenship (unlike the USA's dual citizenship), a strong Centre, and residuary powers with Parliament — quasi-federal features.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The procedure for the amendment of the Constitution is laid down in:
questions.e: Article 368 in Part XX governs constitutional amendments, requiring special majorities (and state ratification for entrenched provisions).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: A constitutional amendment that seeks to change the representation of states in Parliament requires:
o: Special majority of Parliament plus ratification by half the states
questions.e: Changes to state representation in Parliament fall under Article 368's proviso, needing a special majority plus ratification by at least half the state legislatures.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Directive Principles of State Policy is/are correct?
1. They are non-justiciable.
2. They are fundamental in the governance of the country.
3. They were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
questions.e: Article 37 makes DPSPs non-justiciable yet fundamental in governance; they were inspired by the Irish Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'doctrine of pith and substance' is used by courts to:
o: Determine whether a law encroaches on another legislature's field
Decide the validity of constitutional amendments
Resolve conflicts between statutes and delegated legislation
questions.e: Pith and substance examines a law's true nature to decide if it falls within the enacting legislature's competence under the Seventh Schedule.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Article 14 — Equality before law
2. Article 16 — Equality of opportunity in public employment
3. Article 17 — Abolition of titles
4. Article 18 — Abolition of untouchability
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and Article 18 abolishes titles — the pairs 3 and 4 are swapped.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission is a:
questions.e: NHRC is a statutory body created by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 — not mentioned in the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Panchayati Raj institutions under the 73rd Amendment:
1. Reservation of one-third of seats for women is mandatory.
2. The State Election Commission conducts panchayat elections.
3. A uniform five-year term is prescribed for all panchayats.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment mandates one-third women's reservation, a five-year term, and elections by the State Election Commission. (Many states have since raised women's reservation to 50%.)

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution contains:
questions.e: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects (e.g., agriculture, rural housing, poverty alleviation) for Panchayat jurisdiction; the Twelfth Schedule lists 18 for municipalities.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Governor is/are correct?
1. He is appointed by the President and holds office during the President's pleasure.
2. He must have completed 35 years of age.
3. The Constitution lays down the grounds for his removal.
questions.e: The Governor is appointed by the President, must be 35+, and holds office during the President's pleasure — the Constitution prescribes no removal grounds or procedure.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'pleasure doctrine' under Article 310 applies to:
o: Civil servants holding office under the Union or a State
questions.e: Article 310: civil servants hold office during the President's/Governor's pleasure, subject to Article 311's safeguards; judges and CEC enjoy separate tenure protections.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Article provides for the appointment of acting Chief Justice and ad hoc judges in the Supreme Court?
questions.e: Articles 126 (acting CJI) and 127 (ad hoc judges) cover temporary Supreme Court appointments.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction under Article 143 can be invoked by:
questions.e: The President may refer questions of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its opinion under Article 143.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Emergency under Article 352:
1. It can be proclaimed on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
2. It requires the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet.
3. It must be approved by Parliament within one month by special majority.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Post-44th Amendment: 'armed rebellion' (not internal disturbance), written Cabinet advice, and approval within one month by special majority with periodic re-approval every six months.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: During a National Emergency, which Fundamental Rights CANNOT be suspended?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment bars suspension of Articles 20 and 21 even during emergency; other rights' enforcement may be suspended under Article 359.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The concept of 'Public Interest Litigation' in India was pioneered by:
o: Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer and Justice P.N. Bhagwati
questions.e: Justices Krishna Iyer and Bhagwati relaxed locus standi in the late 1970s–early 1980s (e.g., S.P. Gupta, 1981), birthing PIL.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the qualifications for appointment as a judge of a High Court?
o: Held judicial office in India for 10 years
Been an advocate of a High Court for 10 years
questions.e: Article 217 requires citizenship plus 10 years as judicial officer or advocate; no minimum age is prescribed.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Inter-State Council is established under:
questions.e: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council; it was first constituted in 1990 on Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule) is/are correct?
1. It was inserted by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.
2. An independent member joining a party after six months of election is disqualified.
3. The decision of the presiding officer on disqualification is final and not subject to judicial review.
questions.e: 52nd Amendment (1985) created the Tenth Schedule; independents joining a party after election are disqualified. Kihoto Hollohan (1992) held the Speaker's decision is subject to judicial review, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'office of profit' disqualification for MPs is laid down in:
questions.e: Article 102(1)(a) disqualifies MPs holding an office of profit under the government (other than exempted offices); Article 103 gives the President the decision power on the ECI's opinion.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following bodies is responsible for the delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies?
questions.e: A Delimitation Commission (chaired by a retired SC judge, with CEC as ex-officio member) is set up by Parliament; its orders have the force of law and cannot be questioned in court.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The last completed delimitation of constituencies in India was based on which Census, and until which year are the current Lok Sabha seat allocations frozen?
questions.e: The 2002 Delimitation Commission used 2001 Census data; the 42nd and 84th Amendments froze seat allocation (not boundaries) until 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax Council:
1. It is a constitutional body under Article 279A.
2. Decisions require a three-fourths majority of weighted votes.
3. The Centre has a one-third weightage in voting.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Article 279A (101st Amendment, 2016) created the GST Council; decisions need 3/4 weighted majority, with Centre holding one-third weight and states two-thirds collectively.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 101st Constitutional Amendment is associated with:
questions.e: The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced GST by inserting Articles 246A, 269A and 279A.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Right to Information Act, 2005 is/are correct?
1. It extends to the whole of India.
2. The Central Information Commission is a statutory body.
3. Information concerning national security is absolutely exempt from disclosure.
questions.e: RTI covers all of India (the 2019 amendment removed the J&K exception after reorganisation); CIC is statutory; security/intelligence organisations are exempt except in corruption or human-rights cases, so the exemption is not absolute.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in which year, and the first Lokpal of India was:
questions.e: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013; Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal in March 2019.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Match the following Commissions with their subject:
A. Punchhi Commission — 1. Review of the working of the Constitution
B. Venkatachaliah Commission — 2. Centre-State relations
C. Sarkaria Commission — 3. Centre-State relations (earlier)
D. Second ARC — 4. Administrative reforms
questions.e: Sarkaria (1983) and Punchhi (2007) both examined Centre–State relations; the Venkatachaliah Commission (2000) reviewed the Constitution's working; the Second ARC (2005) dealt with administrative reforms.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The concept of 'equality of opportunity' under Article 16 permits the State to make reservations for:
o: Backward classes which are inadequately represented in state services
Socially and educationally backward classes only
questions.e: Article 16(4) permits reservation for backward classes inadequately represented in services; the 103rd Amendment (2019) added EWS reservation under Article 16(6).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Article 21A (Right to Education) is/are correct?
1. It was inserted by the 86th Amendment in 2002.
2. It guarantees free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14.
3. It is enforceable only against private unaided schools.
questions.e: Article 21A (86th Amendment, 2002) makes 6–14 education a Fundamental Right enforceable against the State, implemented through the RTE Act, 2009 — not only against private schools.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'doctrine of basic structure' limits which of the following powers of Parliament?
questions.e: Kesavananda Bharati limits only the amending power under Article 368; ordinary legislation is tested against Fundamental Rights, not basic structure.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following is/are correctly matched?
1. Article 39A — Free legal aid
2. Article 43A — Workers' participation in management
3. Article 48 — Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
questions.e: Article 39A (free legal aid, 42nd Amendment), Article 43A (workers' participation, 42nd Amendment) and Article 48 (agriculture, animal husbandry, cow-slaughter prohibition) are all correctly matched.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: A 'cut motion' in the Lok Sabha can be moved during discussion of:
o: The Finance Bill at third reading
questions.e: Cut motions (policy, economy, token cuts) are moved to reduce demands for grants during budget discussion in the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The maximum number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Union Council of Ministers cannot exceed:
questions.e: The 91st Amendment (2003) capped ministerial strength at 15% of the Lok Sabha's membership (Article 75(1A)).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. He can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all then members of the Lok Sabha.
2. He does not vote in the first instance but exercises a casting vote in case of a tie.
3. He decides whether a bill is a Money Bill, and his decision is final.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: The Speaker is removable by an effective-majority resolution, votes only to break ties, and his Money-Bill certification under Article 110 is final.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Article deals with the appointment of the Chief Justice of India and judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.e: Article 124 governs appointment of the CJI and SC judges (through the collegium system evolved in the Judges cases); Article 217 covers High Court judges.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'collegium system' for judicial appointments in India was established through:
o: Interpretation by the Supreme Court in the Second and Third Judges cases
questions.e: The collegium emerged from the Second Judges case (1993) and Third Judges case (1998); the NJAC (99th Amendment) that tried to replace it was struck down in 2015.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about High Courts is/are correct?
1. Parliament can establish a common High Court for two or more states.
2. The President appoints High Court judges in consultation with the CJI and the Governor.
3. A High Court's writ jurisdiction is wider than the Supreme Court's.
questions.e: Article 231 allows common High Courts; appointments follow Article 217's consultation process; and High Courts can issue writs for legal rights too (Article 226), wider than Article 32.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The power of Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest is provided in:
questions.e: Article 249: Rajya Sabha may by two-thirds resolution authorise Parliament to legislate on a State subject in national interest for one year at a time.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under which Article can the President declare a financial emergency, and has it ever been invoked in India?
questions.e: Article 360 (financial emergency) has never been proclaimed in India; Article 352 was used in 1975 and Article 356 over a hundred times.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'Ninth Schedule' of the Constitution is associated with:
questions.e: The Ninth Schedule (1st Amendment, 1951) sheltered land-reform laws from challenge; I.R. Coelho (2007) held post-1973 insertions remain open to basic-structure review.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles was added by the 97th Amendment (2011)?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment added Article 43B directing the State to promote voluntary formation and democratic functioning of cooperative societies.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
1. He must be qualified to be appointed a Supreme Court judge.
2. He has the right of audience in all courts in India.
3. He can be a member of a parliamentary committee.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Article 76: the AG must be SC-judge-qualified and has audience in all courts; he may attend Parliament but cannot vote, and committee membership is not a right.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The first woman to become the Speaker of the Lok Sabha was:
questions.e: Meira Kumar became the first woman Speaker in 2009 (15th Lok Sabha); Sumitra Mahajan was the second (2014).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee is/are correct?
1. Its chairman is appointed by the Speaker from among Lok Sabha members.
2. By convention, the chairman belongs to the opposition.
3. A minister cannot be elected as its member.
questions.e: PAC's chairman is appointed by the Speaker (conventionally from the opposition since 1967-68) and ministers are barred from membership.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'Zero Hour' in Parliament is:
o: The first hour of sitting devoted to questions
An informal device where members raise matters without prior notice
The time allotted for the budget speech
The hour reserved for private members' bills
questions.e: Zero Hour (12 noon–1 pm) is an Indian innovation with no mention in the Rules of Procedure — members raise urgent matters without prior notice.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following motions is used to censure the Council of Ministers without expressing want of confidence?
questions.e: A censure motion criticises policies or an individual minister; unlike no-confidence, its passage does not compel resignation.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The term 'Office of Profit' has been interpreted by the Supreme Court with reference to which test?
o: The test of pecuniary gain and government control
questions.e: Courts apply tests of actual/expected pecuniary gain and the degree of government control over the office (e.g., Jaya Bachchan case, 2006).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) made ministerial advice binding (Article 74(1)); the 44th Amendment added that the President may require reconsideration once.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Council of States (Rajya Sabha):
1. Twelve members are nominated by the President for contributions to literature, science, art and social service.
2. Its members are elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies.
3. Union territories without legislatures have no representation in it.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Twelve nominated members (Article 80), indirect election by state assemblies; UTs like Delhi, Puducherry and J&K do have Rajya Sabha representation, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The power to grant pardons under Article 72 extends to:
o: All cases where punishment is by a Union law, court-martial cases, and death sentences
Death sentences and court-martial cases only
questions.e: Article 72 covers Union-law offences, court-martial sentences and all death sentences; Governors under Article 161 cover state-law offences (but not death sentences).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Fundamental Duties is/are correct?
1. They were added by the 42nd Amendment on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.
2. They are enforceable by writs.
3. The 86th Amendment added the duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6–14.
questions.e: Fundamental Duties (1976) came from the Swaran Singh Committee; they are non-justiciable; the 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 51A(k) on children's education.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's space programme:
1. ISRO was established in 1969.
2. The first Indian satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in 1975.
3. India launched its first lunar mission, Chandrayaan-1, in 2008.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: ISRO (1969, Vikram Sarabhai); Aryabhata (1975, Soviet launch); Chandrayaan-1 (2008, discovered lunar water signatures) — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Chandrayaan-3 (2023) is significant because India became the:
o: First Asian country to reach the Moon
First country to soft-land near the Moon's south pole
Second country to orbit the Moon
First country to land on the Moon
questions.e: Chandrayaan-3 (23 Aug 2023): Vikram lander + Pragyan rover at Shiv Shakti point — first soft landing near the lunar south pole; India the fourth to soft-land.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Aditya-L1 mission is India's first:
questions.e: Aditya-L1 (2023, Lagrange point L1): coronagraph and solar-wind instruments studying the Sun's corona and space weather.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Match the following ISRO launch vehicles:
A. PSLV — 1. Heaviest operational (GSLV Mk III class)
B. GSLV — 2. Workhorse for polar/SSO missions
C. LVM3 — 3. Geosynchronous missions with cryogenic stage
D. SSLV — 4. Small satellite launcher
questions.e: PSLV (polar workhorse), GSLV (cryogenic upper stage), LVM3 (heaviest, human-rated for Gaganyaan), SSLV (on-demand small sats) — correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The Gaganyaan mission aims to:
o: Land an Indian on the Moon
Send Indian astronauts to low-Earth orbit
questions.e: Gaganyaan: India's first crewed mission (3 astronauts, ~400 km LEO) — uncrewed test flights precede it; the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is a 2035 goal.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'NavIC':
1. It is India's regional satellite navigation system.
2. It provides coverage over India and 1,500 km around it.
3. It was earlier called IRNSS.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NavIC (IRNSS, 7 satellites): regional navigation — positioning over India +1,500 km; used in mobiles and strategic applications.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about '5G' technology is/are correct?
1. It offers higher speed and lower latency than 4G.
2. India launched 5G services in October 2022.
3. mmWave spectrum enables very high speeds over short ranges.
questions.e: 5G: eMBB/URLLC/mMTC use cases; India launch Oct 2022; mmWave (26 GHz) gives multi-Gbps speeds over short distances.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
The 'Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023' provides for:
1. A Data Protection Board of India
2. Consent-based data processing
3. Penalties up to ₹250 crore per contravention
questions.e: DPDP Act 2023: consent framework, Data Protection Board, graded penalties (up to ₹250 crore), following the Puttaswamy privacy judgment (2017).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Artificial Intelligence':
1. Machine learning is a subset of AI.
2. Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers.
3. The IndiaAI Mission was approved in 2024.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: AI > ML > deep learning hierarchy; IndiaAI Mission (₹10,372 crore, 2024) builds compute, datasets and AI safety capacity.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: Quantum computing uses 'qubits' which differ from classical bits because they:
o: Can exist in superposition of 0 and 1
questions.e: Qubits exploit superposition and entanglement; India's National Quantum Mission (2023) targets quantum computing, communication and sensing.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'National Quantum Mission' was approved in 2023 with the goal of developing:
o: Quantum computers, secure communications and sensors
questions.e: NQM (2023–31, ~₹6,000 crore): 50–1000 qubit computers, satellite QKD, quantum sensors — steered by DST.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'CRISPR' technology:
1. It enables precise editing of DNA.
2. It was adapted from bacterial immune systems.
3. Its developers won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: CRISPR-Cas9 (Doudna/Charpentier, Nobel 2020): bacterial-derived gene scissors — used in medicine, agriculture and India's genome-editing guidelines.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Human Genome Project' was completed in:
questions.e: HGP (1990–2003): first human genome sequence; India's GenomeIndia project (2024) sequenced 10,000 Indian genomes.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'vaccines' is/are correct?
1. Covishield is a viral-vector vaccine.
2. Covaxin is an inactivated-virus vaccine.
3. mRNA vaccines carry synthetic messenger RNA.
questions.e: Covishield (ChAdOx1 viral vector), Covaxin (inactivated), mRNA vaccines (Pfizer/Moderna) — the three major COVID vaccine platforms.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'mRNA' vaccine technology was recognised by the Nobel Prize in Physiology/Medicine in 2023 awarded to:
questions.e: Karikó and Weissman's nucleoside-base modifications made mRNA vaccines viable — Nobel 2023.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'nuclear energy' in India:
1. India operates Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors using natural uranium.
2. The three-stage programme was envisaged by Homi Bhabha.
3. Kudankulam uses Russian VVER reactors.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: PHWRs (natural uranium, heavy-water moderated); Bhabha's 3-stage (uranium → plutonium → thorium); Kudankulam VVER-1000 (Russia) — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: India's first nuclear reactor, 'Apsara', was commissioned in:
questions.e: Apsara (1956, Trombay) — Asia's first research reactor; Pokhran-I (Smiling Buddha) was 1974, Pokhran-II 1998.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Pokhran-II' nuclear tests (1998) were conducted under the code name:
questions.e: Operation Shakti (11 & 13 May 1998): five devices; Smiling Buddha was Pokhran-I (1974).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Thorium' in India:
1. India has among the world's largest thorium reserves (monazite sands).
2. Thorium is directly fissile.
3. The third stage of India's nuclear programme is thorium-based.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: India's monazite (Kerala, Odisha coasts) holds vast thorium; Th-232 is fertile (not fissile) — bred to U-233 in stage 3 (AHWR design).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'ITER' is/are correct?
1. It is an international fusion energy project in France.
2. India is a member.
3. It aims to demonstrate net fusion energy gain.
questions.e: ITER (Cadarache, France): 35 nations including India (in-kind contributions via ITER-India); tokamak aiming for Q≥10 fusion gain.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Large Hadron Collider' is located at:
questions.e: LHC (CERN, 27 km ring): discovered the Higgs boson (2012); India contributes through DAE/DST collaborations.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'supercomputers' in India:
1. The National Supercomputing Mission was launched in 2015.
2. PARAM Shivay was the first supercomputer under NSM.
3. AIRAWAT is an AI-focused supercomputer at C-DAC Pune.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NSM (2015, MeitY+DST): PARAM Shivay (IIT-BHU, 2019) first built; AIRAWAT (C-DAC) ranked among top AI supercomputers.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'PARAM' series of supercomputers was developed by:
questions.e: C-DAC (Pune): PARAM 8000 (1991, Vijay Bhatkar) broke the US denial after Pokhran — PARAM Siddhi-AI followed.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'UPI' is/are correct?
1. It was launched by NPCI in 2016.
2. It enables instant interbank transfers via mobile.
3. India processes the highest volume of real-time payments globally.
questions.e: UPI (NPCI, 2016): real-time, interoperable; India leads world real-time payment volumes (ACI Worldwide reports).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Aadhaar' project is implemented by:
questions.e: UIDAI (2009, Aadhaar Act 2016): 12-digit biometric ID — the world's largest biometric identity system.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'blockchain' technology:
1. It is a distributed ledger.
2. Bitcoin was the first blockchain application.
3. It is inherently tamper-evident.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Blockchain (Nakamoto, 2008): decentralised, hash-linked, tamper-evident ledger — RBI's retail CBDC (e₹) pilots use DLT concepts.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: India's Central Bank Digital Currency is called:
questions.e: e₹ (2022 pilots): retail e₹-R and wholesale e₹-W — RBI liability, distinct from private cryptocurrencies.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'cryptocurrencies' in India is/are correct?
1. They are not legal tender.
2. Gains are taxed at 30% plus surcharge.
3. The RBI has warned against their risks.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Crypto: not legal tender; 30% flat tax + 1% TDS (2022 Budget); RBI advocates a ban while pushing CBDC — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'James Webb Space Telescope' primarily observes in which wavelengths?
questions.e: JWST (2021): infrared-optimised (6.5 m gold-coated mirror) — sees the early universe through dust; stationed at Sun–Earth L2.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'black holes':
1. The first image of a black hole was released in 2019.
2. It showed the supermassive black hole in galaxy M87.
3. The Event Horizon Telescope is a global array.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: EHT's 2019 M87* image (and 2022 Sagittarius A*): Earth-sized virtual telescope via VLBI — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Higgs boson' is also called:
questions.e: Higgs (2012, LHC): gives mass via the Higgs field — popularised as the 'God particle'.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'gravitational waves' is/are correct?
1. First detected by LIGO in 2015.
2. Predicted by Einstein's general relativity.
3. India is building LIGO-India in Maharashtra.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: GW150914 (2015, binary black holes); GR prediction (1916); LIGO-India (Hingoli, Maharashtra) approved — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Artemis' programme of NASA aims to:
questions.e: Artemis: lunar return (Artemis II crewed flyby, III landing) and the Lunar Gateway — stepping stone to Mars.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'antibiotics':
1. Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming.
2. Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global threat.
3. India's Red Line campaign marks prescription-only antibiotics.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Fleming (1928); AMR (WHO top-10 threat, India's NAP 2017); Red Line campaign (2016) on antibiotic packs — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'DNA' double-helix structure was proposed by Watson and Crick in:
questions.e: Watson–Crick (1953, Nature), building on Franklin's X-ray data; Nobel 1962 (Wilkins shared).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'stem cells' is/are correct?
1. Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent.
2. iPSCs are reprogrammed adult cells.
3. They hold therapeutic potential for degenerative diseases.
questions.e: ESCs (pluripotent), iPSCs (Yamanaka, Nobel 2012), regenerative-medicine promise — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Polio' eradication in India was certified in:
questions.e: Last wild polio case: Jan 2011 (Howrah); WHO certified India polio-free March 2014 (South-East Asia region).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'tuberculosis' control in India:
1. The National TB Elimination Programme aims for TB elimination by 2025.
2. Nikshay portal tracks TB patients.
3. BCG vaccine protects against severe childhood TB.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: NTEP (2025 elimination goal, ahead of SDG 2030); Nikshay digital surveillance; BCG (childhood severe TB) — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Ayushman Bharat' scheme provides health cover of:
questions.e: PM-JAY (2018): ₹5 lakh/family/year for secondary/tertiary care — the world's largest health assurance scheme.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'defence' technology is/are correct?
1. Agni-V is an intercontinental ballistic missile.
2. INS Arihant is India's first indigenous nuclear submarine.
3. Tejas is an indigenous light combat aircraft.
questions.e: Agni-V (5,000+ km ICBM, MIRV-tested 2024 Mission Divyastra); INS Arihant (SSBN, 2016); Tejas LCA (HAL) — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'BrahMos' missile is:
o: A supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia
questions.e: BrahMos (Brahmaputra–Moskva): Mach 2.8+ supersonic cruise missile — land, sea, air and submarine variants.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'INS Vikrant':
1. It is India's first indigenous aircraft carrier.
2. It was commissioned in 2022.
3. It was built by Cochin Shipyard.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: INS Vikrant (IAC-1, 45,000 tonnes): Cochin Shipyard-built, commissioned Sept 2022 — India joined the indigenous-carrier club.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'S-400' air defence system was procured by India from:
questions.e: S-400 Triumf (Russia, 2018 deal, deliveries from 2021) — long-range SAM; CAATSA-waiver diplomacy surrounded it.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Drones' regulation in India is/are correct?
1. The Drone Rules, 2021 liberalised operations.
2. Drones are categorised by weight.
3. The Digital Sky platform manages permissions.
questions.e: Drone Rules 2021 (amended 2022): 5 weight classes (nano to large), Digital Sky approvals, PLI for drones — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Kavach' system in Indian Railways is:
questions.e: Kavach (RDSO): indigenous ATP preventing collisions/SPAD — being deployed on high-density routes.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'hydrogen' energy:
1. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using renewable electricity.
2. The National Green Hydrogen Mission was launched in 2023.
3. India targets 5 MMT annual green hydrogen production by 2030.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Green H2 (renewable electrolysis); NGHM (Jan 2023, ₹19,744 crore); 5 MMT by 2030 target — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'International Solar Alliance' was launched by India and France at:
questions.e: ISA (2015, Paris): solar-rich countries between the tropics; HQ Gurugram — India's flagship climate diplomacy.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'semiconductors' in India is/are correct?
1. The Semicon India programme (2021) incentivises fabs.
2. SCL Mohali is India's existing fab facility.
3. The Dholera fab proposal involves Tata-PSMC collaboration.
questions.e: Semicon India (₹76,000 crore): fab incentives; SCL Chandigarh (ISRO's fab); Tata–PSMC Dholera fab approved 2024 — all correct.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'Chandrayaan-4' mission planned by ISRO is intended to:
o: Bring lunar samples back to Earth
questions.e: Chandrayaan-4 (approved 2024): lunar sample-return — technology precursor for the planned 2040 crewed Moon landing.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.topic: Science & Tech — Prelims Question Bank (50 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'LiDAR' technology:
1. It uses laser pulses to map terrain.
2. It was used for the Central Vista and SVAMITVA surveys.
3. It can penetrate forest canopy.
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: LiDAR (laser ranging): SVAMITVA drone surveys for rural property cards; canopy-penetrating topographic mapping — all correct.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
With reference to the 2026 SCO Summit, consider the following statements:
1. It was held in Bishkek and marked the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
2. India outlined three priorities at the summit: security, connectivity and opportunity.
3. The summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 26th SCO Summit was held in Bishkek on 31 August–1 September 2026, marking 25 years of the SCO (founded 2001). Prime Minister Modi highlighted security, connectivity and opportunity as India's priorities, reiterated zero tolerance to terrorism with no double standards, and the summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's 2026 BRICS chairship:
1. India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi in September 2026.
2. It was India's first BRICS chairship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
