questions.e: The 4th Report of the Second ARC ('Ethics in Governance', 2007) recommended a Code of Ethics for ministers, a Code of Conduct for civil servants, statutory protection for whistle-blowers, and strengthening of the Lokpal/CVC architecture — forming the doctrinal backbone of GS-IV.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: India's first Lokpal, appointed in March 2019 under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, was:
questions.e: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, former Supreme Court judge, became India's first Lokpal in March 2019 — nearly six years after the Act's passage following the Anna Hazare movement. The Lokpal has jurisdiction over the Prime Minister (with safeguards), ministers, MPs and Group A–D public servants.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of which committee, and given statutory status in which year?
questions.e: The CVC was created in 1964 on the Santhanam Committee's recommendation as the apex vigilance institution, and given statutory status by the CVC Act, 2003 (following the Vineet Narain judgment). It exercises superintendence over the CBI in corruption cases.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The 2019 amendments to the RTI Act, 2005 changed which aspect of the Information Commissions?
o: The tenure, allowances and service conditions of the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners were made subject to central government prescription
The fee for filing RTI applications was abolished
Private companies were brought under the Act's ambit
The Act was extended to Jammu & Kashmir for the first time
questions.e: The RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 removed the fixed five-year tenure and salary equivalence with the Election Commission for the CIC and ICs, empowering the central government to prescribe their tenure and service conditions — a change critics said diluted the commissions' independence.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act received presidential assent in 2014. What is its current status?
o: It was merged with the Lokpal Act
It applies only to the private sector
It has received assent but has not been brought into force
questions.e: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 received assent in May 2014 but has never been brought into force; amendments proposed in 2015 (notably on national security exemptions) lapsed. Whistle-blower protection currently operates through the 2004 Public Interest Disclosure resolution administered by the CVC.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018 introduced which significant change?
o: It abolished the CBI's anti-corruption wing
It decriminalised all corruption by retired officials
It made corruption a bailable offence in all cases
It criminalised bribe-giving and required prior government sanction to investigate serving public servants
questions.e: The 2018 amendment to the 1988 Act made giving a bribe a direct offence, introduced corporate liability for bribing public servants, required prior sanction before investigating serving officers (a shield later debated), and set timelines for trial completion — rebalancing the Act toward the supply side of corruption.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: Daniel Goleman's framework of emotional intelligence identifies five components. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.e: Goleman's five components are self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy and social skills. Cognitive dissonance is Leon Festinger's concept (the discomfort of holding contradictory beliefs), not a component of emotional intelligence — a favourite cross-topic trap.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: Lawrence Kohlberg's theory of moral development proposes how many levels and stages?
questions.e: Kohlberg proposed three levels — pre-conventional, conventional and post-conventional — each with two stages (six total), from obedience-and-punishment reasoning up to universal ethical principles. Administrators are expected to function at the post-conventional level.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: 'The greatest happiness of the greatest number' is the defining maxim of which ethical theory?
o: Social contract theory, associated with Hobbes
Utilitarianism, associated with Jeremy Bentham and J. S. Mill
questions.e: Classical utilitarianism (Bentham's 'greatest happiness principle', refined by Mill) judges actions by their consequences — maximising aggregate welfare. It underpins cost-benefit analysis in policy but is critiqued for potentially sacrificing minority rights, the standard UPSC counterpoint.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: Immanuel Kant's deontological ethics is centred on which concept?
o: The categorical imperative — act only on maxims that can be universal laws
The invisible hand of the market
questions.e: Kant's categorical imperative commands acting only on maxims one could will as universal law, treating humanity always as an end and never merely as a means. It is the philosophical foundation of duty-based, rule-bound administrative conduct — contrasted with consequentialist utilitarianism.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: In public administration, 'probity' is best defined as:
o: Uprightness, honesty and incorruptibility in the discharge of public duty
Speed of file disposal regardless of scrutiny
questions.e: Probity — from the Latin probitas — means integrity, uprightness and honesty in public life. The Second ARC treats probity as the bedrock of governance, operationalised through transparency, accountability, codes of conduct and institutional checks like the CVC, CAG and Lokpal.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Citizen's Charter movement in India began in 1997. What is the Sevottam model associated with it?
o: A charter for private banks only
A framework for assessing and certifying the quality of public service delivery against charter standards
A pension scheme for charter signatories
questions.e: Citizen's Charters (since 1997) declare service standards, and the Sevottam model — developed by the Department of Administrative Reforms — provides a quality-management framework to assess implementation, grievance redress and service delivery, with certification for compliant organisations.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The distinction between a Code of Conduct and a Code of Ethics is that:
o: A code of ethics is legally binding while a code of conduct is voluntary
There is no difference between the two
Only the private sector uses codes of conduct
A code of conduct specifies enforceable rules of behaviour, while a code of ethics articulates aspirational values and principles
questions.e: A code of conduct is a set of specific, enforceable rules (do's and don'ts with penalties — like the Central Civil Services Conduct Rules, 1964), whereas a code of ethics states broad values and principles to guide discretionary judgment. The Second ARC recommended both: conduct rules for enforceability, an ethics code for moral compass.

questions.subject: Ethics
questions.topic: Ethics, Integrity & Aptitude — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'ABC model' of attitude in social psychology stands for:
questions.e: Attitudes comprise three components — affective (feelings), behavioural (action tendencies) and cognitive (beliefs). GS-IV expects administrators to understand this because persuasion and behavioural change (e.g., in Swachh Bharat or Beti Bachao) must target all three, not just information.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992), which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj, came into force on 24 April 1993 and added which schedule listing 29 subjects?
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects like agriculture, primary health and drinking water) for rural local bodies, while the 74th Amendment added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) for urban local bodies.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) is significant because it:
o: Applied only to the Sixth Schedule areas of the Northeast
Extended Part IX panchayat provisions to Fifth Schedule areas with special powers to the Gram Sabha over natural resources
Created a separate Election Commission for tribal areas
questions.e: PESA (1996) extends panchayat provisions to Fifth Schedule areas, vesting the Gram Sabha with powers over minor forest produce, land alienation, village markets and prior recommendation for land acquisition — a legislative recognition of tribal self-governance, though implementation remains uneven.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q:
Under MGNREGA, which of the following entitlements is/are correct?
1. 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year.
2. At least one-third of beneficiaries must be women.
3. Unemployment allowance is payable if work is not provided within 15 days.
questions.e: All three are correct under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005: 100 days per household on demand, one-third women's participation (a floor often exceeded), and unemployment allowance if employment is not provided within 15 days of application.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Aspirational Districts Programme, launched in January 2018, covers 112 districts and tracks progress across five themes. Which of the following is NOT one of the five themes?
questions.e: The ADP's five themes are health and nutrition, education, agriculture and water resources, financial inclusion and skill development, and infrastructure. Districts are ranked monthly on 49 KPIs in a competitive-federalism 'delta ranking' by NITI Aayog.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) was launched on 23 September 2018 from Ranchi. What is its cover and target population?
o: ₹10 lakh per family for government employees only
₹2 lakh per person for all citizens
₹1 lakh per family for urban households only
₹5 lakh per family per year for about 55 crore beneficiaries (12 crore+ families)
questions.e: PM-JAY, the world's largest health assurance scheme, provides ₹5 lakh annual cover per family for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation to about 55 crore beneficiaries identified by SECC 2011 deprivation criteria, implemented through state health agencies with portability across India.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The National Health Mission (NHM) was formed by subsuming which two earlier missions, and in which year?
o: AYUSH Mission and NHM — merged in 2014
ICDS and Mid-Day Meal — merged in 2015
questions.e: The National Rural Health Mission (2005) and National Urban Health Mission (2013) were merged into the National Health Mission in 2013. NHM funds ASHAs, institutional delivery incentives (JSY/JSSK) and health-system strengthening, and anchored India's pandemic response architecture.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: Samagra Shiksha, launched in 2018, subsumed which three schemes?
o: ICDS, Beti Bachao and Skill India
Mid-Day Meal, KGBV and NEP implementation
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and Teacher Education
Operation Blackboard, DPEP and Mahila Samakhya
questions.e: Samagra Shiksha (2018) integrated SSA (elementary), RMSA (secondary) and Teacher Education into a single scheme for school education from pre-school to Class 12, aligned later with NEP 2020's 5+3+3+4 structure and foundational literacy goals.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Jal Jeevan Mission (2019) aims to provide tap water to every rural household. What is its service-level benchmark per person per day?
questions.e: Jal Jeevan Mission targets Functional Household Tap Connections for all rural households with a service standard of 55 lpcd of potable water, quality-tested through village water and sanitation committees and sensor-based monitoring.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) declared rural India open-defecation-free on which date, and what was the mission's launch date?
questions.e: SBM was launched on 2 October 2014 and rural India was declared ODF on 2 October 2019 (Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary), with over 10 crore toilets built. SBM 2.0 (2021–26) shifted focus to ODF Plus — solid and liquid waste management.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: PM-KISAN, launched in February 2019, provides income support of what amount, in how many instalments?
o: ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000
₹5,000 per year in a single instalment
questions.e: PM-KISAN gives ₹6,000 per year to landholding farmer families in three four-monthly instalments of ₹2,000 via DBT, with e-KYC mandatory. It is a central sector scheme fully funded by the Government of India.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin (2016) replaced which earlier rural housing scheme, and what was its original target?
o: Indira Awaas Yojana — 2.95 crore houses by 2022
Rajiv Awaas Yojana — 1 crore houses by 2020
National Rural Housing Mission — 50 lakh houses by 2019
Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana — 5 crore houses by 2025
questions.e: PMAY-G (April 2016) restructured the Indira Awaas Yojana (1985) with a target of 2.95 crore pucca houses by 2022, enhanced unit assistance (₹1.2 lakh plains/₹1.3 lakh hilly), and convergence with toilets (SBM) and LPG (Ujjwala). Additional 2 crore houses were approved in 2024.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) was launched in 2011 and renamed in 2015. In September 2026 its Lakhpati Didi target was revised to:
o: 3 crore women, halved from the earlier target
6 crore women, with about 3.5 crore Lakhpati Didis created so far
1 crore women, the original target unchanged
questions.e: DAY-NRLM (launched as NRLM in 2011, renamed in 2015) had its Lakhpati Didi target doubled from 3 crore to 6 crore women at a September 2026 review, with about 3.5 crore achieved. A Lakhpati Didi is an SHG member whose household earns at least ₹1 lakh annually.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: Digital India, launched on 1 July 2015, is built on nine pillars. Which of the following is one of them?
o: Mandatory social media accounts for all citizens
Broadband highways and universal mobile connectivity
Privatisation of all government data centres
questions.e: Digital India's nine pillars include broadband highways, universal mobile access, public internet access, e-governance, e-Kranti (electronic delivery of services), IT for jobs, electronics manufacturing and early harvest programmes — the architecture behind UPI, DigiLocker, CoWIN and ONDC.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q: The 'One Nation One Election' proposal, examined by the Kovind committee, would require which constitutional step at minimum?
o: Approval by the Election Commission alone
Amendments including a new Article 82A and ratification by at least half the states for certain changes
A simple executive order by the President
questions.e: The high-level committee chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind (report: March 2024) recommended simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly polls via constitutional amendments — including a new Article 82A — with ratification by at least half the states for provisions affecting federal features. Two Bills were introduced in December 2024 and sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.topic: Governance & Social Justice — Wave 2 Bank (15 MCQs)
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025:
1. It renamed the Waqf Act, 1995 as the Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act.
2. It provides for the inclusion of non-Muslim members in Waqf Boards and Tribunals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Passed in April 2025, the Act renamed the 1995 Act as UMEED, mandates inclusion of non-Muslim members in the Central Waqf Council, State Waqf Boards and Tribunals, requires waqf registration on a central portal, and gives the District Collector a role in surveying disputed waqf properties.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 establishes a three-tier institutional structure. Who chairs the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)?
questions.e: The NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister, with up to nine members including a Vice-Chairperson. State DM Authorities are chaired by Chief Ministers and District DM Authorities by Collectors/District Magistrates — a structure mirroring the federal division of responsibility.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) was raised in 2006 and functions under which ministry? Its battalions are drawn from which forces?
o: Ministry of Environment — drawn from forest services
Ministry of Home Affairs — battalions drawn from CAPFs (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, SSB)
NDMA directly — drawn from state police
Ministry of Defence — drawn from the Army
questions.e: The NDRF, raised in 2006 under the DM Act, functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs with battalions drawn from Central Armed Police Forces. It is the world's largest dedicated disaster-response force and deploys for floods, cyclones, building collapses and CBRN emergencies.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030) was adopted in March 2015 at which city, and how many priorities for action does it set?
questions.e: The Sendai Framework (successor to the Hyogo Framework) was adopted at the Third UN World Conference in Sendai, Japan, in March 2015. It sets four priorities — understanding risk, strengthening governance, investing in resilience, and enhancing preparedness — and seven global targets.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) was launched by India in 2019 at which forum, and where is its secretariat?
o: UN Climate Action Summit, New York — secretariat in New Delhi
G20 Summit, Osaka — secretariat in Tokyo
World Economic Forum, Davos — secretariat in Geneva
questions.e: PM Modi launched the CDRI at the UN Climate Action Summit in New York in September 2019. Headquartered in New Delhi, it is a global partnership (40+ countries) promoting resilient infrastructure — India's second major global initiative after the International Solar Alliance.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: India's first National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) was released in which year, and what is its doctrinal basis?
o: 2016 — aligned with the Sendai Framework and the PM's 10-point agenda on DRR
2005 — based solely on the DM Act
questions.e: India released its first-ever NDMP in June 2016 (revised 2019), aligned with the Sendai Framework's four priorities and the Prime Minister's 10-point agenda on disaster risk reduction announced at the 2016 Asian Ministerial Conference in New Delhi.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The Prime Minister's 10-point agenda on disaster risk reduction was announced at which event?
o: Asian Ministerial Conference on DRR, New Delhi (2016)
questions.e: PM Modi announced the 10-point agenda — including leveraging technology, building local capacity, and ensuring wider participation of women — at the Asian Ministerial Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction in New Delhi in November 2016, which India hosted.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: Ahmedabad's Heat Action Plan (2013) is significant in disaster management because it was:
o: A plan to relocate the city away from the Sabarmati
A flood insurance scheme for farmers
South Asia's first city-level heat action plan, later scaled into NDMA's national guidelines
questions.e: After the 2010 heatwave killed over 1,300 people in Ahmedabad, the city launched South Asia's first Heat Action Plan in 2013 (with IIPH-Gandhinagar and NRDC) — early warnings, cool roofs, public awareness — which became the template for NDMA's 2016 national guidelines on heatwave management.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The Bhopal gas tragedy of December 1984 involved the leakage of which gas, and it directly led to which legislation?
questions.e: The leak of methyl isocyanate from the Union Carbide plant on the night of 2–3 December 1984 killed thousands and led directly to the umbrella Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the creation of MoEFCC's EIA regime, and India's push for absolute-liability jurisprudence (Oleum gas leak case, 1986).

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre, established after the 2004 tsunami, is located at which institution?
questions.e: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning System operates from the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Hyderabad, since 2007 — providing tsunami advisories for the Indian Ocean region within minutes of a tsunamigenic earthquake, under UNESCO's IOC framework.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q:
On India's seismic zone map (BIS), Zone V — the highest risk zone — includes which of the following areas?
1. The entire Northeast
2. Parts of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
3. The Rann of Kutch
4. The Andaman & Nicobar Islands
questions.e: All four are in Zone V, the highest damage-risk zone on the BIS seismic map: the entire Northeast, parts of J&K/Himachal/Uttarakhand, the Rann of Kutch (site of the 2001 Bhuj earthquake), and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands (site of the 2004 rupture).

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: IMD's cyclone intensity classification: a 'Very Severe Cyclonic Storm' has maximum sustained wind speeds of:
questions.e: IMD classifies: Cyclonic Storm (62–88 kmph), Severe Cyclonic Storm (89–117), Very Severe Cyclonic Storm (119–165), and Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm (166–221). The 119–165 band is the standard Prelims trap between 'severe' and 'extremely severe'.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The Civil Defence Act, under which civil defence volunteers function, was enacted in which year, and under which ministry does civil defence operate?
questions.e: The Civil Defence Act, 1968 (enacted after the 1962 and 1965 wars) provides for civil defence measures during hostile attack and disasters. Civil defence operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs, with wardens and volunteers forming the community-level response tier.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: The 'Manual for Drought Management' (2016), which standardises drought declaration and relief, was issued by which ministry?
questions.e: The Manual for Drought Management (revised 2016) by the Department of Agriculture lays down the methodology — rainfall deviation, dry spells, remote-sensing indices — for states to declare drought and trigger relief under SDRF/NDRF norms, replacing the earlier 2009 manual.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: Under the DM Act, 2005, the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) is financed primarily through:
o: A cess on excise and customs duties credited to the fund
questions.e: The NDRF (the renamed National Calamity Contingency Fund) is financed through a National Calamity Contingent Duty (a cess on excise/customs) plus budgetary support, and supplements the State Disaster Response Fund when a calamity of severe nature strikes.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.q: With reference to the 2026 monsoon drought assessment, the IIT Gandhinagar India Drought Monitor reported that the area under dry or drought conditions expanded from about 39% to 52.5% in roughly a month. Which index family does such operational drought monitoring primarily rely on?
o: Standardised Precipitation and soil-moisture-based indices from IMD and satellite data
questions.e: Operational drought monitors like IIT Gandhinagar's blend IMD rainfall data with satellite-derived soil moisture, evapotranspiration and vegetation indices (standardised precipitation indices) to classify meteorological, agricultural and hydrological drought in near-real time.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 24 December 2024.
2. It is the first comprehensive global treaty on cybercrime.
3. India signed the Convention on 26 September 2026 on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The Convention — full title: 'Strengthening International Cooperation for Combating Certain Crimes Committed by Means of Information and Communications Technology Systems and for the Sharing of Evidence in Electronic Form of Serious Crimes' — was adopted on 24 December 2024, opened for signature on 25 October 2025, and had 95 signatories when India signed on 26 September 2026. Its nine chapters include human-rights safeguards and a 24x7 cooperation network for investigations, mutual legal assistance and extradition; it is also the first global treaty to specifically criminalise ICT-facilitated sexual violence against children.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to the Election Commission of India's decisions on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, announced on 26 September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The declaration attached to Form 6 will be required only during the SIR exercise; the earlier format will apply otherwise for fresh voter registration.
2. A committee headed by a senior Deputy Election Commissioner, including an independent IIT/IIIT expert, will review ECINET's compliance with relevant laws and rules.
3. Field officers will continue to have unrestricted access to the ECINET platform regardless of their statutory powers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong. The ECI said the Supreme Court upheld the Form 6 declaration for the SIR, and that field officers will have only role-based access to ECINET in line with their statutory powers — not unrestricted access. The expert committee reviewing ECINET's legal compliance follows reports of dissent within the Commission over SIR-related decisions.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to India's first LNG-powered train, flagged off from Sabarmati on 27 September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It uses a dual-fuel system that allows the same engine to run on both LNG and diesel depending on fuel availability.
2. Two Driving Power Cars, each of 1,400 HP, were converted to the LNG-diesel system.
3. LNG is expected to replace up to 100 per cent of the diesel used by the engine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong. After more than 2,000 km of field trials, LNG can replace only up to about 40 per cent of diesel — which is why the dual-fuel design matters, since operations continue even when LNG is unavailable. Each converted DPC carries an LNG tank of about 2,200 litres (950–1,000 kg of usable LNG), and Indian Railways estimates savings of about Rs 11.9 lakh per year per DPC alongside lower CO2, NOx and particulate-matter emissions.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The MOI-1A spacecraft, scheduled to fly aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission on 1 October 2026, is best described as:
o: India's first crewed orbital mission module
A conventional communications satellite meant for rural broadband
An orbital edge-computing satellite that processes data in orbit instead of downlinking raw data to Earth
questions.e: Correct: MOI-1A of Bengaluru startup TakeMe2Space is described as India's first orbital computing satellite — a sub-50 kg spacecraft carrying Nvidia Orin NX edge-computing processors. Customers upload containerised AI models to it, and it processes data as it passes over a target area, transmitting only the analysis to Earth rather than the full dataset — a model aimed at agriculture, mining, supply-chain and insurance users. Its 23 signed customers include US-based Little Place Labs; its predecessor MOI-1 was lost to a launch-vehicle third-stage failure.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
According to the Reserve Bank of India's September 2026 Bulletin, consider the following statements:
1. The Indian economy recorded robust growth of 7.8 per cent in Q1 of 2026-27.
2. Headline CPI inflation inched up to 4.8 per cent in August 2026, driven by the food and beverages group along with a pickup in fuel and core components.
3. India's foreign exchange reserves reached an all-time high.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The Bulletin's 'State of the Economy' noted strong export growth narrowing the merchandise trade deficit, system liquidity surplus surging on FCNR(B) deposit flows, and bank deposits growing at their fastest pace in 15 years in August — while cautioning that re-escalating West Asia tensions had sharply raised crude oil prices, reigniting supply-chain and inflationary pressures.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Government of Maharashtra issued a government resolution on 26 September 2026 declaring drought in 265 of the State's 358 talukas. This declaration was based on:
o: The India Drought Monitor report of IIT Gandhinagar
The report of the Agriculture Commissioner, following prolonged rainfall deficits that caused crop loss
A directive of the National Disaster Management Authority
The recommendation of the State Finance Commission
questions.e: Correct: the GR was issued on the basis of the Agriculture Commissioner's report after prolonged rainfall deficits caused crop loss. Drought declaration is an executive decision of the state government. The declaration covered major parts of Vidarbha, Marathwada, North Maharashtra and the Pune division; the worst-hit districts were Yavatmal (16 taluks), Jalgaon (15), and Ahilyanagar/Nagpur/Amravati/Nanded (14 each).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to India's fifth-generation fighter aircraft programme, consider the following statements:
1. The Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) is India's indigenous fifth-generation fighter programme.
2. The first AMCA prototype is expected to roll out in September 2028.
3. India has decided to acquire the Russian Sukhoi-57 stealth fighter to bridge the stealth gap with China.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong. At the NDTV Defence Summit 2026 (28 September 2026), Defence Secretary R.K. Singh explicitly said the government has not taken any decision on acquiring the Su-57 — though Russia has offered licensed production with deep tech transfer. India plans to bridge the stealth gap (China is believed to operate about 500 J-20/J-35s) by layering AI over the IAF's Integrated Air Command and Control System (IACCS), fused with army and air-defence networks, to improve 4.5-generation fighters like the Tejas until AMCA enters service.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI payments announced in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. From 15 October 2026, a 0.4 per cent MDR applies to commercial person-to-merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.
2. The MDR is capped at Rs 300 for payments of Rs 75,000 and above.
3. Person-to-person transfers of any size will continue to attract zero charges.
4. RuPay debit card payments retain their no-charge protection without any monetary ceiling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. On 28 September 2026 the Supreme Court refused to stay the levy — calling it 'less a legal and more a technical issue' — but issued notice to the Centre, RBI, NPCI and the UPI Steering Committee. Essential thin-margin sectors (railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, agricultural inputs) pay a flat Rs 5 per transaction above Rs 2,000, while payments into mutual funds, securities and stockbrokers attract 0.02 per cent, also capped at Rs 300.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: According to an EY report released on 28 September 2026, which of the following best describes its policy call for the RBI's October 2026 review?
o: A 25-basis-point hike in the repo rate, currently at 5.25%
A pause with a shift to a neutral stance
An off-cycle 100-basis-point hike to defend the rupee
questions.e: EY's 28 September 2026 report makes a case for a 25-bps hike at the October MPC, citing sticky food inflation and strong growth, with the repo at 5.25%. The MPC targets 4% CPI inflation within a ±2% band under the RBI Act, 1934.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: HSBC Global Investment Research, in a note dated 28 September 2026, expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by a cumulative 50 basis points over FY27. Which of the following is cited as a key driver?
o: Resurfacing inflation risks including imported inflation via a weaker rupee and firm crude
A collapse in bank credit growth
A statutory requirement to hold rates unchanged
questions.e: HSBC's call rests on resurfacing inflation risks — imported inflation through a weaker rupee and firm crude prices — even as growth stays resilient. Prelims trap: repo changes transmit through the LAF corridor, not through CRR directly.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: On 28 September 2026, Union Labour and Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya said ESIC provides health security to 25 crore people. Under the ESI Act, 1948, which of the following is correct?
o: ESI applies to factories/establishments with 10+ employees earning up to a notified wage ceiling, with employer-employee contributions
ESI covers only central government employees
ESI is a fully tax-funded universal scheme with no contributions
ESI benefits are limited to maternity relief only
questions.e: The ESI Act, 1948 covers factories and establishments employing 10 or more persons (20 in some states) drawing wages up to the notified ceiling (Rs 21,000/month, Rs 25,000 for persons with disabilities), funded by employer (3.25%) and employee (0.75%) contributions. Benefits include medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Consider the following statements about the National Digital Tourism Stack (NDTS): 1. It was launched on World Tourism Day 2026 by the Tourism Minister at Bharat Mandapam. 2. It is being built with ONDC and ICDIA support. 3. It targets 23,000 tourism experiences and homestays by end-2028. Which are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. NDTS was launched 27 September 2026 (World Tourism Day) by Gajendra Shekhawat at Bharat Mandapam, developed with ONDC and the International Centre for DPI Innovation and Advancement (ICDIA), targeting 23,000 experiences and homestays by end-2028 with a pilot in January 2027.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME), reported on 28 September 2026, maps the 21-cm emission line of neutral hydrogen. This technique is called intensity mapping because it
o: measures the combined radio glow of many unresolved galaxies instead of cataloguing individual ones
uses X-ray intensity to find black holes
maps hydrogen only inside the Milky Way
questions.e: Intensity mapping measures the aggregate 21-cm emission from large cosmic volumes without resolving individual galaxies, tracing large-scale structure and the expansion history shaped by dark energy. The 21-cm line comes from the hyperfine spin-flip transition of neutral hydrogen.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Exercise KAZIND-2026, which began on 28 September 2026, is the bilateral military exercise between India and
questions.e: KAZIND is the India-Kazakhstan joint exercise; the 2026 edition (28 Sep–11 Oct) is at Oskemen with a 60-member Indian contingent mainly from the Garhwal Rifles. Kyrgyzstan pairs with India in KHANJAR; Uzbekistan in DUSTLIK; Mongolia in NOMADIC ELEPHANT.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Global Cooling Pledge Assembly is correct?
o: It was held in Singapore on 15–18 September 2026, where the first Cool Leaders — Singapore, the UAE and Dong Mingzhu — were named
It was the COP30 climate summit held in Belem
It launched the International Solar Alliance
It adopted a binding treaty phasing out HFCs by 2030
questions.e: The Assembly ran 15–18 September 2026 in Singapore under UNEP's Cool Coalition; on 17 September the inaugural Cool Leaders (Singapore, UAE, Gree Electric's Dong Mingzhu) were named alongside a Heat Resilience Roadmap and Nature for Cooling Challenge. The Global Cooling Pledge itself dates to COP28 (2023); the HFC phase-down is the Kigali Amendment.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Home Ministry extended AFSPA for six months from 1 October 2026 in parts of Manipur, Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh. 2. In Manipur, areas under 13 police stations remain excluded. 3. Section 3 of AFSPA empowers declaration of disturbed areas. Which are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The 25 September 2026 notifications extend AFSPA from 1 October 2026 for six months: most of Manipur (excluding 13 police stations in five valley districts), nine Nagaland districts plus 21 police-station areas, and Tirap/Changlang/Longding plus Namsai police-station areas in Arunachal Pradesh. Section 3 allows the Centre/state Governor/UT Administrator to declare disturbed areas.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to the Pashudhan (Livestock) Insurance Portal launched in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched by the Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
2. It provides a digital platform for policy issuance, claims settlement, monitoring and reporting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The Pashudhan (Livestock) Insurance Portal was launched on 28 September 2026 by Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying) and digitises policy issuance, claims, monitoring and reporting. Remember: animal husbandry is a State subject under the Seventh Schedule.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Essar Group announced in September 2026 a plan to invest in a steel plant in the US state of Iowa. What is the announced size of this investment?
questions.e: Essar announced a USD 15-billion investment plan for a steel plant in Iowa, unveiled at the White House by CEO Prashant Ruia. The announcement came amid shifting US tariff and industrial policy — relevant for GS III (industrial policy) and India–US economic ties.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In September 2026, the United States exempted India and 19 other countries from a proposed 100% import tariff on:
questions.e: The US exempted India and 19 other countries from its proposed 100% import tariff on specialty drugs, sparing Indian pharmaceutical exporters. Specialty drugs are high-cost medicines for complex conditions such as cancer and autoimmune disorders, distinct from generics — and the US is India's largest drug export market.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to minimum public shareholding (MPS) norms in India, consider the following statements:
1. Listed companies must maintain at least 25% public shareholding under SEBI rules.
2. In September 2026, SEBI found no violations by Adani Group companies in its MPS probe.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. SEBI's MPS norms require listed companies to keep at least 25% of shareholding with the public, and in September 2026 SEBI closed its probe into alleged Adani MPS breaches with no violations found. SEBI is a statutory body under the SEBI Act, 1992.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The National High Speed Rail Corporation launched its first 100-metre steel bridge in September 2026. For which corridor was this bridge launched?
questions.e: The ~1,405-tonne, 100-metre steel bridge was launched for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor in Maharashtra. Steel bridges are used where the viaduct must cross highways, railways or rivers without intermediate piers. The corridor uses Japanese Shinkansen technology with JICA loan assistance.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q:
With reference to examination reforms in India, consider the following statements:
1. A task force headed by Nandan Nilekani is reviewing the conduct of national-level examinations.
2. In September 2026, the task force consulted K. Radhakrishnan, who headed the 2024 committee on the NEET-UG paper-leak controversy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Nandan Nilekani's task force on examination reforms is reviewing national-level examinations after the 2024 NEET-UG and UGC-NET irregularities, and it consulted former ISRO chairman K. Radhakrishnan, who headed the 2024 NEET-UG paper-leak committee. The National Testing Agency was set up in 2017 under the Ministry of Education.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In September 2026, the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly passed a resolution demanding:
o: A separate High Court for Ladakh
questions.e: The J&K Assembly passed a resolution demanding restoration of statehood, with the National Conference-led government pressing the Centre on its post-2019 commitment. The Supreme Court, while upholding the abrogation of Article 370 in December 2023, directed restoration of statehood at the earliest. J&K was reorganised into two UTs under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay announced in September 2026 that the state government would gift what to every newborn child?
o: A health insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh
A free laptop on admission to Class 1
questions.e: CM Vijay announced a 1-gram gold ring for every newborn child in Tamil Nadu, a welfare measure aimed at new mothers and infants. Health and family welfare schemes are largely in the States' domain — this recalls Tamil Nadu's earlier marriage-assistance schemes involving gold.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is available to both citizens and non-citizens?
o: Article 16 — equality of opportunity in public employment
Article 20 — protection in respect of conviction
Article 19 — protection of the six freedoms
questions.e: Article 20 uses 'person', so it protects everyone including foreigners. Articles 15, 16 and 19 are expressly citizen-only.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The writ of Habeas Corpus is issued to:
o: Command a public authority to perform a legal duty
Produce a detained person before the court
Quash the order of a subordinate court
Restrain a person from holding public office
questions.e: Habeas Corpus ('to have the body') tests the legality of detention. Mandamus commands duty; Certiorari quashes orders; Quo Warranto questions authority to hold office.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which amendment added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is the only amendment to have touched the Preamble.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Under Article 32, a citizen can move the Supreme Court:
o: For enforcement of any legal right
Only for enforcement of Fundamental Rights
Only after exhausting High Court remedies
questions.e: Article 32 is confined to Fundamental Rights — but it is itself a Fundamental Right ('heart and soul'). Article 226 is wider, covering legal rights too.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The minimum age for election to the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha is respectively:
questions.e: 25 years for the Lok Sabha (Art 84/173 read with RPA) and 30 years for the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A money bill, after being passed by the Lok Sabha, can be detained by the Rajya Sabha for a maximum of:
questions.e: Article 109: the Rajya Sabha must return a money bill within 14 days with recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The doctrine of basic structure was laid down in:
questions.e: Kesavananda Bharati (13-judge bench, 1973): Parliament may amend but cannot destroy the Constitution's basic structure.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article:
questions.e: Article 280 mandates a Finance Commission every five years to recommend tax-sharing between the Union and states.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which list in the Seventh Schedule contains 'education'?
questions.e: Education is in the Concurrent List (moved there by the 42nd Amendment). On repugnancy, Union law prevails (Art 254).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The 73rd Amendment constitutionalised:
questions.e: The 73rd (1992, in force 24 April 1993) added Part IX on panchayats; the 74th covers municipalities (Part IXA).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution lists:
questions.e: 29 subjects for devolution to panchayats (Art 243G). The Twelfth Schedule has 18 urban functions.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament under Article 108?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Article 118(4): the Speaker presides (Deputy Speaker in absence). Deadlocks on ordinary bills are resolved by simple majority.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The collegium system of judicial appointments emerged from the:
questions.e: The Second Judges case (1993) gave primacy to the CJI-led collegium; the Third Judges case (1998) refined it. The NJAC (99th Amendment) was struck down in 2015.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the:
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Part IVA/Article 51A on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation; the 86th added the eleventh duty.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: PESA, 1996, extends panchayat provisions to:
o: Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule
questions.e: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 adapts Part IX for Fifth Schedule areas with tribal self-governance safeguards.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The residuary powers of legislation vest in:
questions.e: Article 248 assigns unlisted subjects (cyber law, space) to Parliament — a unitary tilt in India's quasi-federal scheme.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A no-confidence motion requires the support of how many members for admission?
questions.e: Under Rule 198, at least 50 Lok Sabha members must rise in support for a no-confidence motion to be admitted.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The President's rule in a state (Article 356) can initially last for:
questions.e: Proclamation under Article 356 must be approved by Parliament within two months and then lasts six months at a time (extendable to three years with conditions).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which article empowers Parliament to create new states and alter boundaries?
questions.e: Article 3 lets Parliament form new states and alter areas, boundaries or names by simple majority — a key reason India is a 'Union', not a federation.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Directive Principle in Article 40 relates to:
questions.e: Article 40 (Gandhian DPSP) directs the State to organise village panchayats — given teeth by the 73rd Amendment.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Harappan site of Lothal is best known for its:
questions.e: Lothal (Gujarat, S.R. Rao) had the dockyard and bead factory. Great Bath: Mohenjo-daro; ploughed field: Kalibangan; signboard: Dholavira.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Harappan script is:
o: Undeciphered, known from short seal inscriptions
questions.e: The script remains undeciphered — short inscriptions, no bilingual key. Brahmi appears two millennia later in Ashokan edicts.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Who excavated Harappa in 1921?
questions.e: Daya Ram Sahni (1921) at Harappa; R.D. Banerji (1922) at Mohenjo-daro; John Marshall announced the civilisation in 1924.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The largest Harappan site excavated in India is:
questions.e: Rakhigarhi (Hisar, Haryana) is the largest Harappan site in India.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Kalinga war was fought in:
questions.e: 261 BCE (Ashoka's 8th regnal year); the remorse in Major Rock Edict XIII marks his turn to Dhamma.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Arthashastra was composed by:
questions.e: Kautilya (Chanakya), Chandragupta Maurya's minister. Megasthenes wrote the Indica; Panini the Ashtadhyayi (grammar).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Ashokan edicts were deciphered by James Prinsep in:
questions.e: Prinsep's 1837 decipherment of Brahmi unlocked the edicts; the Maski edict names their author as 'Ashoka'.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Third Buddhist Council was convened under:
questions.e: Third Council (~250 BCE) at Pataliputra under Moggaliputta Tissa with Ashoka's patronage. First: Rajgir (Ajatashatru); Fourth: Kashmir (Kanishka).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: In the mansabdari system, 'sawar' indicated:
questions.e: Sawar = horsemen maintained; zat = personal rank/salary. Pay came via jagir (transferable revenue assignments).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The dahsala (zabt) revenue system was systematised under Akbar by:
questions.e: Todar Mal's dahsala (1580) averaged ten years' produce and prices; Abul Fazl documented it in the Ain-i-Akbari.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Din-i-Ilahi was propounded in:
questions.e: 1582 — Akbar's syncretic order under his sulh-i-kul (universal peace) policy; joined by a handful of courtiers.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in 1885 at:
questions.e: Bombay (Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College), presided by W.C. Bonnerjee, 72 delegates; A.O. Hume was the founder-organiser.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Surat split (1907) divided the Congress into:
questions.e: Moderates vs Extremists (Lal-Bal-Pal) over methods after the 1905 Bengal partition; reunited at Lucknow in 1916.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by the:
questions.e: The 1909 reforms conceded separate electorates — the institutional seed of communal electorates, later extended.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on:
questions.e: 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi): General Dyer's firing at Amritsar on a gathering protesting the Rowlatt Act.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after:
questions.e: Chauri Chaura (5 Feb 1922): a mob killed 22 policemen; Gandhi suspended the movement (Bardoli, 12 Feb 1922) on non-violence grounds.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Dandi March began on:
questions.e: 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati; Gandhi reached Dandi on 6 April and broke the salt law — launching Civil Disobedience.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between:
questions.e: 24 September 1932: after Gandhi's fast against the Communal Award, reserved seats for Depressed Classes within joint electorates replaced separate electorates.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: 'Do or Die' was the mantra of the:
questions.e: Gandhi's call at the Bombay AICC session, 8 August 1942, launching Quit India — demanding immediate British withdrawal.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in:
questions.e: March 1946: proposed a three-tier federation; its failure led to Direct Action Day (16 Aug 1946) and the Interim Government (2 Sep 1946).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) provided for:
o: A united India with strong provinces
Partition and transfer of power in August 1947
questions.e: The 3 June Plan accepted partition into India and Pakistan with independence on 15 August 1947; the Radcliffe Award drew the boundaries.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The 'drain theory' was propounded by:
questions.e: Naoroji's Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901) argued Britain drained India's wealth — the economic critique of colonialism.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 at:
questions.e: Founded by Lala Har Dayal and others among Indian immigrants at San Francisco (1913); its journal 'Ghadar' called for armed revolt.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Home Rule Leagues (1916) were led by:
questions.e: Tilak's league (Maharashtra) and Besant's (rest of India) demanded self-government within the Empire; both merged efforts in 1916.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Lucknow Pact (1916) is remembered for:
questions.e: Congress and the Muslim League presented common demands (brokered by Tilak and Jinnah); the Congress wings also reunited.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Rowlatt Act (1919) was opposed because it:
questions.e: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act allowed detention without trial — protested via Gandhi's first all-India satyagraha (April 1919).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The last Mauryan ruler was:
questions.e: Brihadratha (c. 185 BCE), assassinated by his commander Pushyamitra Shunga, founder of the Shunga dynasty.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which Mughal officer handled military pay and recruitment?
questions.e: Mir Bakshi: military administration, pay and the dagh/chehra checks. Mir Saman: imperial household; Sadr-us-Sudur: religious grants.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) resolution was passed at the Congress session held in:
questions.e: The Lahore session (Dec 1929, president Jawaharlal Nehru) declared Purna Swaraj the goal; 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Article 50 of the Constitution directs the State to:
o: Separate the judiciary from the executive
questions.e: Article 50 (liberal–intellectual DPSP): separation of judiciary from executive — the root of judicial independence.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: K2, the highest peak in territory claimed by India, lies in the:
questions.e: K2 (8,611 m) is in the Karakoram (Baltistan, PoK). Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak wholly within India.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The correct southward order of the Northern Plains' belts is:
questions.e: From the foothills: Bhabar (porous) → Terai (marshy) → Bhangar (old alluvium) → Khadar (new floodplain alluvium).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Anamudi, the highest peak of peninsular India, is located in the:
questions.e: Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Anaimalai Hills (Kerala), part of the Western Ghats — higher and more continuous than the Eastern Ghats.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Barren Island, India's only active volcano, is in the:
questions.e: Barren Island (Andaman Sea) is India's only active volcano; the Andaman–Nicobar chain is a volcanic island arc, Lakshadweep coral atolls.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Lakshadweep islands are of:
questions.e: Lakshadweep's 36 islands are coral atolls, distinct from the volcanic Andaman–Nicobar chain.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The south-west monsoon normally arrives in Kerala around:
questions.e: Normal onset ~1 June (the monsoon 'burst'), reaching Mumbai ~10 June and covering India by mid-July.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The south-west monsoon contributes about what share of India's annual rainfall?
questions.e: Roughly 75% falls in June–September — the economic metronome for kharif sowing, reservoirs and food inflation.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Mawsynram gets the world's heaviest rainfall chiefly due to:
o: Orographic lift of Bay-branch winds over the Khasi hills
questions.e: Moist Bay of Bengal branch winds are forced up the Khasi hills, cooling and condensing — classic orographic rainfall.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: El Niño conditions are generally associated with the Indian monsoon being:
questions.e: El Niño (eastern Pacific warming) usually weakens the monsoon; La Niña and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole usually strengthen it.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Tamil Nadu receives most of its rainfall during:
questions.e: The retreating (north-east) monsoon picks up Bay of Bengal moisture and strikes the Coromandel coast in Oct–Dec.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Winter rainfall in northwest India, vital for rabi wheat, comes from:
questions.e: Western disturbances — temperate cyclones from the Mediterranean — bring winter rain and Himalayan snow.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The longest river flowing through India is the:
questions.e: Ganga (2,525 km) has the longest course within India; Indus and Brahmaputra are longer overall but mostly outside India.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The 'Panchnad' tributaries of the Indus are:
questions.e: The five rivers (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) merge and join the Indus in Pakistan.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The 'Sorrow of Bihar' is the:
questions.e: The Kosi's shifting course and floods earned the name; it joins the Ganga in Bihar.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) was brokered by the:
questions.e: World Bank-brokered: eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Inter-state river water disputes are adjudicated under:
questions.e: Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide for adjudication — via the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 and tribunals.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Narmada and Tapi form estuaries (not deltas) because they:
o: Flow through rift valleys carrying less silt
questions.e: Their rift-valley, hard-rock channels carry little silt, so they meet the sea as estuaries — unlike the delta-building east-flowing rivers.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The longest peninsular river, also called 'Dakshin Ganga', is the:
questions.e: Godavari (1,465 km), rising at Trimbak (Maharashtra), is the longest peninsular river.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Majuli, among the world's largest riverine islands, is in the:
questions.e: Majuli (Assam) sits in the Brahmaputra — also a noted centre of Vaishnavite culture.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which river is antecedent — older than the Himalayas it cuts through?
questions.e: The Sutlej (like the Indus and Brahmaputra) predates the Himalayan uplift and cuts through in deep gorges.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: National Income is defined as:
questions.e: NNP at factor cost = GNP − depreciation, at factor cost. Per capita income is this divided by population.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: GDP at factor cost = GDP at market prices minus:
questions.e: Net indirect taxes (indirect taxes − subsidies) bridge market prices and factor cost.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Real GDP is measured:
questions.e: Real GDP uses base-year (2011–12) prices to isolate volume growth; the GDP deflator (nominal/real × 100) captures price change.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The largest contributor to India's Gross Value Added is the:
questions.e: Services contribute over half of GVA, though agriculture still employs the largest share of workers.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: India's national income series currently uses the base year:
questions.e: The 2011–12 series (CSO, now NSO under MoSPI) is current; base years are revised to update the basket.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The RBI was established on:
questions.e: 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934 (Hilton Young Commission); nationalised in 1949.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: India's inflation target is:
questions.e: 4% CPI (Combined) with a 2–6% tolerance band, reviewed every five years; the MPC answers for three straight quarters outside it.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee has:
questions.e: Six members (Governor as chair with casting vote, Deputy Governor, one RBI officer, three government nominees); decisions need four votes.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A repo rate hike by the RBI is expected to:
questions.e: Costlier policy rates → costlier bank credit → slower money and demand growth → lower inflation.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) requires banks to:
o: Park a share of deposits as cash with the RBI
questions.e: CRR: a percentage of net demand and time liabilities kept as cash with the RBI, earning no interest — a direct liquidity tool.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Stagflation means:
questions.e: Stagnation + inflation: rate hikes to fight inflation worsen the slowdown — the policymaker's dilemma.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: CPI (base 2012) differs from WPI (base 2011–12) mainly in that CPI:
o: Tracks retail consumer prices and anchors the inflation target
questions.e: CPI tracks retail prices (NSO) and is the RBI's target variable since 2014; WPI (Office of Economic Adviser) tracks wholesale prices.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Annual Financial Statement (Budget) is laid before Parliament under:
questions.e: Article 112 mandates the Annual Financial Statement each year. Article 265 bars taxation except by law.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Fiscal deficit equals:
o: Total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings
Revenue deficit + grants for capital assets
questions.e: The government's total borrowing requirement. (Revenue expenditure − revenue receipts = revenue deficit; minus interest = primary deficit.)

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The FRBM Act was enacted in:
questions.e: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 (effective 2004); reviewed by the N.K. Singh committee (2017).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: GST was launched on:
questions.e: 1 July 2017, via the 101st Amendment (2016): CGST+SGST intra-state, IGST inter-state, destination-based.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The separate Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget from:
questions.e: From 2017–18 (Bibek Debroy committee), ending the 1924 Acworth-committee legacy; the Budget also moved to 1 February.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Primary deficit =
questions.e: Primary deficit strips out interest on past debt, showing the current year's own fiscal stance.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The GST Council is chaired by the:
questions.e: Article 279A: Union FM chairs; state FMs are members; decisions need a three-fourths majority (Centre holds one-third weight).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.e: Corporation tax falls on the earner and cannot be shifted; GST, customs and excise are indirect (shifted to buyers).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A 'break in the monsoon' occurs when:
o: The monsoon trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills, drying the plains
questions.e: The trough's northward shift parks rain over the hills while the plains go dry for days — a classic monsoon-break pattern.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Chilika, India's largest coastal lagoon, is in:
questions.e: Chilika Lake (Odisha) on the east coast — India's largest brackish-water lagoon and a Ramsar site.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Palghat Gap is a pass in the:
questions.e: The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap breaks the Western Ghats in Kerala, linking Tamil Nadu and Kerala — also a monsoon wind corridor.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which state gets the most from the Bay of Bengal branch's early burst, facing frequent floods?
questions.e: The Bay branch hits the Northeast first; deflected west by the Himalayas, it brings heavy rain and floods to Assam and Bihar.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.e: Eight: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Core inflation excludes:
questions.e: Core strips volatile food and fuel to reveal underlying price trends; headline CPI includes everything.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Open Market Operations by the RBI involve:
o: Buying/selling government securities to adjust liquidity
questions.e: OMOs: RBI buys gilts to inject liquidity, sells to absorb it — a quantitative monetary tool alongside rate moves.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Disinvestment receipts are classified as:
questions.e: Sale of government assets/stakes is a non-debt capital receipt — it reduces assets, unlike borrowing which creates liability.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The reverse repo rate is the rate at which:
o: The RBI lends short-term to banks
Banks park surplus funds with the RBI
Banks lend to each other overnight
The government borrows from the RBI
questions.e: Reverse repo: the RBI absorbs liquidity by paying banks to park funds with it — raising it sucks money out of the system, fighting inflation.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The 'Hindu rate of growth' phrase (Raj Krishna) referred to India's:
questions.e: The ~3.5% annual average of the pre-reform decades — the classic contrast point with post-1991 growth in Mains answers.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The United States announced sanctions on the International Criminal Court on 9 October 2026. The announcement came:
o: hours after the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay
a day after the UN Security Council extended the Gaza ceasefire
alongside the signing of the India-US trade pact
after the ICC opened an investigation into the Gaza conflict
questions.e: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US would 'dismantle' the court 'brick by brick'; a six-month Treasury waiver lets firms wind down dealings. The ICC condemned the move as an assault on the rule of law.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 24th National Maritime Search & Rescue Board meeting (October 2026, Bhubaneswar) was chaired by:
o: DG Paramesh Sivamani, Director General, Indian Coast Guard
questions.e: The meeting preceded SAREX-2026 (7–8 October 2026 off Paradip), the 12th national maritime SAR exercise with 32 observers from 30 countries.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In October 2026, the Kerala Assembly passed a resolution seeking:
o: the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner over SIR irregularities
a referendum on the SIR exercise
the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly
questions.e: The resolution targeted CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, and demanded a CEC selection panel of the PM, LoP and CJI.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: At its 7 October 2026 meeting, the RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee raised the policy repo rate to:
questions.e: On 7 October 2026 the RBI’s MPC unanimously hiked the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% (first hike since February 2023), with SDF at 5.25% and MSF/Bank Rate at 5.75%. The stance moved from neutral to ‘calibrated tightening’ by a 4–2 majority. Real GDP for FY27 was projected at 7.1% and CPI inflation at 5.2%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which policy stance did the RBI MPC adopt at its October 2026 meeting?
questions.e: The MPC changed the policy stance from neutral to ‘calibrated tightening’ by a 4–2 majority on 7 October 2026, signalling that rate cuts are off the table in the near term and future action will be a hike or a pause.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: What real GDP growth projection for FY2026–27 did the RBI announce in October 2026?
questions.e: For FY27 the RBI projected real GDP growth of 7.1% (raised from 6.7%) and CPI inflation of 5.2%. Headline CPI had risen to 4.82% in August 2026, and Q1 FY27 GDP growth was 7.8%.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The controversial additions to the Election Commission’s revised Form 6 (July 2026) require applicants to declare:
questions.e: The revised Form 6 introduced in July 2026 asks new voters to declare ancestry details or linkage to previous SIR rolls on the ECINet portal. On 12 October 2026 the Supreme Court clarified it had neither approved nor disapproved these changes, and will hear challenges on 27 October.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: Which Indo-French satellite, announced for launch within 12–16 months in October 2026, is designed for thermal infrared monitoring of water resources?
questions.e: The Indo-French TRISHNA (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural Resource Assessment) satellite will launch in 12–16 months (announced 11 October 2026 by URSC Director Jasvinder Singh Khoral). It is the third India–France satellite after Megha-Tropiques and SARAL, and will monitor surface temperature for water-resource management.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The appointment of state governors by the President is provided for under:
questions.e: Article 155: the Governor of a State shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. Six states saw governor changes on 12 October 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 13 October 2026 Supreme Court notice to the Centre and ECI concerns a PIL challenging:
o: Blanket immunity to the CEC and ECs under Section 16 of the CEC Act, 2023
The appointment process of the CEC under the 2023 Act
The ECI's model code enforcement powers
questions.e: The PIL challenges blanket immunity granted to the CEC and Election Commissioners under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The International Big Cat Alliance covers seven species. Which of the following is NOT among them?
questions.e: IBCA covers tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. Its HQ at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi, was inaugurated on 12 October 2026; it has 29 member countries.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.q: Under Special Campaign 6.0, what will the Ministry of Panchayati Raj do on 14 October 2026?
o: Conduct a cleanliness drive and dispose of pending cases
Launch a new rural housing scheme
questions.e: On 14 October 2026, the Ministry will conduct a cleanliness drive and dispose of pending cases under Special Campaign 6.0.

questions.subject: International relations
questions.q: The first BIMSTEC Home Ministers' meeting was held in October 2026 in:
questions.e: India hosted the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers' meeting in New Delhi under Home Minister Amit Shah (13 October 2026).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: How many member states does BIMSTEC have, all of whose interior ministers adopted the Delhi Declaration in October 2026?
questions.e: BIMSTEC has seven member states; their interior ministers unanimously adopted the Delhi Declaration at the 1st Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Governor of a state appointed by the President?
questions.e: Article 155 provides that the Governor of a state shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Who received the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize?
questions.e: South African jurist Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India’s trade deficit with China in 2026 has:
questions.e: India’s trade deficit with China crossed $100 billion in 2026, per China’s General Administration of Customs data released 14 October 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The RBI’s monetary policy stance since 7 October 2026 is:
questions.e: The MPC moved the stance from neutral to calibrated tightening, signalling rate cuts are off the table in the near term.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: On which date did UPSC declare the NDA & NA Examination (II) 2026 written result?
questions.e: The written result was declared on 9 October 2026; the written examination itself was held on 13 September 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: How many vacancies are to be filled through the NDA & NA Examination (II) 2026?
questions.e: A total of 394 vacancies were announced across the Army, Navy, Air Force wings and the Naval Academy (15 Oct 2026).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who has been appointed Deputy Election Commissioner with tenure until 8 April 2030?
questions.e: Prakash Rajpurohit, a 2010-batch Rajasthan-cadre IAS officer, was appointed Deputy Election Commissioner (Oct 2026).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who was appointed Governor of Karnataka on 12 October 2026?
questions.e: Dr Sudha Yadav was appointed Governor of Karnataka on 12 October 2026, succeeding Thawar Chand Gehlot.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, which completed five years in October 2026, was launched on:
questions.e: Launched on 13 October 2021, the plan completed five years on 13 October 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), continued by the Cabinet on 15 October 2026 with a ₹53,428 crore outlay, is best located constitutionally under which part of the Constitution?
o: Federal distribution of powers under the Seventh Schedule
questions.e: The Cabinet approved continuation of NSAP for 2026–27 to 2030–31 with ₹53,428 crore on 15 October 2026. NSAP operationalises Article 41, the Directive Principle directing the State to secure the right to work, education and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls — now under Supreme Court examination after the 12 October 2026 petition by INDIA bloc leaders — is carried out under the constitutional authority vested in the Election Commission by:
questions.e: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections in the Election Commission. The SIR is a revision of electoral rolls carried out under the Commission's powers under Article 324 read with the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The acceptance of Dr L Murugan's resignation from the Union Council of Ministers by the President on 15 October 2026 on the PM's advice was made under:
questions.e: Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister under Article 75(1) and hold office during the pleasure of the President under Article 75(2); the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the House of the People is under Article 75(3).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The RBI's shift to a 'calibrated tightening' stance in its October 2026 policy most accurately implies which of the following?
o: Guarantees another rate hike at the next meeting
Takes near-term rate cuts off the table while future moves stay data-dependent
Automatically raises all lending rates by 25 bps
questions.e: 'Calibrated tightening' — adopted after the unanimous 25 bps repo hike to 5.50% on 7 October 2026 — means the MPC sees near-term rate cuts as off the table but will calibrate future action (hike or pause) to evolving inflation and growth data.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which transaction was approved by the Union Cabinet on 15 October 2026 as the country's biggest financial-sector foreign direct investment, worth ₹52,878 crore?
questions.e: The ₹52,878 crore Fairfax–IDBI Bank deal approved by the Cabinet on 15 October 2026 was described as the country's biggest financial-sector FDI, reducing the government's stake to 15% and LIC's to 19%.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: CJI Surya Kant said on 15 October 2026 that the Supreme Court will soon take a decision on the plea concerning which of the following?
o: Recall of the CEC law order
