The SIR of Delhi's electoral rolls
questions.e: On 15 October 2026 CJI Surya Kant said the Supreme Court will soon decide on the plea to recall the CEC law order; the Court also agreed to examine the SIR of Delhi's electoral rolls and the validity of the revised Form 6.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: A Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan directed that travel insurance, identical to that on online bookings, be made mandatory on offline counter tickets at every railway station from 27 October 2026. The directive was issued by:
questions.e: The Supreme Court issued the mandatory directive; railway authorities must implement it from 27 October 2026.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 298-km Nimmu–Padum–Darcha road, dedicated on 15 October 2026, connects Nimmu in Leh with Darcha in Himachal Pradesh. It passes through which valley?
questions.e: The road runs through the Zanskar Valley, providing an alternative corridor to Ladakh alongside the Srinagar–Leh and Manali–Leh highways and strengthening strategic mobility for the armed forces.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: September 2026 WPI inflation (11.39%) is the highest in the 'revised series'. The revised Wholesale Price Index series uses which base year?
questions.e: The government introduced the revised WPI series with 2022-23 as base year in June 2026; historical data exists from April 2023. The August 2022 reading of 12.48% was on the old 2011-12 base and is not directly comparable.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the RBI's October 2026 bi-monthly monetary policy: (1) The MPC raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50%. (2) The stance was changed from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening'. (3) CPI inflation for FY27 was projected at 5.2%. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct: the MPC raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% (first hike since February 2023), shifted stance to 'calibrated tightening', and projected FY27 CPI inflation at 5.2% (GDP growth 7.1%). The vote on the rate decision was unanimous. (Dated: 7 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: With reference to the RBI's liquidity management measures in October 2026, consider the following: (1) The minimum daily CRR maintenance was raised to 99% of the prescribed requirement. (2) An OMO sale of ₹25,000 crore of government securities was announced on 13 October. Which are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Daily CRR maintenance rose to 99% from the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026, and the RBI announced a ₹25,000 crore OMO sale on 13 October to align overnight rates with the repo rate and absorb surplus liquidity. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: IBSAMAR is a trilateral maritime exercise involving India and which two other countries? Its ninth edition (IBSAMAR IX) is being held in October 2026 with participation of INS Tarkash.
questions.e: IBSAMAR is the India–Brazil–South Africa maritime exercise. Its ninth edition is being held in South Africa in October 2026 with the Indian Navy's INS Tarkash participating. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Who will assume charge as the Chief of the Air Staff on 31 October 2026, as reported in October 2026?
questions.e: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit becomes Chief of the Air Staff on 31 October 2026. The same reports noted the India–UAE exercise Mountain Guardian 2026 (Chaubatia, Uttarakhand) ends on 18 October. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Canada on 11–12 December 2026. Who is the Prime Minister of Canada with whom Modi recently discussed strengthening bilateral ties?
questions.e: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney held a recent conversation with PM Modi; both agreed to build momentum in trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people relations ahead of the 11–12 December 2026 visit. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: Regarding India's planned AI regulation framework announced in October 2026, which of the following are stated components? (1) A consultation paper within about a month covering AI safety, humanity, skilling and inclusivity. (2) Empanelment of AI models for government use. (3) A three-to-four-year roadmap for GPUs for AI inference.
questions.e: All three were stated by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw at a World Bank event: a consultation paper on AI in about a month, empanelment of AI models eligible for government use, and a three-to-four-year GPU roadmap for AI inference. (Dated: 10 Oct 2026)

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following wetlands were designated Ramsar sites on 15 October 2026?
questions.e: Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh) were designated Ramsar sites on 15 October 2026, taking India's tally to 103.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The RBI shifted its monetary policy stance in October 2026 from 'neutral' to:
questions.e: The MPC changed the stance to 'calibrated tightening' on 7 October 2026 while hiking the repo rate to 5.50%, signalling that rate cuts are off the table in the near term.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The October 2026 Supreme Court ruling on conversion and reservation held that conversion to a non-Hindu religion:
o: Does not automatically entitle a person to affirmative action under Article 16(4) based on pre-conversion status
Confers OBC status automatically in all states
Requires a fresh caste certificate from the district magistrate
questions.e: The Court held that a person converting from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order cannot claim affirmative action under Article 16(4) merely on the basis of the social backwardness associated with pre-conversion status.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India proposed BS-VII emission standards with effect from:
questions.e: India proposed Bharat Stage-VII emission standards to be implemented from April 2029, as announced on 15 October 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Election Commission announced a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in how many states and Union Territories in October 2026?
questions.e: On 15 October 2026 the Election Commission announced that Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls would be conducted in 17 states and Union Territories, including those where assembly polls are due next year.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Shri Sudhakar Malli was appointed Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India with effect from 1 October 2026. Which department does he oversee?
questions.e: RBI Press Release 2026-2027/1241 states Shri Sudhakar Malli, a career central banker, looks after the Department of Supervision (Supervisory Assessment).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford. The citation honoured their work on which theme?
questions.e: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded Hall and Woodford the 2026 Economics Prize 'for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation'.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: As per the UPSC CSE 2026 notification, which of the following candidates CANNOT appear in CSE 2026?
o: A candidate appointed to the IPS from an earlier CSE
A candidate already appointed to the IAS from an earlier CSE and continuing in the service
A final-year graduate with no prior attempt
A candidate who appeared in CSE 2025 but was not selected
questions.e: The CSE 2026 notification bars absolutely any candidate already appointed to the IAS or IFS from an earlier CSE from appearing at all; if such an appointment happens after Prelims 2026, they cannot write Mains. IPS appointees from an earlier CSE may appear but cannot opt for IPS again.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: How many vacancies were notified in the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2026?
questions.e: CSE 2026 notified 933 vacancies, compared with 979 in CSE 2025 and 1,105 filled through CSE 2024.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following is a NEW requirement in the UPSC CSE 2026 application process?
o: Submission of the form only by post
Mandatory live photograph capture via webcam or phone camera during application
Physical verification at the UPSC office before applying
Submission of the Class 12 marksheet at the Prelims stage
questions.e: CSE 2026 introduced a four-stage online process (OTR, main form, DAF with service preferences, fee/documents/centre) with mandatory live photo capture to prevent fraud, plus a signature upload in JPG (20–300 KB).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Supreme Court's 15 October 2026 judgment setting aside the write-down of Yes Bank's Additional Tier-1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore was reported under which citation?
questions.e: Yes Bank Ltd. v. Axis Trustee Services Ltd., 2026 INSC 1132, decided 15 October 2026 by Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih, dismissed appeals by Yes Bank, the RBI and the Union of India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In October 2026 the Supreme Court held that private citizens can file criminal complaints for false election affidavits under which provision?
o: Section 123, Representation of the People Act
Section 125A, Representation of the People Act
Section 126, Representation of the People Act
questions.e: On 16 October 2026 the Court held a private complaint alleging an offence under Section 125A of the RoP Act, 1951 need not pass the rigours of Section 195 CrPC.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: What does the RBI's shift to a 'calibrated tightening' stance in October 2026 signal about the next policy move?
o: Rate cuts are on the table
The next move will be either another hike or a pause
The repo rate will be cut by 50 bps
The stance has no forward guidance
questions.e: The MPC changed the stance from neutral to 'calibrated tightening' by a 4–2 vote, taking rate cuts off the table for now: the next move will be either another hike or a pause.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: SRIA, provisions of which were waived by the US President on 17 October 2026, stands for:
o: Special Relief for International Allies Act
questions.e: The Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act empowered tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil and gas; the 17 October 2026 waiver pauses enforcement for 60 days.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Supreme Court's 17 October 2026 judgment barring the Tamil Nadu government from accepting temple land as a gift turned on which statute?
o: Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1959
Tamil Nadu Inam Estates Abolition Act, 1963
questions.e: The Court held the transfer violated the TN HR&CE Act, 1959, declared the 2017 gift deed illegal, and ordered Rs 31,000 monthly rent. Bench: Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: Against how many notified vacancies was the Civil Services Examination 2026 held?
questions.e: CSE 2026 was notified for approximately 933 vacancies; 13,343 candidates qualified the prelims.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: The UPSC CSE Mains 2026 written result is expected in which period?
questions.e: Following the 60-75 day pattern of recent cycles (CSE 2025 took 72 days), the Mains 2026 result is expected in early to mid-November 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In September 2026, which body directed the UPSC to publish paper-wise marks for the Civil Services Main Examination 2026?
o: The Department of Personnel and Training
questions.e: The CIC directed disclosure of detailed marks to ensure transparency and fairness, noting no record existed to justify discontinuing publication from 2018.

questions.subject: Current affairs
questions.q: What are the maximum marks for the written papers and the Personality Test respectively in the Civil Services Examination final merit?
questions.e: The final merit is drawn from 2,025 marks: 1,750 for the Mains written papers and 275 for the Personality Test.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Following the RBI's October 2026 monetary policy, the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate stand at:
questions.e: The 25 bps repo hike to 5.50% adjusted the SDF to 5.25% and the MSF rate and Bank Rate to 5.75%. The hike was the first since February 2023.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The RBI's October 2026 shift to a 'calibrated tightening' stance was adopted on what MPC vote?
questions.e: The stance change to 'calibrated tightening' was adopted 4-2; Dr Nagesh Kumar and Prof Ram Singh wanted to retain 'neutral'. The rate hike itself was unanimous. The stance means rate cuts are off the table - the next move can only be a hike or a pause.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, which aims to double bilateral trade in goods and services, comes into force on:
questions.e: Announced by Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal on 19 October 2026, the FTA takes effect on 20 October 2026, giving Indian goods 100% duty-free access to New Zealand while excluding dairy, sugar, edible oils and most animal meat.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: As per the UPSC 2027 annual calendar, the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination 2027 is scheduled for:
questions.e: CSE Prelims 2027: notification 13 January 2027, applications close 2 February, Prelims 23 May 2027, Mains from 20 August 2027. 11 April 2027 is the date for NDA & NA (I) and CDS (I) 2027.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: For the FY27 ethanol tender, the government has decided to:
o: Exclude sugar-based ethanol and cut the maize incentive
questions.e: The FY27 tender (supply year Nov 2026-Oct 2027) excludes sugar-based ethanol and cuts the maize incentive; grain feedstocks (maize, rice) will carry the E20 programme.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which two MPC members wanted the policy stance retained at 'neutral' in October 2026?
o: Dr Nagesh Kumar and Prof Ram Singh
Governor Sanjay Malhotra and the Deputy Governor
questions.e: Dr Nagesh Kumar and Prof Ram Singh favoured retaining 'neutral'; the majority (4-2) adopted 'calibrated tightening'. All six members voted unanimously for the 25 bps repo hike itself.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: With reference to the IndiaAI Mission's compute expansion announced in October 2026, consider the following statements: 1. MeitY tendered 10,000 AI compute units on 19 October 2026. 2. Over 38,000 GPUs had already been empanelled under the Mission. 3. Bids were invited from foreign data centres. Which statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the 19 October 2026 RFE seeks 10,000 compute units on top of 38,000+ empanelled GPUs. Statement 3 is incorrect - each cluster of 512+ units must sit in an Indian data centre.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In October 2026 (2026 INSC 1149), a Supreme Court Bench of Justices J. B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran held in Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish that:
o: The right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right under Articles 21 and 19(1)(a), extending to children
Internet access is only a statutory right under the IT Act, 2000
Children below 14 have no right to internet access
questions.e: The Court declared internet access a standalone fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a), expressly extending it to children of all ages while ordering proportionate safeguards against child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the India-New Zealand FTA mobility provisions (in force 20 October 2026), India receives:
o: 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas and 1,000 Working Holiday visas per year
10,000 permanent residency slots for Indian workers
Visa-free travel for Indian business visitors
5,000 student visas with no work rights
questions.e: The FTA gives 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas for skilled Indians, 1,000 Working Holiday visas every year, post-study work rights up to 3 years for STEM graduates and up to 4 years for doctoral scholars.

questions.subject: GS-2
questions.q: Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (false statements in election affidavits) was inserted in:
questions.e: The SC bench (Dipankar Datta & Sheel Nagu, 16 Oct 2026) noted Section 125A was inserted in 2002 while Section 195 CrPC was amended in 2006 — and Parliament's omission of 125A from the Section 195 list was deliberate, so private complaints are maintainable.

questions.subject: GS-2
questions.q: Which authority fixes the number of judges of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.e: Under Article 124(1), the number of Supreme Court judges is fixed by Parliament by law — not by constitutional amendment. The 2026 amendment raised the sanctioned strength from 34 to 38 (including the CJI).

questions.subject: GS-2
questions.q: After the swearing-in of three new judges on 6 October 2026, the working strength of the Supreme Court of India is:
questions.e: With the 6 October 2026 oath of Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh (administered by CJI Surya Kant), the Court's working strength is 37 against a sanctioned strength of 38 — one vacancy.

questions.subject: GS-2
questions.q: India and Canada are targeting the conclusion of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by:
questions.e: India and Canada signed commercial agreements in October 2026 with both sides targeting CEPA conclusion by December 2026.

questions.subject: GS-2
questions.q: Which constitutional provision protects the right to assemble peaceably and without arms, as reiterated by the Supreme Court in its October 2026 protest ruling?
questions.e: The bench of CJI Surya Kant (9 Oct 2026) held that restrictions on protest must be proportionate — authorities 'can't shut down an entire city' — grounding the right in Article 19(1)(b) (assemble peaceably and without arms).

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Tarang Shakti 2026, in which Defence Minister Rajnath Singh called for self-reliance in Tejas and Akash, was held at which station?
questions.e: Tarang Shakti 2026 was held at Jodhpur Air Force Station, with 32 observer nations; the Defence Minister pressed for self-reliance in indigenous platforms such as Tejas, Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand and Akash.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.q: Under Section 145(2) of the Railways Act (as amended by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026), playing audio on speaker mode causing public nuisance attracts which penalty?
questions.e: Section 145(2) provides for a Rs 1,000 fine and ticket forfeiture for public nuisance; continued nuisance can attract six months' simple imprisonment or a Rs 5,000 fine.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.q: The national governance committee for India's proposed National Electricity Data Sharing Framework (October 2026) is to be headed by whom?
o: The Chairperson of the Central Electricity Authority
questions.e: Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal announced on 14 October 2026 that the framework's national data governance committee will be led by the Chairperson of the Central Electricity Authority.

questions.subject: Governance
questions.q: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education that proposed sweeping NTA reforms in its 382nd report (October 2026) is chaired by whom?
questions.e: The 382nd report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, chaired by Mukul Wasnik, proposed NTA accountability to Parliament, a phased NEET-UG move to CBT, and permanent test centres in every district.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under which constitutional provisions did the Supreme Court (Oct 2026) recognise internet access as a fundamental right?
questions.e: In Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish (2026 INSC 1149, 15 Oct 2026), Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran held the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) — for children too. Blanket denial in the name of safety was held unreasonable.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: What does the RBI's October 2026 “calibrated tightening” stance signal about future rate action?
o: Rate cuts are certain within two quarters
The repo rate is frozen for a year
Cuts are off the table; the next move is a hike or a pause
The stance has no signalling value
questions.e: “Calibrated tightening” (adopted 4–2 in Oct 2026, replacing neutral) signals that rate cuts are off the table: the next move will be either another hike or a pause, depending on growth–inflation dynamics. Repo: 5.50%; SDF 5.25%; MSF/Bank Rate 5.75%.

questions.subject: Security
questions.q: Which is India's only tri-services command, currently conducting the aerial firing exercise near Sri Vijaya Puram?
questions.e: The Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC), headquartered at Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), is India's only tri-services theatre command — integrating the Navy, Army, Air Force and Coast Guard. It conducted the 20–22 Oct 2026 aerial firing exercise and earlier Exercise Dweep Shakti (Mar 2026).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: According to the RBI's October 2026 policy report, which combination drove the food-price surge?
questions.e: The RBI's October 2026 Monetary Policy Report attributes food inflation to a 13% cumulative deficit in the southwest monsoon plus El Niño conditions — sharply raising sugar and onion prices — alongside crude at $114–116/barrel from West Asia escalation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Centaurus X-3, in the news after an RRI study (Oct 2026), is best described as a:
questions.e: Centaurus X-3 is a high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB): a highly magnetised neutron star (pulsar) accreting matter from a companion more than 10 times the Sun's mass, ~24,000 light years away in Centaurus. RRI researchers (Oct 2026) found it accretes via an accretion disk — rare for its class.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The SC's October 2026 ruling on converts claiming Backward Class Muslim status turned on which Article?
questions.e: The Supreme Court (15 Oct 2026) held that converting from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu one does not transfer backwardness-based claims: affirmative action under Article 16(4) (reservation in public employment) cannot be claimed merely on pre-conversion social status.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: China's fresh global export restrictions on tunnel boring machines (TBMs), announced in October 2026, take effect from:
questions.e: China's Commerce and Industry Ministry announced the curbs in October 2026, effective 18 November 2026, requiring export licences for TBMs as dual-use items.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which Indian infrastructure project is most directly affected by China's TBM export curbs announced in October 2026?
questions.e: The 508-km Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (bullet train) corridor, which includes a 7-km undersea tunnel, is the project most directly hit by the curbs on the 3,000-tonne tunnel boring machines.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In the Secretary to Government v. Sameer Ahamed N. ruling upheld by the Supreme Court, which state's 9 March 2024 Government Order on religious conversion and reservation was invalidated by the Madras High Court?
questions.e: The Supreme Court upheld the Madras High Court verdict invalidating Tamil Nadu's 9 March 2024 GO, which had permitted converts to Islam from BC/MBC/Denotified/SC communities to seek Backward Class Muslim certificates.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Who was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, announced on 9 October 2026?
questions.e: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law — cited for ensuring war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Navi Pillay, the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, served as the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights during:
questions.e: Navi Pillay was UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014. She also served as judge on the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court, and is currently an ICJ judge in the Myanmar genocide case.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Election Commission announced the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in 17 states and Union Territories. Why was SSR 2026 skipped?
o: After the June 2025 Special Intensive Revision (SIR) rolls were prepared afresh
questions.e: After announcing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in June 2025 — where rolls were prepared afresh requiring all electors to re-establish eligibility — the EC did not conduct SSR 2026. The routine annual exercise with 1 January as qualifying date resumes now in 17 states/UTs.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The UPSC CDS (II) 2026 written result, declared on 19 October 2026, shortlisted how many candidates for SSB interviews, and for how many total vacancies?
questions.e: 8,956 candidates qualified the CDS (II) 2026 written exam for 451 vacancies (IMA 100, INA 26, AFA 32, OTA Men 275, OTA Women 18).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In the CDS (II) 2026 vacancy distribution, which academy has the largest share?
questions.e: OTA Men has 275 of the 451 CDS (II) 2026 vacancies — the largest share, followed by IMA (100).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: After the NDA & NA (II) 2026 written result (9 October 2026), qualified candidates must:
o: Report to their nearest Army unit immediately
Register on joinindianarmy.nic.in within two weeks for SSB interview dates
Appear directly at the SSB centre without registration
Wait for a postal call letter only
questions.e: Qualified candidates must register on joinindianarmy.nic.in within two weeks of the result to be allotted SSB interview dates; courses begin 1 July 2027.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: As per UPSC's 2027 examination calendar, the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination 2027 is scheduled on:
questions.e: The CSE Prelims 2027 is scheduled on 23 May 2027 per UPSC's Programme of Examinations 2027.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The notification for NDA & NA (I) and CDS (I) 2027 will be issued on 2 December 2026. The last date for applications is:
questions.e: UPSC's 2027 calendar fixes the NDA/CDS (I) 2027 notice for 2 December 2026 with the last date on 22 December 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The UPSC APFC 2026 recruitment test (80 posts) is scheduled on 20 December 2026. Its scheme is:
o: Descriptive paper only, no negative marking
2-hour objective paper, 1/3 negative marking, 75:25 weightage with interview
questions.e: The APFC RT is a 2-hour objective paper with 1/3 negative marking and a 75:25 weightage between the written test and the interview.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) was recently expanded by DPIIT. Which of the following is NOT part of the expansion?
o: 100% coverage for all loans up to ₹20 crore
Annual guarantee fee cut to 1% for 27 Champion Sectors
Maximum cover per borrower doubled to ₹20 crore
85% coverage for loans up to ₹10 crore
questions.e: CGSS covers 85% for loans up to ₹10 crore and 75% above it — not 100%. The cover ceiling doubled to ₹20 crore and the AGF was cut from 2% to 1% for 27 Champion Sectors under Make in India.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.q: The Delhi Declaration was adopted at which first-ever meeting held in New Delhi in October 2026?
questions.e: The first BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting concluded in New Delhi in October 2026 with the adoption of the Delhi Declaration.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.q: The new DRDO missile testing range at Junput is located in which state?
questions.e: Junput is in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district; a NOTAM notified test activity over the Bay of Bengal from 6 to 9 October 2026 — the first disclosed test window at the facility, which complements the ITR at Chandipur, Odisha.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.q: Under DRDO's Project Kusha, the M2 interceptor has a range of:
questions.e: Project Kusha fields three interceptors: M1 (150 km, maiden flight 23 July 2026), M2 (250 km, trials expected November/December 2026) and M3 (350–400 km).

questions.subject: Governance
questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years covering which period?
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme from 2026-27 to 2030-31.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: In October 2026 the Maharashtra government ordered a revamp of Women and Child Development schemes. Which of these is a feature of the order?
o: Abolition of the Lek Ladki Yojana
Merger of Poshan Tracker with Aadhaar
Four schemes discontinued to avoid duplication
questions.e: The 16 October 2026 order discontinues four schemes to avoid duplication, moves Lek Ladki applications online to MahaDBT, and uses Poshan Tracker and DigiLocker with automated identity and bank verification.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI hikes repo rate to 5.50%, shifts stance to ‘calibrated tightening’ (7 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee met on 5–7 October 2026 and unanimously raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% — the first hike since February 2023 — with immediate effect (circular RBI/2026-27/282 dated 7 October 2026). The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate is now 5.25% and the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and Bank Rate 5.75%. The stance shifted from neutral to ‘calibrated tightening’ (4–2 majority), signalling rate cuts are off the table. Governor Sanjay Malhotra cited West Asia conflict-driven crude volatility and food/fuel/fertiliser pressures. Real GDP growth for FY27 is projected at 7.1% (up from 6.7%) and CPI inflation at 5.2%; headline CPI was 4.82% in August 2026.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Supreme Court on Form 6: no adjudication yet; hearing on 27 October (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: On 12 October 2026, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana clarified the Supreme Court had “neither approved nor disapproved” the Election Commission’s revised Form 6 (voter registration), noting its May 27, 2026 Bihar SIR judgment (Association for Democratic Reforms v. ECI, 2026 INSC 564) pre-dated the July 2026 changes that added ancestry/roll-linkage declarations. “Do not put words in our mouth,” the bench said, countering the ECI’s claim of judicial approval. Petitions challenging the form will be heard on 27 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Indo-French TRISHNA satellite to launch in 12–16 months (11 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: TRISHNA (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural Resource Assessment), the third satellite jointly developed by India and France after Megha-Tropiques and SARAL, is in an advanced stage of realisation and will launch in 12–16 months, URSC Director (Projects) Jasvinder Singh Khoral announced on 11 October 2026. ISRO builds the bus while France’s CNES delivers payloads; data will be processed jointly with an open-data policy. Its mission: high-resolution monitoring of Earth’s surface temperature, emissivity and biophysical variables for water-resource management. Launch vehicle: PSLV.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Prizes 2026 — full winners list (5–12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The 2026 Nobel Prizes, announced 5–12 October: Medicine — Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel (light-gated ion channels, optogenetics); Physics — Francis Halzen (IceCube Neutrino Observatory, high-energy cosmic neutrinos); Chemistry — Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai (non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric synthesis); Literature — Anne Carson (Canada); Peace — Navanethem “Navi” Pillay (South Africa), for promoting peace and international law; Economic Sciences (12 Oct) — Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation). Prize money: 12 million Swedish kronor. Award ceremonies on 10 December, Alfred Nobel’s death anniversary.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Governor reshuffle across six states (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu reshuffled governors on 12 October 2026: Braj Mohan Ram to Odisha, Dr Sudha Yadav to Karnataka, Dr Dhal Singh Bisen to Uttarakhand, Dushyant Gautam to Sikkim; Om Prakash Mathur moved from Sikkim to Kerala and Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar became Governor of Tamil Nadu. Effective on assumption of charge (Article 155).

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Odisha Cabinet decisions (13 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Chaired by CM Mohan Charan Majhi on 13 October 2026, the Odisha Cabinet approved free textbooks for ~28.7 lakh Class 9-10 students in government and aided secondary schools (five years, 2025-26 to 2029-30, Rs 284.07 crore; SC/ST students were already covered) and a Rs 500-crore urban drainage programme against flooding.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: India-Czech defence industrial cooperation (13 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Czech First Deputy PM Karel Havlicek in New Delhi on 13 October 2026, agreeing to expand defence industrial cooperation including joint ventures via the India-Czech Joint Defence Committee, in line with Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

capsules.subject: International Relations
capsules.title: Delhi Declaration adopted at 1st BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting
capsules.body: Interior ministers of all seven BIMSTEC member states met in New Delhi under the chairmanship of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and unanimously adopted the Delhi Declaration, formalising regional counter-terror intelligence sharing, joint border policing mechanisms, and common protocols to interdict maritime smuggling and cross-border cyber financial fraud across the Bay of Bengal.

capsules.subject: International Relations
capsules.title: India–US trade deal nearing ‘landing point’: Jaishankar
capsules.body: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said in October 2026 that India and the US continue to engage to iron out differences on the proposed trade deal, with negotiations heading towards a ‘landing point’, while the core fundamentals of the bilateral strategic partnership remain unchanged.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls reaches the Supreme Court
capsules.body: In October 2026 AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi moved the Supreme Court challenging the manner of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls; the Court agreed to hear the plea with other pending petitions. Separately, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 10 opposition leaders moved the top court against alleged malpractices in the SIR process.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Dr Sudha Yadav appointed Governor of Karnataka
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu appointed Dr Sudha Yadav as Governor of Karnataka on 12 October 2026, succeeding Thawar Chand Gehlot (in office since July 2021). Under Article 155 of the Constitution, the Governor of a state is appointed by the President.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Prakash Rajpurohit appointed Deputy Election Commissioner
capsules.body: Prakash Rajpurohit, a 2010-batch Rajasthan-cadre IAS officer, has been appointed Deputy Election Commissioner until 8 April 2030, as the Centre approved 27 appointments at joint secretary and equivalent levels (Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Dr Sudha Yadav appointed Governor of Karnataka
capsules.body: President Droupadi Murmu appointed Dr Sudha Yadav as the Governor of Karnataka on 12 October 2026. She succeeds Thawar Chand Gehlot, who had held the office since July 2021 (15 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: NSAP continued for 2026–31 with ₹53,428 crore outlay (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet on 15 October 2026 approved the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored National Social Assistance Programme for 2026–27 to 2030–31 with a total outlay of ₹53,428 crore. NSAP provides monthly pensions and lump-sum assistance to elderly persons, widows and persons with severe disabilities below the poverty line — operationalising the Directive Principle in Article 41 (right to work, education and public assistance in old age, sickness and disablement).

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: MHA demography panel launches portal for public inputs (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The demography panel set up by the Ministry of Home Affairs launched a portal on 15 October 2026 inviting government bodies, members of the public, NGOs and even international organisations to submit inputs on 'frequent demographic changes in the country', preferably post-2011. The move raises federal, census and rights-related dimensions relevant to GS Paper II.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: SC to examine SIR of Delhi electoral rolls; Form 6 under scrutiny (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Supreme Court agreed on 15 October 2026 to examine the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Delhi's electoral rolls. A petition by Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, filed 12 October 2026, seeks access to the Commission's records, an independent audit of voter-database changes, a bar on voter removal without notice and a fair hearing, and a halt to the revision until the court decides. The Court also said it would examine the validity of the revised Form 6.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: India–China trade deficit crosses $100 billion in 2026
capsules.body: Fresh customs data reported on 15 October 2026 shows India's trade deficit with China has crossed $100 billion in 2026, even as Indian exports to China grew 40% in the first nine months. The data is a staple for GS Paper III questions on external sector vulnerability and trade policy.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Yes Bank AT-1 verdict: SC overturns ₹8,415-crore bond write-off (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Supreme Court delivered its final decision overturning the ₹8,415 crore Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bond write-off at Yes Bank, with analysts flagging potential balance-sheet and capital-adequacy pressure on the lender. AT-1 bonds are perpetual instruments banks use to shore up capital under Basel III. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: International Relations
capsules.title: Rajnath Singh to represent India at SCO heads-of-government summit (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will represent India at the SCO heads-of-government summit, as reported by The Hindu. The SCO is a Eurasian political, economic and security organisation; India's engagement includes counter-terrorism cooperation under its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Ramsar sites rise to 103
capsules.body: On 15 October 2026 India added Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh's first Ramsar site, a peri-urban reservoir at the foothills of the Outer Himalayas on the Central Asian Flyway) and Sauj Jheel (a shallow lake in the Ganga floodplain, Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh — the district's second Ramsar site after Saman Bird Sanctuary), taking the tally from 101 to 103.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: SC: conversion does not preserve BC reservation
capsules.body: A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar dismissed the Tamil Nadu government's challenge and upheld the Madras High Court's striking down of a 2024 state order that permitted converts to Islam from certain backward communities to claim community certificates as members of notified Backward Class Muslim communities. The ruling has wide implications for reservation jurisprudence under Articles 15(4) and 16(4).

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: BS-VII emission standards proposed from April 2029
capsules.body: India proposed Bharat Stage-VII emission standards from April 2029, with a notified timeline and key features announced on 15 October 2026 — a major development for GS Paper 3 (environment, infrastructure) and prelims, where emission standards are a recurring question area.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: EC orders Special Summary Revision in 17 states/UTs
capsules.body: The Election Commission announced on 15 October 2026 that Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls will be conducted in 17 states and Union Territories, including those where assembly polls are due next year — relevant for polity questions on electoral processes and voter-list revision under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: Nobel Peace Prize 2026: Navi Pillay — Verified: 17 Oct 2026
capsules.body: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded on 9 October 2026 to South African jurist Navanetham (Navi) Pillay, of Tamil origin, for her efforts to promote peace and international law. Pillay served as a judge of the ICTR (1995–2003), as an ICC judge (2003–2012), and as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (2008–2014).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI's senior leadership churn: three new Executive Directors — Verified: 17 Oct 2026
capsules.body: RBI appointed Sudhakar Malli as Executive Director from 1 October 2026 to head the Department of Supervision (Supervisory Assessment). In September 2026 it had appointed Suman Ray as ED (Deposit Insurance & Credit Guarantee Corporation and Premises Department), and in August 2026 Monisha Chakraborty as ED (Foreign Exchange Department and Financial Markets Regulation Department).

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: UPSC CSE 2026: 933 vacancies; new 4-stage application and eligibility bars
capsules.body: The UPSC CSE 2026 notification announced 933 vacancies (979 in 2025; 1,105 in 2024). New this cycle: a four-stage application process — Part-I One-Time Registration, Part-II main application form, Part-III Detailed Application Form with service preferences, and Part-IV fee payment, document upload and centre selection — along with mandatory live photo capture (webcam/phone) and a signature upload in JPG (20–300 KB). Eligibility was tightened: candidates already appointed to the IAS or IFS from an earlier CSE cannot appear at all; IPS appointees may appear but cannot opt for IPS again; and a one-time improvement attempt linked to training exemption is allowed in CSE-2027.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: UPSC Advt 11/2026: 212 posts; applications closed 2 Oct
capsules.body: UPSC's Advertisement 11/2026 covered 212 vacancies: 140 Assistant Public Prosecutor (Delhi), 60 Specialist Grade-III Assistant Professor (General Medicine), 4 Specialist Grade-III Assistant Professor (Anatomy), 2 Assistant Editor, 1 Specialist Grade-II each in Anaesthesiology and Pediatrics, and 4 Public Law Officer/District Litigation Officer/Law Officer posts for the UT of Ladakh. Applications ran 12 September–2 October 2026 (Ladakh law posts till 9 October 2026); fee ₹25 for General/OBC/EWS.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: UPSC APFC recruitment test on 20 December 2026
capsules.body: The UPSC's Special Advertisement 52/2026 notified 80 Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner (APFC) posts. The Recruitment Test is scheduled for 20 December 2026: a 2-hour objective paper with one-third negative marking, carrying 75% weightage against 25% for the interview. Applications closed on 11 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Yes Bank AT-1 bonds: SC sets aside Rs 8,415 crore write-down
capsules.body: On 15 October 2026 (Yes Bank Ltd. v. Axis Trustee Services Ltd., 2026 INSC 1132), the Supreme Court dismissed appeals by Yes Bank, the RBI and the Union of India against the Bombay High Court's decision setting aside the write-down of Yes Bank's Additional Tier-1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore. The Court held the write-down could not be sustained once the final Reconstruction Scheme omitted a write-down provision — administrative action in bank reconstruction must stay within statutory and scheme authority. Bench: Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Private complaints allowed over false election affidavits
capsules.body: On 16 October 2026, the Supreme Court held that private citizens can file criminal complaints against candidates who furnish false information in election affidavits under Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and that Section 195 CrPC is no bar to such complaints. Bench: Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Temple land cannot be gifted to the government, rules SC
capsules.body: On 17 October 2026, the Supreme Court ruled the Tamil Nadu government cannot accept temple land as a gift even for public use — the state is only a custodian of temple property. It declared illegal a 2017 gift deed transferring land of the Nagapalayam Mariamman-Ponnachiamman Temple (Erode) for a Taluk Office, holding it violated the TN Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1959, and ordered Rs 31,000 monthly rent. Bench: Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI October 2026 policy: hike plus calibrated tightening
capsules.body: The RBI's October 2026 MPC (5–7 October) raised the repo rate to 5.50% and shifted the stance to 'calibrated tightening', projecting FY27 GDP growth of 7.1% and CPI inflation of 5.2%. The hike responds to hardening crude prices after the West Asia re-escalation, rupee weakness and broadening price pressures — about 37% of the CPI basket now rising above 4%.

capsules.subject: International Relations
capsules.title: SRIA waiver: 60 days of relief, not certainty
capsules.body: The 17 October 2026 US waiver of SRIA provisions pauses up to 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil for 60 days. For India — whose Russian oil share fell from 51% in July to 44% in August as it diversified toward US and UAE crude — the waiver buys negotiating time ahead of the bilateral trade deal, but the law stays on the books and tariffs can return. GS-II relevance: energy security and strategic autonomy in trade negotiations.

capsules.subject: Current affairs
capsules.title: UPSC CSE Mains 2026 result expected early to mid-November
capsules.body: The written result of the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026, held on 21, 22, 23, 29 and 30 August 2026, is expected in early to mid-November 2026 — about 60-75 days after the final paper, following the pattern of the last five cycles (CSE 2025 took 72 days, with the result dated 11 November). Some 13,343 candidates qualified the prelims against 933 vacancies, and roughly two to two-and-a-half times the vacancies are typically called for the interview. The result appears as a roll-number PDF on upsc.gov.in; marks are released only after the final result.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: CIC directs UPSC to publish paper-wise Mains marks (September 2026)
capsules.body: The Central Information Commission has directed the UPSC to publish paper-wise marks for the Civil Services Main Examination 2026, observing that the detailed marks 'should be disclosed' to ensure transparency and fairness in the selection procedure. The Commission noted that the Department of Personnel and Training could produce no record substantiating the discontinuation of marks publication from 2018 onwards, and that disclosure of optional-subject marks would let aspirants make informed choices instead of depending on unreliable sources.

capsules.subject: Current affairs
capsules.title: CSE 2027 calendar: notification 13 January, Prelims 23 May 2027
capsules.body: As per the UPSC annual calendar, CSE 2027 will be notified on 13 January 2027 with the Preliminary examination on 23 May 2027. Aspirants awaiting the CSE 2026 Mains result are advised to keep Prelims preparation running in parallel, since the CSE 2026 interview process will run from early 2027 and the final result is expected in spring 2027.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: UPSC 2027: what the calendar fixes, and what the 1 October speech did not change
capsules.body: The UPSC 2027 annual calendar (issued 20 May 2026) fixes: CSE Prelims notification on 13 January 2027, applications close 2 February, Prelims on 23 May 2027, and Mains from 20 August 2027. NDA & NA (I) and CDS (I) 2027 are notified on 2 December 2026 with exams on 11 April 2027. At UPSC's centenary on 1 October 2026, the Prime Minister pressed for faster, fairer conduct and shorter examination cycles. A fact-check (5 October 2026) confirms no official change to the CSE 2027 pattern, syllabus, attempts, or age limits: the three-stage structure continues. Any real overhaul needs fresh Civil Services Examination Rules in the Gazette and a UPSC notification - a speech signals direction, not a rule change.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI October 2026: first hike since February 2023
capsules.body: At its 63rd meeting (5-7 October 2026) under Governor Sanjay Malhotra, the MPC voted unanimously to raise the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% - the first hike since February 2023. The stance moved from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening' on a 4-2 vote (Dr Nagesh Kumar and Prof Ram Singh favoured retaining 'neutral'). Consequent rates: SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%. The RBI expects headline CPI to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters and core inflation at 4.4% this fiscal; FY27 projections are 5.2% CPI and 7.1% real GDP growth. Drivers cited: crude oil at $114-116 per barrel in September amid West Asia war escalation, a 13% cumulative southwest monsoon deficit with El Nino conditions pushing food prices, and August CPI at 4.82% - the third straight month above the 4% target. 'Calibrated tightening' takes rate cuts off the table: the next move can only be a hike or a pause.

capsules.subject: GS-2
capsules.title: SC (16 Oct 2026): private individuals can file Section 125A RPA complaints over false election affidavits
capsules.body: In a judgment pronounced on 16 October 2026, a Supreme Court bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that private individuals can file criminal complaints against elected candidates for offences under Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (knowingly furnishing false information or concealing material facts in nomination papers/election affidavits) — without the complaint of a public servant that Section 195(1) of the CrPC, 1973 requires for certain specified offences. The Court reasoned that Section 195(1) does not list Section 125A: 125A was inserted in 2002 while Section 195 was amended in 2006, and Parliament's omission was deliberate. It added that Section 125A applies 'notwithstanding anything contained in any other law', and that EC guidelines and press notes cannot determine statutory interpretation — that is a judicial function. While settling the law, the Court upheld the Karnataka High Court's quashing of the specific proceedings (the complaint by Rajkumar Madki against Karnataka MLA Shailendra Beldale of Bidar over an alleged false address declaration in his 2023 assembly-poll affidavit stood rebutted on record), noting magistrates are equipped to deal with frivolous complaints meant to harass elected candidates. Exam angle: expands voter-led enforcement of candidates' disclosure obligation; links to ADR v. Union of India disclosure jurisprudence, the Section 195 CrPC bar on cognisance, and separation of judicial interpretation from EC's administrative role.

capsules.subject: GS-2
capsules.title: SC (9 Oct 2026): right to protest — restrictions must be proportionate
capsules.body: On 9 October 2026, a three-judge Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant held that restrictions on protest must be proportionate, remarking that authorities 'can't shut down an entire city'. The writ petition was filed after train services to Delhi were cancelled and people were stopped in several States ahead of a demonstration planned for 10 October. The Court suggested an alternative open space for the rally, which the government agreed to. Exam fact: Article 19(1)(b) protects the right to assemble peaceably and without arms; any restriction must be reasonable.

capsules.subject: GS-2
capsules.title: Three new Supreme Court judges sworn in (6 Oct 2026); working strength 37
capsules.body: Three new Supreme Court judges were sworn in on 6 October 2026 by CJI Surya Kant: Justice Sunita Agarwal (formerly Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court), Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (formerly CJ of the Delhi High Court) and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh (formerly CJ of the Telangana High Court). With the oath, the Court's working strength rose to 37 against a sanctioned strength of 38 (including the CJI) — raised from 34 by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 (Rajya Sabha passed it 5 August 2026; replaced a May 2026 Ordinance). Exam facts: the number of SC judges is fixed by Parliament by law under Article 124(1) (not by constitutional amendment); SC judges retire at 65; collegium jurisprudence flows from the Second (1993) and Third (1998) Judges cases.

capsules.subject: GS-2
capsules.title: India-Canada sign commercial agreements; CEPA targeted by December 2026
capsules.body: India and Canada signed commercial agreements in October 2026, with both sides targeting the conclusion of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by December 2026 — a significant normalisation-and-deepening of the economic relationship.

capsules.subject: GS-2
capsules.title: India approves Rs 3,000 crore currency-swap rollover for Maldives
capsules.body: India approved the rollover of a Rs 3,000 crore currency swap facility to the Maldives in October 2026, sustaining financial support to the Indian Ocean neighbour under the RBI's SAARC currency-swap framework.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: GRAP Stage I in Delhi-NCR: AQI 244 (21 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
On 21 October 2026 the CAQM invoked GRAP Stage I across Delhi-NCR (AQI 244, Poor). For UPSC: GRAP is notified by the Commission for Air Quality Management under the CAQM Act, 2021; Stage I (201–300) bans coal/firewood in tandoors and restricts diesel generators; forecasts come from IMD and IITM.

Mains angle: graded emergency response vs structural causes — stubble burning, vehicular emissions, dust — and Centre–state coordination in the NCR.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: SC: internet access is a fundamental right under Art 21 + 19(1)(a), extends to children (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
In Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish (2026 INSC 1149, 15 Oct 2026), a bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran held that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a), extending to children irrespective of age.

The Court said denying children internet access altogether in the name of safety would be unreasonable — safety and freedom are not at odds — while directing stronger action against child sexual exploitation material (CSEAM) online.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: SC: Hindu-to-Islam converts cannot claim Backward Class Muslim status (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
On 15 October 2026 the Supreme Court (Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar) upheld the Madras High Court ruling that a person converting from Hinduism to Islam cannot claim Backward Class Muslim reservation on the basis of pre-conversion caste status.

The Court held conversion to a non-Hindu order does not transfer affirmative-action benefits under Article 16(4) tied to the previous social identity — striking down Tamil Nadu's 2024 order on community certificates for converts.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI October 2026 policy: repo 5.50%, calibrated tightening (minutes 21 Oct)
capsules.body:
RBI's October 2026 policy: repo 5.50% (+25 bps, first hike since Feb 2023), SDF 5.25%, MSF/Bank Rate 5.75%, stance “calibrated tightening” (4–2 vote; dissenters Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh wanted neutral). Governor Sanjay Malhotra; 63rd MPC meeting, 5–7 Oct; minutes released 21 Oct.

Drivers: CPI at 4.8% in August (third straight month above 4% target), crude at $114–116/barrel on West Asia escalation, 13% monsoon deficit + El Niño pushing food prices. FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7.1%; inflation forecast 5.2%.

capsules.subject: Security
capsules.title: Tri-services aerial firing exercise in the Andamans (20–22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
A three-day strategic aerial firing exercise is underway near Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands (20–22 Oct 2026). The Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC) — India's only tri-services command (Navy, Army, Air Force, Coast Guard) — issued a NOTMAR for 10 am–12:30 pm daily.

Su-30MKIs, missile/rocket firings (BrahMos, Crystal Maze 2 in such drills) and MiG-29Ks participate. The archipelago, ~1,200 km from the mainland near the Malacca Strait, anchors India's Indian Ocean posture.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: RRI finds accretion disk around X-ray pulsar Centaurus X-3 (21 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
Researchers at the Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru — led by Kinjal Roy — found that Centaurus X-3, one of the brightest X-ray pulsars, is accreting material through an accretion disk, rare for its class (DST statement, 21 Oct 2026).

Centaurus X-3 is a high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB), ~24,000 light years away; its companion is over 10 times the Sun's mass. The finding sharpens models of binary pulsars and their magnetic-field geometry.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: India–US trade deal 'very, very close': Rubio–Jaishankar Mumbai talks
capsules.body: On 20 October 2026, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks in Mumbai, covering oil supplies, a plan for additional Venezuelan oil to be refined at the Reliance plant in Jamnagar, and the long-delayed free trade agreement — which Rubio said is 'very, very close' with only a small number of items left to wrap up. A trilateral meeting with UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah Bin Zayed Al Nahyan was also held. (Dated: 22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: China's TBM export curbs from 18 Nov 2026 hit bullet train project
capsules.body: China's Commerce and Industry Ministry announced fresh global export restrictions on tunnel boring machines (TBMs) — critical for metro rail and highway construction — effective 18 November 2026, under its dual-use export control law. The 3,000-tonne machines are vital for the 508-km Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor, which includes a 7-km undersea tunnel. India has faced TBM import delays since 2024. (Dated: 22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: SC upholds HC verdict on Tamil Nadu's conversion-reservation GO
capsules.body: In The Secretary to Government v. Sameer Ahamed N., the Supreme Court upheld the Madras High Court's verdict invalidating Tamil Nadu's 9 March 2024 Government Order, which permitted converts to Islam from Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes, Denotified Communities and Scheduled Castes to seek Backward Class Muslim certificates. Key doctrine: under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 (Article 341), SC status is restricted to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists — conversion to Islam or Christianity removes eligibility. (Dated: 22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: EC announces Special Summary Revision in 17 states/UTs
capsules.body: Amid protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Election Commission announced the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls. The annual exercise — updating rolls with 1 January as the qualifying date, adding newly eligible electors and removing the deceased/shifted — was skipped in 2026 after the June 2025 SIR prepared rolls afresh. It will now run in 17 states and UTs, including the five states with Assembly elections in early 2027. (Dated: 22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: CDS II 2026: result 19 Oct; 8,956 qualified for SSB for 451 vacancies (22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: UPSC declared the Combined Defence Services Examination (II), 2026 written result on 19 October 2026 (exam held 13 September 2026, notification 11/2026-CDS-II): 8,956 candidates qualified for the SSB interviews. The drive covers 451 vacancies — IMA 100, INA 26, AFA 32, OTA Men 275, OTA Women 18. Result PDF on upsc.gov.in. (22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: NDA & NA (II) 2026: 7,886 qualify; SSB registration due within two weeks (22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: UPSC declared the NDA & NA Examination (II), 2026 written result on 9 October 2026 (exam 13 September): about 7,886 candidates qualified (~7,400 men, ~480 women). Qualified candidates must register on joinindianarmy.nic.in within two weeks of the result for SSB interview allotment. Courses commence 1 July 2027. (22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: UPSC calendar 2027: CSE prelims 23 May 2027; NDA/CDS (I) notice 2 Dec 2026 (22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Per UPSC's Programme of Examinations 2027: CSE (Prelims) 2027 on 23 May 2027; NDA & NA (I) and CDS (I) 2027 notification on 2 December 2026 (last date 22 December 2026); Engineering Services 2027 notified 16 Sep 2026 with ~480 vacancies, prelim on 31 January 2027; CISF AC(EXE) LDCE notice on 25 November 2026. (22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: IES/ISS interviews 2–5 Nov; IFoS Main 21–22 Nov; APFC RT 20 Dec 2026 (22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: UPSC IES/ISS 2026 interviews run 2–5 November 2026 (40 Economic Service, 94 Statistical Service candidates). Indian Forest Service (Main) 2026 is on 21–22 November 2026. The APFC 2026 recruitment test (80 Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner posts, Special Advt 52/2026) is scheduled on 20 December 2026 — a 2-hour objective paper with 1/3 negative marking and a 75:25 written–interview weightage. (22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Startup credit guarantee gets a leg up
capsules.body: DPIIT expanded the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups: the ceiling doubled to ₹20 crore per borrower with 85% cover up to ₹10 crore and 75% beyond, while the annual guarantee fee for 27 Champion Sectors was halved to 1% — a push to de-risk startup lending and deepen Make in India manufacturing.

capsules.subject: International Relations
capsules.title: BIMSTEC's first Home Ministers' meet
capsules.body: The first BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi adopted the Delhi Declaration, marking a new institutional layer in Bay of Bengal security cooperation among the seven member states.

capsules.subject: Science & Technology
capsules.title: Junput: DRDO's second eastern test range opens up
capsules.body: The Junput DRDO Missile Testing Range in Purba Medinipur, West Bengal, saw its first notified test window (6–9 October 2026) over the Bay of Bengal. Proposed in 2024, it complements the Chandipur ITR, adding capacity for trials needing a larger engagement envelope.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: The Central Agriculture Minister and the Environment Minister conducted a joint review on stubble management on 13 Oct 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: NIFTEM-Kundli organised an India-Canada roundtable on pulses protein innovation, value addition and strategic partnerships (13 Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Governance
oneliners.text: The 21st Maritime State Development Council meeting concluded in Mumbai on 13 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: International Relations
oneliners.text: India condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in October 2026, calling them ‘unacceptable’ and stating ‘we stand with Saudi Arabia’.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Dr L. Murugan resigned as MoS for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs and from the Rajya Sabha (October 2026).

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: UPSC declared the NDA & NA Examination (II) 2026 written result on 9 October 2026 (written exam held 13 September 2026) for 394 vacancies; qualified candidates proceed to the SSB interview (15 Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: Lakshadweep has become India's first 100 per cent literate Union Territory under the ULLAS scheme (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan completed five years on 13 October 2026 - it was launched on 13 October 2021 for integrated infrastructure planning (15 Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: President Droupadi Murmu accepted Dr L Murugan's resignation from the Union Council of Ministers on 15 Oct 2026, acting on the PM's advice under Article 75(2).

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: DARPG's 53rd monthly CPGRAMS report: a record 2,38,579 grievances disposed in September 2026; average resolution time down to an all-time low of 14 days.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: The SC asked the government to clarify the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site, while petitions allege police excesses during the Delhi CEC protests of 10–12 October.

oneliners.subject: Governance
oneliners.text: DARPG's 53rd monthly CPGRAMS report: central ministries disposed a record 2,38,579 grievances in September 2026; average resolution time fell to an all-time low of about 14 days, aided by AI-driven semantic categorisation.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The Supreme Court on 15 October 2026 heard pleas against the EC's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, seeking clarity on requiring deleted voters to reapply as fresh applicants through Form 6.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: DRDO's Advanced Agni missile with MIRV was flight-tested from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island; multiple independently-targeted re-entry vehicles struck different targets across a large geographical area in the Indian Ocean Region.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The government's export levy on petrol was raised to ₹2.5 per litre (from ₹0.5) and the duty on diesel exports cut to ₹8.5 per litre (from ₹16), effective 16 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Science & Tech
oneliners.text: ISRO completed Crew Module–Service Module separation tests for Gaganyaan at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Thiruvananthapuram, ahead of the first uncrewed mission targeted for 2026.

oneliners.subject: Governance
oneliners.text: The Cabinet approved continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for 2026-31 on 15 October 2026; NSAP was launched on 15 August 1995 under Article 41 of the Directive Principles.

oneliners.subject: Infrastructure
oneliners.text: On 15 October 2026 the Prime Minister inaugurated Ladakh projects including a new geothermal-heated terminal at Leh airport, the 298-km Nimmu-Padum-Darcha road, the 9 MW Hanu hydro project and India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat.

oneliners.subject: Environment
oneliners.text: Asiatic lions returned to Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, Gujarat, after 144 years (reported 15 October 2026).

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI approved the amalgamation of Emirates NBD Bank's Indian branches with RBL Bank, effective 1 December 2026 (announced 16 Oct 2026) — Verified: 17 Oct 2026

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: On 15 October 2026 the Supreme Court (2026 INSC 1132) set aside the Rs 8,415 crore write-down of Yes Bank's AT-1 bonds.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: On 16 October 2026 the Supreme Court allowed private complaints for false election affidavits under Section 125A, RoP Act, holding Section 195 CrPC is no bar.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: On 17 October 2026 the Supreme Court ruled the state is only a custodian of temple property and cannot accept temple land as a gift.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: The draft National Steel Policy (17 October 2026) targets 604 MT crude steel capacity and 302 kg per-capita consumption by 2047.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: UPSC CSE Mains 2026 (held 21-30 August) result is expected in early to mid-November 2026; about 13,343 candidates qualified the prelims against 933 vacancies.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: The Central Information Commission has directed UPSC to publish paper-wise marks for the Civil Services Main Examination 2026, citing transparency and fairness in the selection procedure.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: UPSC released the recommended candidates list for the CAPF (Assistant Commandants) 2024 examination on 15 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: CSE 2027 will be notified on 13 January 2027 with the Prelims on 23 May 2027, as per the UPSC annual calendar.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: India-New Zealand FTA in force from 20 October 2026 (announced 19 October by Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal): 100% duty-free access for Indian goods; target to double bilateral trade; dairy, sugar, edible oils and most animal meat excluded (GS-III relevant).

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI's October 2026 policy (63rd MPC, 5-7 October, Governor Sanjay Malhotra): repo up 25 bps to 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' (4-2 vote); SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; FY27 CPI forecast 5.2%, real GDP growth 7.1%.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: UPSC 2027 calendar: CSE Prelims notification 13 January 2027, last date 2 February, Prelims 23 May 2027, Mains from 20 August 2027; NDA and CDS (I) 2027 notifications on 2 December 2026, both exams on 11 April 2027.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: India-New Zealand FTA (in force 20 October 2026) is India's first FTA with full duty-free access across all tariff lines from entry into force; bilateral goods and services trade target NZ$7 billion (about Rs 35,000 crore) by 2030, up from about $2.4 billion in 2024-25; $20 billion NZ investment committed over 15 years. - Verified: 20 Oct 2026

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: MPC minutes of the 7 October 2026 policy meeting (repo rate raised 25 bps to 5.50%, stance shifted to 'calibrated tightening' on a 4-2 vote) are due on 21 October 2026; the next MPC meeting is 2-4 December 2026. - Verified: 20 Oct 2026

oneliners.subject: GS-2
oneliners.text: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet appointed Subhas Chandra Lal Das as part-time Chairperson of the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB).

oneliners.subject: GS-3
oneliners.text: NCISM Chairperson Prof. Maneesha Kothekar launched 'CCRAS SPARK 5.0' and 'CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026' for Ayurveda research capacity-building.

oneliners.subject: GS-3
oneliners.text: The BHASHINI Division and the Manipur government signed an MoU to expand multilingual AI and digital governance in the state.

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: Tarang Shakti 2026 at Jodhpur Air Force Station: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh called for self-reliance in indigenous platforms like Tejas and Akash; 32 observer nations attended. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: Governance
oneliners.text: Indian Railways warns of action against passengers playing audio/video on speaker mode: Rs 1,000 fine + ticket forfeiture under Section 145(2); continued nuisance up to 6 months' simple imprisonment or Rs 5,000 fine, under the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: Governance
oneliners.text: Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal announced (14 Oct 2026) that India's National Electricity Data Sharing Framework will launch in October 2026 to support AI applications, with a governance committee headed by the CEA chairperson. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: Defence
oneliners.text: UPSC CDS-II Result 2026 has been declared. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: 21 Oct 2026: Goldman Sachs — 84 privately held Indian AI firms worth ~$55 bn; 25–50% of the ~70 mid-to-late-stage ones could list in 2–5 years at ~4x valuations, adding $50–100 bn to India's listed AI market cap.

oneliners.subject: Security
oneliners.text: 21 Oct 2026: At the 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh called for dismantling the “entire ecosystem of terrorism.”

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: 22 Oct 2026: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and EAM S. Jaishankar held talks in Mumbai on 20 Oct 2026; Rubio said the India–US trade deal is 'very, very close' with only a few items left to wrap up.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: 22 Oct 2026: China announced fresh global export curbs on tunnel boring machines effective 18 November 2026, hitting the 508-km Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train corridor's 7-km undersea tunnel.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: 22 Oct 2026: 2026 Nobel Peace Prize (announced 9 Oct) awarded to Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay, ex-UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (2008–2014), for promoting peace and international law.

oneliners.subject: Polity
oneliners.text: 22 Oct 2026: Election Commission announced Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states/UTs; SSR 2026 had been skipped after the June 2025 Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: CGSS expanded: cover doubled to ₹20 crore per borrower; 85% cover up to ₹10 crore; AGF cut to 1% for 27 Champion Sectors.

oneliners.subject: International Relations
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: First-ever BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting concluded in New Delhi; Delhi Declaration adopted.

oneliners.subject: Science & Technology
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: First missile-test window notified at DRDO's new Junput range, West Bengal (NOTAM 6–9 October 2026).

oneliners.subject: Governance
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: Union Cabinet extended the National Social Assistance Programme from 2026-27 to 2030-31.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: Union Cabinet approved ₹10,000-crore commitment to the SME Growth Fund.

oneliners.subject: International Relations
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited India on 21 October 2026 (Mumbai meetings, Jamnagar refinery visit).
